title: Senior Cyber Security Engineer - Identity and Device Management, & Networking Security
description:
Latitude AI (lat.ai) is building the future of Ford’s autonomy roadmap to make travel safer, less stressful, and more enjoyable for everyone. Bringing this vision to scale, our fully in-house developed hands-free ADAS platform will debut on the all-new Ford Fathom in 2027.

When you join the Latitude team, you’ll work alongside leading experts across machine learning and robotics, cloud platforms, mapping, sensors and compute systems, test operations, systems and safety engineering – all dedicated to redefining the relationship between people and their vehicles for millions of customers.

As a Ford Motor Company subsidiary, we operate independently to develop automated driving technology at the speed of a technology startup. Latitude is headquartered in Pittsburgh with engineering centers in Dearborn, Mich., and Palo Alto, Calif.

Meet the Team:

The Enterprise Cyber Security team is focused on ensuring the resilience of our corporate environment with focus on protection of our corporate systems, IP, and employee data. We are a close-knit team with strong cross-functional roles in the company.

As a Cyber Security Engineer, you will be the hands-on technical lead securing our High Performance Computing (HPC)/Virtualization environments. Your job is to have a deep understanding of this infrastructure, network architecture, and the operations depending on it, including our software/hardware/network engineering, fleet operations requirements, and administrative functions. You will use your knowledge and experience to design, implement, automate, and continuously improve our security posture.

What you'll do:

- Identity Management and Device Management design, implementation, and deployment (Entra/Okta, MDM solutions like Intune)

- Network Security design and engineering, applying best practices in software, network, and infrastructure engineering

- Consult and advocate security best practices for DMZ architectures, NAC/NAP, lateral isolation, and multi-site data movement in Network management tooling (like Palo Alto, Fortinet, F5)

- Deliver projects on time, on budget, with excellent quality and security configurations

- Review the existing and new deployments and architecture designs looking for design flaws, security improvements, and advocate for stronger security controls that meet functional and operational needs

- Work hand-in-hand with the Cloud Platform, IT, and Product teams to research, design and develop security solutions and deployments and strategies tailored to Latitude’s business needs

- Engage actively in Data Center and Network Security initiatives to assess existing security access controls, and implementations of supplemental technical solutions to improve overall security.

- Document findings, conduct comparisons, perform threat and risk assessments, and Proof of Concepts aiding the team in making informed decisions about the impact of various design options.

- Develop, Review, and Design the automation and orchestration for security aspects device controls and access to services

- Provide inputs into dashboards and report metrics on the status of the Cyber Security posture

- Plan for, execute, and follow through on projects and engagements independently

- Hands on deployment of solutions, working independently and as part of a team

- Provide mentoring and skill set knowledge transfer to team members and engineering staff

- Moderate and contribute to Supercomputing System Administration that contributes to:

- Proactive monitoring, analysis, and correcting system security issues

- Development of scripts to automate, perform security checks, and develop tools to enhance support of the Cloud/Virtualized systems and development environments

- Developing playbooks/runbooks, operational and troubleshooting documentation

- Evaluate and contribute to designs for Network and Infrastructure Solutions with Security and Functionality as pillars of implementation

- At a minimum, a Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Cyber Security or a related field and 4+ years of relevant experience (or Master's degree and 2+ years of relevant experience)

- Strongly prefer 8+ years related experience or 6 years with a Master’s degree; as an Identity and Device Management Engineer and/or Network Security Architect/Engineer. Actively deploying solutions from scratch to Production

- 2+ years of related experience in vulnerability management and adjusting the risk rating/severity dependent on internal factors for cloud and other infra.

- Experience with Lustre, Kerberos, and Linux Administration

- Proficiency in scripting languages, including Bash, Python, Go, or Java to create production level services and automation tools that incorporate into CI/CD

- Proficiency and hands-on experience using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to automate the creation of cloud resources, virtualized systems, and review infrastructure deployments. E.g. Terraform, Cloud Formation, Ansible, or others

- Ability to grasp new technologies quickly and prioritize and multitask on multiple responsibilities.

- Hands-on Experience with patching and hardening Linux, MacOS, and Windows Systems (clients and servers), images, and containers.

- Proficient in Network Protocols and Firewall Management, with hands-on experience in configuration and optimization to ensure network security internally and at perimeters.

- Critical thinking and a holistic view of Cyber Security with ability to balance security requirements with mission needs and collaboration across teams

- Exceptional organizational and time management skills demonstrated through adept autonomy, independent work, collaborative teamwork, and a professional demeanor.

- Strong experience with architecting/deploying scalable security services and workloads in cloud native and virtualized environments

- Ability to deploy Device Management solutions to control access to Company Solutions

- Understand engineering design limitations and provide guidance for teams to secure their deployments to achieve desired performance in budget and on time

- An Independent take-charge attitude while being open-minded, creatively thinking, willing to take calculated risks, and make informed decisions

- Strong understanding of Cyber Security Standards (ISO27001, NIST 800-53)

- Experience with Jenkins a plus

- Experience with Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles and implementations

- Exposure to data governance, secure data movement, and storage lifecycle management

- Must have demonstrated proficiency and strength in verbal, written, presentation, and communications skills, including technical diagramming

- A sense of comradery, compassion, and unparalleled passion/energy

title: Robotics Research Intern
description:
Company Description

The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design.

As a part of the global research, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models, Big Data Visual Analytics, Explainable AI (XAI), Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision & Mixed Reality, Cloud Robotics, Data Science, AI System Engineering, Time-series Analysis. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AIoT solutions for Bosch products and services in application areas such as automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, health care, smart home and building solutions.

Originating from the AI research in Silicon Valley, our Intelligent Autonomous Systems group is responsible for enabling future autonomous Bosch products by pushing the boundaries of automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics and automation through key innovations that encompass system architecture and AI components. These include methods for motion planning, high level task planning and decision making as well as systems for making these technologies work on real products by building frameworks that take advantage of technologies in the field of reliable distributed computing. We work with internal partners of different Bosch business units to transfer our solutions into future products. We also actively collaborate with leading groups in academia and industry to promote research ideas and publish research findings in internationally renowned conferences and journals such as CVPR, ICRA, IROS, RSS, NeurIPS and CoRL.

Job Description

As the Robotics Manipulation intern, you will advance Bosch's capabilities in robotic manipulation, specifically in the area of agentic robotics (coding agents for robotics manipulation).

A few of your responsibilities will include:

* Research the state-of-the-art in agentic robotics.

* Evaluate this research on a realistic, industrial Bosch use case.

* Develop improvements to make these techniques practical.

* Report experimental results and prepare a draft to a high-quality conference.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

- Ph.D. or Masters student in Computer Science, Robotics or related fields. (Must be a current student.)
- Experience using agents, e.g. Anthropic Claude Code or OpenAI Codex.
- Experience implementing algorithms on robotic arms, humanoids, or quadrupeds.
- Proficient in Python and C++, with experience using Ubuntu and ROS2.
- Minimum GPA of 3.0.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience applying large generative multi-modal models, VLAs, VLMs, or LLMs to robotics problems.
- Familiarity with simulation and motion planning suites (e.g., NVIDIA Isaac Sim, cuRobo).
- Experience with perception models (e.g., SAM/SAM2, DINOv2) and spatial representation (e.g., Gaussian Splatting, NeRFs).
- Publication record in top venues, such as ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS, etc.
- Focus on embodiment transfer, learning from demonstration, and/or semantic scene understanding.
- Able to work independently, has strong research and problem-solving skills.
- Good communication and teamwork skills.

Additional Information

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans 

*Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date.

BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics)

- FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)
- AWIM (A World In Motion)

The U.S. base salary range for this intern position is $48.00-69.00 hourly. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process.

For more information on our culture and benefits, please visit:

Culture and Benefits | Bosch in the USA

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

title: Research Scientist, Benchmarks & Evals
description:
ABOUT KLED

Kled is building the largest opt-in human data network in the world.

We are not a labeling firm. We are not a task marketplace.

We are a consumer application where people upload their real photos, videos, and documents and get paid continuously.

We then filter, standardize, and license that data to frontier AI labs and enterprises that need fresh, rights-aware training data.

Since launching our mobile app in 2026, we have:

• Reached #1 on the App Store (Finance) with 0 paid marketing
• Scaled to 600,000+ active data contributors
• Processed 5M uploads per day
• Raised $15M+ from investors behind SpaceX, Airbnb, Coinbase, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Spotify, Lyft, Uber, and more

Our mission is to let anyone download the app and earn a real living wage from uploading their data.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Research Scientist - Benchmarks & Evals

AI labs buy data when a benchmark shows it works.

You’ll build the benchmarks that show what one of the largest human data networks in the world can do for frontier AI models.

You will:

- Design and ship public benchmarks for image, video and document models

- Build private test sets from real, opt-in data that no model has trained on

- Run data-value experiments: train models with and without Kled data, measure what changes

- Design human evaluation studies and the automatic metrics that track them

- Publish leaderboards and reports that researchers at frontier labs trust

- Find where models fall short and tell our team what data to collect next

- Work directly with the founders and lab buyers to turn results into data deals

WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- 3+ years ML research or research engineering experience

- A benchmark or evaluation you built that other people actually used

- Strong hands-on experience training and fine-tuning image or video models (PyTorch)

- Deep understanding of experimental design and statistics (controls, ablations, human studies)

- Experience running experiments end to end, from GPUs to final report

- Clear writing for both researchers and buyers

Bonus:

- Publications at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR or CVPR (datasets and benchmarks especially)

- Experience on an evaluation or data team at an AI lab

- Experience selling or licensing data to AI labs

- Experience with data valuation or data attribution research

CURRENT STACK

Research

- Python / PyTorch

- Open-weight image and video models

- Cloud GPUs

Data

- Hundreds of millions of opt-in photos, videos and documents

- PostgreSQL (Supabase)

- S3 storage

title: Senior Fullstack Engineer, Growth
description:
Location: US - NYC, Boston

Compensation: $200,000 - $280,000

💎 About Nivoda

Nivoda is the operating system for the global jewellery industry. We connect diamond and gemstone suppliers directly with jewellery retailers across more than 70 countries, replacing a slow, offline, relationship-gated way of trading with a single digital marketplace. We're already powering over $300M in annual transactions, inside an industry worth more than $350B globally — and we're still early. Jewellery is one of the last major global industries to go digital, and we're the ones building the rails it will run on.

Our Mission

Diamond and gemstone trading has run for decades on fragmented networks, manual processes, and who-you-know relationships — which locks smaller and newer businesses out, and leaves even the biggest players losing time and margin to inefficiency. We started Nivoda to fix that: to give any jewellery business, wherever it is and whatever size it is, the same access, pricing transparency, and ease of trading as an industry giant. Our mission is to make buying and selling diamonds and gemstones radically simpler, everywhere in the world.

The Growth Pod

You'd be joining the Growth Pod 🚀 — the team responsible for everything that happens between a business discovering Nivoda and becoming one of our most valuable customers: sign-up, onboarding, verification, activation, and the ongoing work of keeping accounts engaged instead of letting them slip away. We're a small, high-ownership team inside an engineering org that moves fast and expects you to bring judgement, not just code. You'll work closely with Product, Data, and Risk, and you'll have a real say in how we solve problems that don't yet have a playbook.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Senior Engineer for the Growth Pod to own both the backend systems and the front-end experiences that turn a new sign-up into an active, paying customer — the services and screens that decide whether a business converts or falls out of the funnel. The problems worth solving here span Sign-up/Onboarding, Discovery, and Checkout: you’ll build the event-driven, always-on backend systems that track thousands of accounts through activation, slipping, winback, lapsed, and churned states in real time, and the seamless front-end moments that educate customers, represent the Nivoda brand, and move them toward a purchase. This isn’t a role where you ship a spec and move on: you’ll be expected to dig into the data yourself to work out what’s actually going wrong when conversion isn’t where it should be. You’ll also work with identity verification and risk providers and with sensitive credit and payment data, so judgement and rigor matter here as much as raw engineering skill.

Tech Stack

-
Search: OpenSearch fed via CDC from PostgreSQL plus Spark/EMR/Glue ingestion jobs.

-
Core DB / warehouse: PostgreSQL (OLTP) → Snowflake (dbt-modeled, medallion raw/curated/presentation layers)

-
Backend: TypeScript/Node.js, GraphQL API gateway, Nx monorepo + PNPM

-
Auth: Keycloak · SSO: Okta

-
CI/CD: Jenkins (“Nivoda Build”) + GitOps for deploys

-
Cloud: AWS (EMR, Glue, DMS, Kubernetes-based deploys)

-
Observability: Grafana for logs/traces — I’d flagged Datadog as a guess earlier based on the Frontier agent skill descriptions; the real Confluence docs point to Grafana instead, so I’ve dropped Datadog from both JDs.

What would you be doing?

Core Funnel & Lifecycle Systems

-
Own and evolve the backend services behind onboarding, verification, activation, and the broader sign-up-to-purchase funnel, most likely in TypeScript/Node.js given our stack

-
Design and build event-driven, workflow-orchestrated systems that evaluate account state continuously — activation, slipping, winback, lapsed, churned — and trigger the right action automatically, rather than relying on batch scripts

Identity, Risk & Trust

-
Integrate with third-party identity verification, KYB/KYC, and fraud/risk providers, and make sure those integrations are resilient, well-monitored, and fail safely

-
Handle credit and payment data responsibly as part of personalization and reactivation logic, with full awareness of what’s at stake if that logic is subtly wrong

Experimentation & Analysis

-
Design and run experiments properly — including defining guardrail metrics and knowing when a result is real versus noise — for things like referral incentives, reactivation offers, and onboarding changes

-
Write your own SQL and work directly in the warehouse (Snowflake or similar) to run cohort analysis, diagnose time-to-activation and time-to-churn, and get to the bottom of funnel problems without waiting on a data team

-
Take on problems that don’t have an established playbook — like a credit utilization gap or a signup-to-purchase conversion decline — and help define the problem, not just solve a given brief

Building with AI

-
Use AI agents to accelerate building and testing funnel and lifecycle services, with extra care reviewing anything that touches credit, payment, or verification logic

-
Use AI to help draft and sanity-check your own analytical queries, while owning full responsibility for verifying results before they inform a real decision

-
Evaluate AI-generated output — personalized messaging, reactivation copy, churn-cause suggestions — critically, rather than shipping whatever the model produces uncritically

What do we need from you?

Years of Experience: 4 - 7 years

-
Strong backend product engineering experience, most likely in TypeScript/Node.js, with real ownership of funnel-critical, production services

-
Hands-on experience with event-driven architectures and workflow orchestration — workflow engines or event pipelines that evaluate state continuously and trigger actions automatically

-
Genuine experimentation rigor: you've designed experiments properly, you understand guardrail metrics, and you know when a result is real versus noise

-
Strong SQL and warehouse fluency (Snowflake or similar), and the confidence to do your own cohort and funnel analysis rather than waiting on a data team

-
Comfort using AI agents to build and test software and to draft and sanity-check analytical work, paired with the judgement to catch the subtle errors a reasonable-looking AI output can hide

-
High tolerance for ambiguity — you're energised by problems that don't have an established playbook, not just ones with a clear spec

-
Practical fluency evaluating AI-generated output for fitness before it ships, whether that's copy, messaging, or a suggested root cause

Nice to have

-
Direct experience integrating with identity verification, KYB/KYC, or fraud and risk providers

-
Fintech-adjacent experience handling credit, payment, or other sensitive financial data responsibly

-
Experience in a high-growth marketplace or fintech environment with similar account lifecycle complexity

-
Familiarity with workflow/orchestration tooling such as Temporal, AWS Step Functions, or event-streaming platforms like Kafka

⭐️ Our culture and what we offer

We're a collaborative, high-growth team that believes in empowerment over hierarchy. You'll have real ownership from day one, the chance to work on problems most companies don't even know they have yet, and a culture that takes learning and growth seriously — because we're scaling fast, and we need you to grow with us.

Our current benefits

-
🏡 Flexible working hours and a remote-first culture

-
📈 Real opportunities for growth and learning

-
🌴 Unlimited holiday allowance

-
🚀 The chance to join during an exponential expansion phase

Equal Opportunity

Nivoda is an equal opportunity employer. We're committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of race, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. Even if it seems you don't meet 100% of our musts, don't let that stop you from applying — we'd still love to hear from you.

Please submit your CV in English.

👋 Not quite the right role?

Join the Nivoda Talent Pool and we'll reach out when something that's a better fit comes up.

Senior Airtable Data Operations Architect

Advanced Systems Group (ASG) is seeking a Senior Airtable Data Operations Architect to lead the implementation of an enterprise data ecosystem for a major global live-streaming and commerce platform through an embedded engagement. This is a full-time, on-site position, 5 days per week, in the office in Culver City, CA, New York City, or Seattle, WA.

The architecture is designed, the roadmap is approved, and the ecosystem foundation is in place. The heavy build work lies ahead, and you will lead it. This is not a maintenance role.

The scope spans multiple departments, numerous bases, and integrations with several external systems, and it will grow as the organization expands. You will lead a small team of embedded team members, set technical direction, and assign build work, without formal people-management responsibilities. You are expected to lead architecture decisions and drive the build forward independently.

Experience working within large enterprise environments where integrations require navigating corporate systems and formal approval processes

Preferred Experience

title: AI Full Stack Engineer
description:
About Mem0

We're building the memory layer for AI agents. Think long-term memory that enables AI to remember conversations, learn from interactions, and build context over time. We're already powering millions of AI interactions for enterprise customers and an open-source community of 160,000+ developers. We're a Y Combinator-backed company that has raised a $24M Seed + Series A from top-tier investors.

This position reports directly to the CTO, making it a highly visible role with significant influence on product direction, engineering execution, and the future of the Mem0 platform.

Role Summary

Build the AI product surface of the Mem0 Platform, the memory infrastructure powering the next generation of AI agents.

You'll own the frontend end to end. We don't have a designer, so the person in this seat sets the visual and interaction bar for everything our users touch: the dashboard, the playground, the docs experience, the onboarding flow. You'll decide what it looks like, build it in Next.js and React, and wire it to the Python services behind it.

Our users are developers building agents, so the product you ship is the thing they judge us on. You'll work directly with the CTO, research, and customers to turn real memory problems into interfaces that feel fast and obvious.

This is a role for an engineer who has shipped LLM products to real users, has taste, and gets energy from owning the whole surface.

What You'll Do

-
Own the frontend: Design and build the Mem0 dashboard, playground, and developer surfaces in Next.js and React. You set the design direction, build the component system, handle streaming responses and live state, and hold the quality bar.

-
Ship AI features end to end: Design APIs, build retrieval and memory pipelines, own the data models, and deploy to production.

-
Build with LLMs in production: Work with embeddings, vector search, RAG, function calling, and agent orchestration. Handle the messy parts: context windows, token budgets, non-deterministic output, graceful degradation.

-
Make quality measurable: Build evals, golden datasets, and regression suites for AI behavior so that model and prompt changes ship with evidence behind them.

-
Build for scale and speed: Optimize retrieval latency, caching, database queries, bundle size, and inference cost across the stack.

-
Own quality: Write tests, maintain strong typing and linting standards, review code thoughtfully, keep the codebase clean.

-
Collaborate deeply: Partner with Research to bring new memory capabilities into the product, and talk to customers directly to sharpen what you build.

-
Operate what you build: Implement observability for both application and model behavior, monitor production, troubleshoot, and keep improving reliability.

-
Lead with product sense: Make thoughtful technical and product tradeoffs, prioritize well, iterate on user feedback and data.

-
Go beyond your lane: Unblock teammates, pick up new technologies fast, do what it takes to deliver.

Minimum Qualifications

-
5+ years building and shipping production-grade full-stack applications at scale.

-
Deep frontend craft in Next.js, React, and TypeScript. You've owned the look and feel of a product in production, with examples you can show us.

-
Strong design sense and the ability to work without a designer. You can take a rough idea to a polished, accessible interface on your own, with a point of view on layout, typography, spacing, and motion.

-
Hands-on experience shipping AI-native products to real users using LLMs, RAG, embeddings, or vector databases. We want to hear about what you built, who used it, and what broke.

-
Strong proficiency in Python and modern web application architecture.

-
Experience with REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis, background job systems, and modern backend frameworks.

-
Practical experience with prompt engineering, model evaluation, and debugging non-deterministic systems.

-
Demonstrated track record of owning features end to end, from technical design through deployment and post-launch iteration.

-
Strong engineering fundamentals: testing, CI/CD, type safety, maintainability, code quality.

-
Experience operating production systems with logging, metrics, tracing, and monitoring while meeting low-latency requirements.

-
Excellent communication skills and comfort working directly with customers and leadership.

-
Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent coursework and practical experience.

Nice to Have

-
Experience building and maintaining a design system or component library from scratch.

-
Comfort in Figma, or a habit of designing directly in code.

-
Experience with agent frameworks, multi-agent systems, or tool-use architectures.

-
Familiarity with vLLM, model serving, fine-tuning, or lightweight ML infrastructure.

-
Experience building developer-facing products: SDKs, API design, docs, playgrounds.

-
Infrastructure experience with Docker, Kubernetes, IaC, AWS, GCP, or Vercel.

-
Understanding of security and privacy best practices, including PII handling and audit logging.

Our Culture

-
Office-first collaboration. We're an in-person team based in San Francisco. Hallway conversations, whiteboard sessions, and spontaneous collaboration help us move faster and build better products than remote meetings alone.

-
Velocity with craftsmanship. We move quickly without sacrificing engineering excellence. Every system we build should be fast, reliable, scalable, and thoughtfully designed.

-
Extreme ownership. Everyone at Mem0 is a builder-owner. If you see a problem or opportunity, you're empowered to solve it. Titles matter less than impact.

-
High bar, high trust. We hire exceptional people, give them autonomy, and hold ourselves to a high engineering standard. We challenge ideas, review code thoughtfully, and celebrate wins together.

-
Data-driven, not ego-driven. The best ideas win regardless of where they come from. We rely on data, customer feedback, and thoughtful experimentation to guide decisions.

Benefits & Perks

-
Health, dental & vision coverage. Comprehensive plans, fully covered for you and subsidized for dependents.

-
Lunch & dinner, on us. Daily meals catered in-office, because good food fuels good work.

-
Flexible PTO. Take the time you need to recharge, no rigid accrual counting.

-
Equity in an early-stage company. Real ownership in what you're building, not just a paycheck.

-
Regular team happy hours & events. Built into the culture, not an afterthought.

-
Top-tier equipment. The laptop and setup you need to do your best work.

description:

AiDASH is leading the PreventionFirst™movement for electric utilities and transforming grid resilience through its pioneering platform that unifies vegetation, asset, storm, and wildfire intelligence. In 2026, Forbes named AiDASH one of America's Best Startup Employers for the 4th consecutive year, and TIME included AiDASH among America's Top GreenTech Companies for the 3rd year in a row. Deloitte Technology Fast 500™ ranked AiDASH No. 12 in the San Francisco Bay Area, and No. 59 overall in their selection of the top 500 for 2024.

Join us in Securing Tomorrow Together!

The Role

Our satellite and AI-powered products are changing how utilities see and protect the grid, and we're gearing up for aggressive customer growth over the next two years. That growth runs on AI at scale. We're building a brand-new Data Inference AI Pipeline team to deliver it, and we're looking for a Staff MLOps Engineer to architect its operational backbone from the very first line of infrastructure code.

As the very first engineer on this team, you'll start with a blank canvas and a rare chance to build something that lasts. You'll shape how our models are deployed, how the pipeline scales and recovers under load, and what it costs to run. Just as importantly, you'll help define the culture, engineering standards, and ways of working that every future teammate inherits. This is a hands-on, high-leverage individual contributor role: your decisions will set the foundation the entire team builds on, and you'll be the go-to technical authority on MLOps as the team grows. You'll report to the Director of Engineering for the Data Inference AI Pipeline team.

Our pending acquisition by Schneider Electric will accelerate our mission as we bring our combined offering to our joint customer base, and the infrastructure you build will power outcomes at an even greater scale.

Location: This is a hybrid role based in Palo Alto, CA, requiring 2 days per week in the office.

How you'll make an impact:

Deployment

- Own the model deployment pipeline end-to-end: packaging, versioning, rollout, and rollback for ML models moving from training to production

- Build and maintain deployment infrastructure on SageMaker (endpoints, batch transform, multi-model/multi-container hosting), and evaluate where alternatives such as self-hosted serving or other managed options are a better fit

- Set the CI/CD pattern for model releases, including automated testing, staged rollout, and canary/shadow deployments

Scalability & elasticity

Cost

title: Head of Catastrophe and Emergency Response
description:
Why Join Stand: At Stand, you’ll help build a new class of global property protection. We use advanced physics and AI to model catastrophic risk at the asset level, then automate underwriting and mitigation before loss occurs. Insurance is simply the current delivery mechanism. The real product is a scalable risk engine, our Stand World Model.

We stay when traditional insurers exit. We model what others approximate. And we build systems that change outcomes, not just prices.

Our leadership team includes former successful founders and CEOs from Metromile, PolicyGenius, WePay, and HotelTonight, bringing deep experience in building and scaling high-growth companies.

Background: The property insurance industry is built to price loss after it happens. It relies on coarse proxies, backward-looking data, and manual processes, then accepts damage as unavoidable.

Stand takes a different approach. We simulate how real-world catastrophes affect individual properties, translate that into actionable decisions, and automate the business around it. The result is a platform that can underwrite what others can’t and operate with far less friction.

The role

Stand is a homeowners insurance carrier for people who live where wildfire and hurricanes are a fact of life. The promise we make them is unusual: we try to reach you before the loss and get you help, and we handle the claim fast when it comes. This role owns both ends of that promise.

Right now there is no single person who owns catastrophe readiness and response across Stand. Someone has to build the plan before a season, hold our claims partners to a real standard every day, and then run the whole thing when an event is bearing down on our customers. Without that, the promise is a slogan; with it, it's something a homeowner can count on.

Concretely, the job is three things. You build and keep current the catastrophe plan, covering activation levels, who does what, vendor capacity, regulatory reporting, and how we reach customers and brokers. You manage the third-party administrators who handle our claims, day to day and against their service standards. And you own the Emergency Response Program: the work that finds policyholders in the path of an event and gets them help, increasingly automated, with people kept in the loop for the judgment calls.

You report to the Head of Claims and Client Experience and work across the company. You'd partner with Product and Engineering on the automation, with Underwriting and the market teams on where our exposure sits, and with our TPAs and field vendors every week. When an event hits, you lead the response and brief leadership. This is an in-office role in Austin.

What you'll do

-
Own the catastrophe plan across every peril and state we write, including activation levels, roles, vendor capacity, regulatory reporting, and customer and broker outreach. Keep it current and tested with a tabletop before each season.

-
Run the response when an event hits: call the activation level, lead the daily team call, direct the TPAs and field vendors, brief leadership, and put Stand people on the ground at insurance villages and with our hardest-hit customers.

-
Manage our claims TPAs day to day, including staffing, open inventory, escalations, large losses, and payment approvals within your authority. Hold them to their service standards with a regular scorecard, closed-file audits, and remedies when they slip.

-
Own the Emergency Response Program end to end: watch active events, decide when a property needs monitoring, outreach, or a vendor deployment, and direct it remotely.

-
Work with Product and Engineering to automate exposure analysis, deployment recommendations, and customer and broker outreach, extending the approach from one peril to the next while keeping the judgment calls with people.

-
Own the vendor bench across field response, mitigation, housing, contents, engineering, and independent adjusting firms. This includes contracts, standby terms, capacity, and performance, reviewed ahead of each season.

-
First 30 days: a read-out on where the current plan, TPA standards, and vendor bench actually stand, with the biggest gaps named.

-
First 3 months: a written catastrophe plan signed off by leadership and a tabletop run with each TPA, with gaps logged and closed.

-
First year: TPA scorecards running on a regular cadence with remedies applied, a vendor bench with standby terms across every active peril and state, automated exposure analysis and outreach live for the lead peril, and a response you've run cleanly through a live event or exercise.

What we're looking for

-
You've led property claims through real catastrophe events, calling the response, directing adjusters, and holding quality steady while everything is moving fast. Hurricane experience is a strong plus.

-
You've managed TPAs or independent adjusting firms: set and enforced service standards, watched capacity and pricing, and run scorecards that actually changed behavior.

-
You know state catastrophe reporting requirements and claim-handling deadlines well enough to keep a carrier compliant across several states.

-
You can run a live response from both the office and the field, and make fast, sound calls when the information in front of you is incomplete.

-
You're comfortable building from a blank page in a small, fast-moving company. There's no playbook handed to you, no large team under you yet.

Nice to have

-
Wildfire experience.

-
You've scoped automation with product and engineering teams and held them to a timeline.

-
Underwriting, inspection, or mitigation experience alongside claims.

-
Florida or high-net-worth property experience.

-
You've built or run an emergency response program before.

You're probably not a fit if

-
You want a mature playbook and a built-out team to step into. Most of this you'll build yourself.

-
You'd rather stay at the desk; this role goes to the ground when an event hits.

-
You're looking for predictable hours. Catastrophe season has no rhyme or reason.

Benefits:

Above-market Health, Dental, and Vision coverage

-
Weekly lunch stipend

-
Flexible time off + holidays

-
401(k) plan

-
Commuter benefits

-
PAT & MAT Leave

-
Short-Term and Long-Term Disability

-
Monthly team gatherings

-
In-office perks

title: Data Operations Engineer (Seattle, WA)
description:
Advanced Systems Group, LLC enables creativity through better technology and operations for media creatives and content owners. From acquisition to delivery, on-premises or in the cloud, ASG ensures our clients’ success through tailored solutions. One of North America’s largest Media and Entertainment Technology and Operations suppliers, we provide engineering services, physical and cloud integration, training, support, and managed services. ASG delivers customized operations and services for all phases of media production, including creative and engineering. Founded in 1997, and providing nationwide services, ASG has teams based in North America, South America, and Europe.

Job Summary

ASG is looking for a Data Operations Engineer to join our client’s Business Operations data team, supporting the Senior Data Operations Architect in maintaining and growing the operational backbone for a fast-growing live-streaming and commerce business. This role centers on Airtable systems, API integration maintenance, and cross-source data reliability — not traditional software or data engineering.

The complexity of this role isn't about the number of systems connected — it's about understanding how marketing, production, and monetization financials interconnect, and keeping that web of data trustworthy. You'll spend most of your time testing, maintaining, and troubleshooting; there's a real opportunity to grow into more build work as the team's data infrastructure matures.

This is a strong fit for someone who wants ground-level exposure to how a high-growth business actually runs — production economics, efficiency metrics, financial reporting — with mentorship from the Senior Data Operations Architect, and a full tech team behind you.

This full-time role is 100% onsite in the South Lake Union Neighborhood of Seattle, WA, where you will report directly to the Senior Data Operations Architect.

What You'll Do

-
Help consolidate and manage the team’s Airtable environment.

-
Maintain and troubleshoot API connections between systems like Salesforce, Coupa, and internal AWS finance tools to ensure reliable data flow.

-
Assist with automated reporting by tying financial, moderation, and production data to one central identifier (Stream ID).

-
Build and support dashboards and executive reports to track efficiency and performance.

-
Test and validate new integrations before launch, and proactively fix issues as they arise.

-
Be the go-to person onsite in Seattle, WA for daily support, escalating more complex issues to the Senior Data Operations Architect.

-
Keep our data standards, naming conventions, and system documentation up to date as we scale.

Required Qualifications

-
Experience with data engineering, SQL, data modeling, or cloud data platforms.

-
Hands-on experience building and maintaining Airtable systems at scale (multi-base, relational, dashboards).

-
Experience integrating Airtable or similar tools with other systems via API.

-
Strong troubleshooting skills; you enjoy testing, breaking, and fixing connections.

-
Curiosity about how businesses really work—with a willingness to work with financial and operational data even if you don’t have a finance background.

-
Excellent written communication and documentation skills.

-
Able to work independently and solve moderately complex problems with general guidance.

Nice to Have

-
Background in media, entertainment, live events, or e-commerce operations.

-
Experience with metadata governance, taxonomies, or data standards.

-
Familiarity with automation tools like Zapier, Make, or n8n.

If you’re ready to dive in, learn a ton, and help build the foundation for a dynamic business, we’d love to meet you!

Advanced Systems Group LLC provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

title: Engineering Lead, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
description:
Who We Are & Why Join Us

Avathon is the leading Industrial AI autonomy platform, helping customers across heavy industries -- energy, mining, manufacturing, aerospace, defense, and logistics -- accelerate the journey toward autonomous operations. Our platform is built on a Computational Knowledge Graph foundation that contextualizes and connects operational data across siloed systems, bringing together time series, structured, unstructured, and machine vision data to power AI-driven applications in asset performance management, supply chain intelligence, visual AI, and global trade management. With capabilities spanning digital twins, normal behavior modeling, natural language processing, and computer vision, Avathon delivers real-time predictive intelligence and agentic decision-making at industrial scale.

Cutting-Edge AI Innovation -- Join a team at the forefront of AI, developing groundbreaking solutions that shape the future. High-Growth Environment -- Thrive in a fast-scaling startup where agility, collaboration, and rapid professional growth are the norm. Meaningful Impact -- Work on AI-driven projects that drive real change across industries and improve lives.

Learn more at: avathon.com

We are hiring an Engineering Lead for Product Lifecycle Management to own the technical delivery of Avathon's PLM integrations and the AI capabilities built on top of them. You will work alongside our Forward Deployed Design Leads and customer engineering teams to connect PLM, CAD/PDM, ERP and MES systems to the Avathon platform, model product structures and engineering change flows in our Computational Knowledge Graph, and ship the BOM comparison, change impact and digital thread features customers use every day. This is a hands-on lead role. You will write code, own the integration architecture, and lead a small team of engineers through implementation, go-live and hypercare.

Responsibilities:

PLM Integration Architecture
- Own the technical design for integrating customer PLM systems (Teamcenter, Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, SAP PLM, Oracle Agile) with the Avathon platform
- Build and maintain connectors and data pipelines from PLM, CAD/PDM, ERP and MES sources into our Bronze/Silver/Gold data lake
- Define canonical data models for parts, EBOM and MBOM structures, variants, effectivity and engineering changes
- Set standards for data quality, sync latency and reconciliation between source systems and the platform

Knowledge Graph and AI Features- Model product structures and change relationships (ECR, ECO, MCA, MBOM, BOP) in the Computational Knowledge Graph so any change can be traced to its downstream impact
- Build the backend services behind BOM comparison, engineering change impact and clear-to-build views
- Work with our ML, data science and agent teams to apply Normal Behavior Models and AI agents to PLM data, such as flagging unusual ECR patterns or change-driven supply risk
- Turn one-off customer work into reusable platform components

Delivery and Technical Leadership
- Hands on lead to through discovery, build, go-live and hypercare on customer deployments
- Run technical working sessions with customer PLM, IT and engineering teams and act as the senior technical contact on the account
- Own go-live readiness: integration testing, data validation, performance and security review
- Review designs and code, set engineering practices, and mentor engineers on the PLM domain
- Partner with design, product and customer success to scope work, call out risk early and keep delivery on plan

Key Qualifications:

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field
- 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years leading engineers or technical delivery
- Hands-on integration experience with at least one enterprise PLM platform (Teamcenter, Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, SAP PLM or Oracle Agile), including its APIs and data model
- Strong working knowledge of BOM management, engineering change management, variants and effectivity
- Experience integrating PLM with ERP, CAD/PDM, MES and quality systems
- Strong backend skills in Python with experience building data pipelines and REST APIs
- Experience with graph data models or graph databases is a strong plus
- Familiarity with digital thread concepts; MBSE exposure (SysML, Cameo, Rhapsody) is a plus
- Experience in manufacturing, automotive, aerospace or defense environments
- Comfortable working directly with customers and traveling to customer sites
- Clear technical writing and communication

Salary Range: $160,000-$220,000

Avathon is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Avathon is committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process. If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us to discuss how we can assist you.

title: Director, Research & Data
description:
About Ceribell

Ceribell is a medical technology company focused on transforming the diagnosis and management of patients with serious neurological conditions. The Ceribell System is a novel, point-of-care electroencephalography (“EEG”) platform specifically designed to address the unmet needs of patients in the acute care setting, and is being used in hundreds of community hospitals, large academic facilities and major IDN's across the country. Our entire team is driven by a shared commitment to transforming the landscape of critical care through our rapid seizure detection technology, come join the movement!

Position Overview:

As Director/Manager of Research and Data at Ceribell, you will lead the effort to find, acquire, and secure the clinical and EEG datasets that power the development of new indications for the Ceribell EEG platform. This role is part of Ceribell's Data Science team, with a dotted line to the Clinical team, and sits at the intersection of R&D, Clinical, and our academic and hospital partners. You will build relationships with researchers and academic centers, evaluate research proposals and support research collaborations, and drive EMR integrations with partner hospitals so that Data Science has the high-quality, clinically well-characterized data it needs to build and validate new algorithms. The Ceribell EEG platform opens the door to additional clinical indications where faster access to EEG-based insight could improve patient care, and this is an opportunity to help shape that expansion.

What you'll do:

- Work with Data Science team to translate the needs of new indications into specific data requirements and a prioritized data acquisition plan.

- Identify, evaluate, and build relationships with researchers, physician advisors, and academic centers who hold or can collect the data we need. Negotiate data access, licensing, and purchase arrangements.

- Evaluate research proposals from external investigators for scientific merit, clinical relevance, and alignment with our indication priorities. Serve as the scientific point of contact for research collaborations from proposal through data return, and help shape study designs so the resulting data is usable for algorithm development.

- Lead EMR integration efforts with partner hospitals to obtain linked clinical context and outcomes data. Work with hospital IT, clinical informatics, and clinical champions to scope data feeds, mappings, and workflows.

- Assess the quality and fit of incoming datasets (label quality, cohort definition, population diversity, annotation methodology) in partnership with data scientists before and after acquisition.

- Partner with Legal, Regulatory, and Privacy on data use agreements, IRB requirements, de-identification, and HIPAA compliance.

- Work closely with the Clinical team to support early-stage clinical studies and ensure data collection aligns with study protocols.

- Maintain a data asset inventory and pipeline tracker: what we have, what we need, and what is in negotiation.

- Manage multiple simultaneous data partnerships and projects across indications.

- Represent Ceribell at scientific conferences and in academic networks.

What We're Looking For:

- Advanced degree (MD, PhD, PharmD, DNP, or equivalent) in a clinical or research-oriented field, such as neurology, neuroscience, critical care, neurophysiology, or biomedical science.

- At least 5 years of experience in clinical research, healthcare, or medical technology, with a track record of building and managing research collaborations with academic institutions and investigators.

- Strong clinical and research judgment, including the ability to evaluate study design, research proposals, and clinical data quality.

- Working knowledge of data science and machine learning fundamentals sufficient to judge dataset suitability.

- Working knowledge of basic statistics, including sample size and power, confidence intervals, sensitivity and specificity, and common sources of bias and confounding, sufficient to evaluate study designs and dataset adequacy.

- Experience with EMR data and integrations, or clinical informatics projects.

- Familiarity with clinical research regulations and data governance (IRB, HIPAA, de-identification, data use agreements).

- Experience with EEG or other biosignal data is preferred.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical data needs to clinicians and clinical context to data scientists.

- Entrepreneurial mindset, adaptability, and a passion for improving patient outcomes through data.

Compensation Range

$222,000—$242,000 USD

A candidate’s final salary offer will be based on their skills, education, work location and experience, and thus it may differ from the posted range. Compensation may also include bonuses consistent with Ceribell’s corporate compensation plan. Note, the above description is not all-encompassing and Ceribell reserves the right to change or modify job duties and assignments at any time.

In addition to your base compensation, Ceribell offers eligible employees the following:

- Performance-based incentive compensation (varies by role)

- Equity opportunities

- 100% Employer paid Health Benefits for Employees

- 50% - 70% Employer paid Health, Dental & Vision for dependents (depending on plan selection)

- 100% paid Life and Long-Term Disability Insurance

- 401(k) with a generous company match

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with a discount

- Monthly cell phone stipend

- Flexible paid time off

- 13 Paid Holidays + 3 Company Wellness Days

- Excellent parental leave policy

- Fantastic culture with tremendous career advancement opportunities

- Joining a mission-minded organization!

Application Deadline: Ongoing

Other Job Details
Ceribell reports transfers of value to health care providers (HCPs) as required by federal and state transparency laws. These laws and implementing regulations require Ceribell to provide government agencies with HCPs’ names, addresses and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. If you are an HCP and we pay or reimburse your recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Ceribell, your name, address and the amount of payments made may be reported to the government.

Equal Opportunity Employer
Ceribell is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, disability, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. Ceribell complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Ceribell is an E-Verify employer. Any applicant with a disability who requires an accommodation during the application process should contact [email removed] to request reasonable accommodation.

Privacy Statement
For information on how Ceribell processes personal data of job applicants, please review our Privacy Policy.

Compliance Disclaimer
If you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report to [email removed]. Please note that we will not respond to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

title: Portfolio Lead
description:
Portfolio Lead Salesforce, Data & AI | Financial Services & Regulated Industries

Zennify is hiring a Portfolio Leader to sell our Salesforce, data, and AI solutions to financial institutions. This is a quota-carrying role. You own pipeline, forecast, and closed revenue across your territory, and you lead deals from first contact through close.

You understand our solutions and how they translate into outcomes for banks, credit unions, wealth firms, and insurers. You know them well enough to lead the conversation, and you quarterback the right team of solution architects and engineers to scope, estimate, and win the deal.

You work AI-first, using agents and AI tooling to research accounts, prepare for meetings, support discovery, and draft proposals. That frees up time for the customer relationships that move deals forward. You have either sold into financial services or worked inside it, so you understand how these buyers evaluate and make decisions.

This is a quota-carrying role with on-target earnings of $250,000 to $350,000. You own pipeline, forecast, and closed revenue across your territory, and you lead deals from first contact through close.

Primary Responsibilities

Own the commercial cycle

- Own pipeline, forecast, and closed revenue for Salesforce, data, and AI across your territory.

- Run the full sales cycle from prospecting through close, for both new-logo and expansion business.

- Keep an accurate forecast with clear stages, next steps, and close dates.

- Co-sell with Salesforce Account Executives and RVPs to source, advance, and close opportunities.

Sell AI-first

- Use agents and AI tooling to research accounts, prepare for meetings, support discovery, and draft first-pass proposals.

- Anchor each pursuit in ZennifyAccelerate, our AI-first deal process.

- Use the time AI saves to deepen customer relationships and sharpen deal strategy.

- Apply AI in line with each client's security and regulatory requirements.

Understand the solution and quarterback the deal

- Understand Zennify's Salesforce, data, and AI solutions well enough to explain how they translate into outcomes for financial institutions.

- Position the full portfolio: Salesforce, including Financial Services Cloud, Data Cloud, Agentforce, and Marketing, plus data and AI on Databricks and Snowflake.

- Quarterback solution architects and engineers to scope, estimate, and shape each deal.

- Bring the business context and customer outcomes that let the technical team scope accurately and price with confidence.

Required Qualifications

- 5 to 7 years in a quota-carrying sales role, including experience selling Salesforce or Salesforce consulting services, ideally through the partner ecosystem.

- Financial services experience, either selling into financial institutions or working inside one, such as banking, credit unions, wealth, or insurance.

- Familiarity with the Salesforce platform and how it is sold through the partner ecosystem, including clouds such as Sales, Service, Marketing, or Financial Services Cloud.

- Working knowledge of the data and AI ecosystem around Salesforce, including Data Cloud, Agentforce, Databricks, and Snowflake.

- Fluency using AI tools and agents in your own workflow.

- A consultative approach with strong discovery skills, and the ability to connect a business problem to the right solution and outcome.

- The ability to quarterback solution architects and engineers through scoping, estimation, and proposal development.

- Clear communication with stakeholders from admin to the C-suite.

- A track record of managing a pipeline, forecasting accurately, and hitting targets.

- Willingness to work as a remote team member and travel as needed, up to approximately 30% of the time

Preferred Qualifications

- Salesforce certifications such as Administrator, Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, or Financial Services Cloud.

- Exposure to Databricks, Snowflake, or other data platforms.

- Experience with nCino for banking and lending.

- Experience with Twilio, including Flex, messaging, and customer engagement. Twilio is a plus, not a requirement.

- Experience co-selling with Salesforce Account Executives and RVPs.

- Prior time at a consulting firm or systems integrator serving financial services.

Qualities of the Ideal Candidate

- Brings grit and hustle, with strong follow-through.

- Forms a point of view and leads the conversation rather than reacting to a requirements list.

- Curious and quick to learn, especially with new technology and AI.

- Comfortable moving between technical detail and executive business value.

- Collaborative across sales, delivery, and partner alliances.

- Trusted with sensitive client data, and disciplined about security and compliance.

The full compensation package is based on candidate's experience and certifications.

Zennify pay range

$140,000—$165,000 USD

Rooted in care. Built for what’s next. At Zennify, you help people in regulated industries solve real problems at the intersection of data, AI, and customer experience. You will work across Salesforce, nCino, MuleSoft, Twilio, and Databricks, and you will deliver outcomes that hold up in production. You will join smart, kind, collaborative people who move with urgency and lead with care. We challenge each other, we support each other, and we keep expectations clear. Diverse perspectives make us better partners and better teammates, so we build teams where everyone can do their best work and feel like they belong.

How we work

- Fully remote, designed for flexibility, focus, and balance

- Paid training and certifications to support your growth

- Unlimited PTO so you can take the time you need

Benefits that support real life. We offer strong medical, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits, plus mental health support. You will also have pet insurance, pawternity and pawreavement leave, and other programs that meet you where you are.

Belonging and equity matter here. We are committed to an inclusive and equitable workplace with equal opportunity, fair pay practices, and respect for every background and identity. Come for the mission. Stay for the people.

Pay Transparency. We believe that pay transparency helps to foster trust and open communication between employers and employees. It allows our team members to have a clear understanding of their earning potential and the expectations associated with their roles. We also believe that pay transparency promotes fairness, as everyone is compensated based on their experience and skills, regardless of factors such as gender, race, or ethnicity. We recognize that the skills and experience of our candidates may vary, and we are committed to compensating them accordingly. As such, we will evaluate each candidate's qualifications, experience, and performance to determine the appropriate compensation within the stated salary range. We hope that this transparent approach to compensation will provide our potential candidates with the information they need to make informed decisions about their career paths.

About Zennify. Zennify is a data engineering and customer experience consultancy built for industries where trust and precision matter, including financial services, healthcare, and utilities. We deliver strategy, implementation, and managed services with warmth, speed, and reliability. We have delivered 600+ Salesforce projects and 200+ data projects, with a 4.9/5 CSAT. Our team holds 750+ certifications, and we continue to grow our data and AI work as our fastest-expanding area. While our roots are in Salesforce, today we help clients build modern foundations that connect data, systems, and experiences, so teams can move faster, serve better, and scale with confidence. Zennify is privately owned and backed by Tercera and Salesforce Ventures. We invest in our people, our partnerships, and our purpose.

title: Financial Planning & Analysis Manager
description:
Rhombus Power, Inc. delivers AI-powered predictive intelligence in real time for defense and national security organizations worldwide. Our mission-built products— Ambient AI and Guardian— are transforming strategic, operational, and tactical decision-making. By empowering the shift from reactive analysis to proactive, predictive intelligence and decision support, Rhombus Power is providing foresight and freedom of action when it matters most.

Come join our cross-disciplinary and world-class team that is delivering game-changing solutions to transform global security.

Learn more about Rhombus Power, Inc. and watch a demonstration of Guardian, our AI Platform here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3PxY6su1Q-Q

https://www.youtube.com/@rhombuspower8558/videos

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iby5WVNfQiI

See the following articles to learn more about what we do:

https://www.rhombuspower.com/news-and-media

Job Description

Rhombus Power seeks a hands-on, ownership-minded FP&A professional to help build financial models, reporting, forecasting, and planning processes that support our next stage of growth.

Our business combines software subscriptions with customer implementation, deployment, and support across commercial and government environments. You will help leadership understand how revenue, delivery costs, hiring, and contract timing affect profitability and cash—and turn that understanding into actionable investment decisions.

This is an ownership role within a small but robust team, with substantial ownership from data collection through recommendations. You need to bring established FP&A skills, enjoy building with limited infrastructure, and be comfortable moving between detailed analysis and practical business decisions, all within a fast-paced environment.

Please note that this is a HQ-based role with a 4 days/week onsite policy in our Palo Alto office. Please do not apply if you cannot meet this requirement.

What You’ll Own:

Budgeting, Forecasting & Modeling

- Assist in the creation, maintenance, and execution of the annual corporate budget, partnering with department leaders on revenue, headcount, infrastructure, and operating expenses.

- Update and maintain monthly and quarterly rolling forecasts using integrated three-statement models covering the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow.

- Build driver-based forecasts connecting sales pipeline, contract start dates, implementation schedules, renewals, and expansion to financial performance.

- Perform scenario analysis and financial modeling to stress-test growth assumptions, including delayed awards, longer sales cycles, customer concentration, and accelerated hiring.

Revenue

- Maintain clear visibility into bookings, annual recurring revenue (ARR), recognized revenue, billings, and cash collections, distinguishing recurring software revenue from implementation and services.

- Partner with Sales and customer teams to forecast renewals, expansion, churn, and pipeline conversion; explain changes in revenue performance and forecast confidence.

- Incorporate government contract funding, periods of performance, option-year assumptions, award timing, and invoicing milestones into forecasts.

- Distinguish funded commitments from potential contract value, and model the cash and resource implications of procurement or payment delays.

- Support contract and deal reviews with pricing, margin, payment-term, and delivery-cost analysis.

Monthly Variance Analysis

- Conduct monthly actual-versus-budget and actual-versus-forecast variance analysis, explaining underlying drivers and identifying actions for business owners.

- Review general ledger details to identify misclassifications or unexpected spending trends, partnering with Accounting to resolve discrepancies.

- Track corporate cash burn, working capital metrics, and primary efficiency ratios on a daily or weekly cadence, as appropriate.

- Maintain workforce models covering approved positions, hiring dates, compensation, benefits, contractors, and vacancies; partner with Recruiting and department leaders to keep assumptions current.

Financial Reporting & Dashboarding

- Prepare monthly and quarterly financial reviews that explain performance, forecast changes, and emerging risks in clear business terms.

- Build, update, and maintain business intelligence (BI) dashboards tracking financial and operational key performance indicators (KPIs).

- Provide data-driven schedules, trend charts, and commentary for monthly business review decks and support board reporting.

Systems

- Clean and structure historical operational datasets to improve forecasting precision.

- Support development projects, ROI analyses, pricing reviews, and unit economics updates, including product investments and expansion opportunities.

- Identify and implement ways to automate manual data collection workflows and recurring reporting.

- Help build the FP&A function’s core models, planning calendar, reporting standards, and tools, introducing useful structure as business needs evolve.

What You Bring

- Approximately 3-5 years of relevant experience, including direct responsibility for budgeting, forecasting, financial modeling, and variance analysis, preferably in a small or midsize B2B SaaS company. Candidates with specific experience working in enterprise sales cycles or meaningful implementation and delivery costs is ideal.

- Experience working on lean teams, with personal ownership from gathering inputs and building models through presenting findings and following up with business owners and executives alike.

- Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, experience building integrated three-statement and driver-based models, and strong accounting fundamentals.

- An understanding of SaaS revenue mechanics and metrics, including ARR, retention, bookings, revenue recognition, and gross margin.

- Experience developing BI dashboards and reconciling financial and operational datasets; SQL and workflow automation skills are a plus.

- Demonstrated ability to build planning models, reporting, or processes from scratch and translate incomplete information into clearly documented assumptions.

- Creative problem-solving, flexibility, and sound judgment: you can adapt quickly while preserving accuracy, checking your work, and making uncertainty visible.

- Strong communication skills and the confidence to question assumptions constructively with technical, commercial, and executive stakeholders.

Helpful Additional Experience

- Exposure to government-facing software businesses, federal procurement cycles, or contract-level financial analysis.

- Experience forecasting cloud or AI infrastructure costs, deployment economics, or customer-level profitability.

Salary

- This position has a salary range of $110,000 to $140,000. Final salary will be determined based on experience and qualifications.

Benefits

- Full medical, dental, vision coverage for employee and dependents

- 401k matching program

- PTO and Holidays

- Bonus and other incentive programs

- Access to mental health program

- Access to Flexible Spending Accounts for Health Care, Dependent and Commuter

About Rhombus

Rhombus Power Inc. (Rhombus) is a startup located in the heart of Silicon Valley at Stanford Research Park in Palo Alto. We use cutting-edge cross-disciplinary approaches to solve pressing Big Data and Sensing problems in security, energy, and healthcare. Our advisory board includes two Nobel Laureates and a Draper Prize winner.

Rhombus compensates, motivates, and develops employees, who are trusted, empowered, and involved. Employees have clear roles and expectations – and their roles are flexible enough to move at the speed of innovation in order to meet and exceed client expectations. We have a unique culture of global purpose, rooted in the innovation and progress of Silicon Valley.

Rhombus knows that diversity is a condition for success. We are committed to hiring and retaining a diverse workforce. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer.

title: Research Program Manager
description:
About AfterQuery

AfterQuery is an applied research lab curating data solutions for foundation model development. We serve every frontier AI lab with the mission of delivering the best data to power the best models. In doing so, we can make expertise that once took a lifetime to build available to anyone who needs it.

Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We're based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI.

Why Apply

Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we're not slowing down.

Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up.

Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity. As we scale, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the engineering organization and lead major technical initiatives.

Strong Team: Our founding team has experience from Citadel Securities, Meta, Google, Silver Lake, and Morgan Stanley — work alongside world-class engineers and researchers.

Overview

AfterQuery is hiring a Research Program Manager to run the operations behind its research programs: public benchmark releases, collaborations with academic and industry partners, and the research roadmap. You own the coordination, external relationships, and progress tracking that keep the program moving, and you are welcome to contribute to the research itself, from benchmark design to co-authoring publications.

This is a technical, hands-on role, not a pure coordination one. You will read results tables, run evals, sanity-check numbers before they go public, and turn loosely specified research needs into engineering and operational roadmaps. You will also be the program's voice to external partners, so clear writing and confident communication across researchers, executives, and academics are as important as technical fluency. You work daily with researchers, engineers, domain experts, and go-to-market partners.

Responsibilities

-
Serve as the point of contact for collaborations with academic and industry partners, including fellowships, grants, and joint research projects, and run each from scoping through delivery.

-
Coordinate benchmark releases end to end, from launch checklist through publication, and keep releases on cadence.

-
Maintain AfterQuery's leaderboards and benchmark sites, and verify every result before it goes to a community leaderboard or publication.

-
Track progress across all active research projects. Anticipate resourcing gaps and technical bottlenecks, unblock projects that fall behind, and escalate with a clear recommendation when a timeline or scope needs to change.

-
Coordinate the expert pool for upcoming benchmarks: forecast expert needs, manage capacity, and keep contributor logistics running.

-
Write the program's external and internal communications: launch briefs, partner updates, planning documents, and status memos that turn technical detail into clear, actionable summaries.

Required Qualifications

-
1-3+ years in research operations, technical program management, or a similar role in a fast-moving research or engineering organization.

-
Technical background in computer science, machine learning, statistics, or a related field, with working Python and SQL.

-
Evaluation literacy: you have taken part in evaluating a product, an agent, or a foundation model, can read a results table, and can tell when a number should not be trusted.

-
Excellent written and verbal communication. You can distill a technical result into a summary a partner, executive, or academic collaborator can act on, and you write documents people actually read.

-
A track record of running cross-functional programs end to end, including managing external partners, contractors, or collaborators.

-
Comfort with ambiguity and building processes from scratch, and the judgment to keep processes light so researchers stay effective.

Preferred Qualifications

-
Graduate degree or research experience in a technical field.

-
Contributed to a benchmark, dataset, or evaluation project in any role.

-
Familiarity with public leaderboards or open research communities.

-
