If you’re looking for a role where you’ll tackle challenging problems, work with ambitious brands, and help shape the future of organic growth, let’s talk.

Learn about the principles that drive how we work and build a company.

About This Role
We're hiring a native Japanese-speaking content editor and writer to edit and create long-form content in Japanese for our B2B SaaS clients. This is a freelance position. Most of the work will be editing and refining LLM-generated drafts so they read naturally, accurately, and persuasively for Japanese professional audiences. You'll also write original content from scratch when a project calls for it. You'll work closely with our editorial team to produce well-researched, engaging, AEO and SEO-optimized content that drives results.

We're ideally looking for someone based between GMT-0 and GMT+9, so you can collaborate easily with our Japan and EU teams. We may be open to other time zones for the right candidate.

If you're a native Japanese speaker with a sharp editorial eye, you're comfortable working with AI-generated content, and you enjoy digging into complex topics, we'd love to hear from you. The application passcode is 言葉の職人. Please note that we do not work with writers or editors who subcontract their work.

Responsibilities

-
Edit LLM-generated drafts into polished, natural Japanese. You'll spot and fix the telltale signs of machine-generated text, such as awkward phrasing, unnatural sentence rhythm, literal translations, inconsistent register, and factual inaccuracies. The finished piece should read as if a skilled native writer wrote it.

-
Write high-quality, long-form content in Japanese from scratch across a variety of B2B, SaaS, and technical topics. You'll create informative, engaging, and well-researched content for professional audiences in the Japanese market.

-
Fact-check and verify claims, statistics, and sources in every draft. LLM content can sound confident and still be wrong, so you'll make sure everything is accurate and properly supported.

-
Conduct thorough research to understand client products, target audiences, and industry context. Your work will be rooted in real understanding, not surface-level fluff.

-
Localize content for Japanese readers, not just translate it. You know how Japanese business audiences expect information to be structured, framed, and supported, and you'll adapt examples, tone, and references to match.

-
Use our internal briefs to structure and outline articles clearly and effectively. Our briefs give direction, and you'll bring clarity, logic, and structure to each piece.

-
Incorporate keywords and AEO/SEO best practices without compromising readability or quality. You'll balance search optimization with a natural, audience-first style that fits Japanese search behavior.

-
Adapt your style to match the voice and tone of different client brands. You're comfortable moving between registers, including appropriate use of keigo, depending on the brand and audience.

-
Collaborate with our Japan and EU editorial teams across time zones. You'll revise and refine content based on feedback and communicate clearly with the Editorial Strategist about progress, questions, or blockers. You'll join occasional meetings with the internal team and client teams.

-
Consistently meet deadlines. You'll stay on top of timelines and keep communication proactive and respectful.

Who You Are

-
A native Japanese speaker. Native-level written fluency is required. You write and edit with confidence for a native Japanese audience.

-
An experienced editor and writer with 2–3 years of experience editing and/or writing content for marketing, SEO, or B2B brands.

-
Comfortable working with AI-generated content. You've edited LLM output before, or you're confident you can quickly recognize and fix its weak points in Japanese.

-
Professionally proficient in English. Briefs, feedback, and team communication are primarily in English.

-
Detail-oriented, with a strong grasp of Japanese grammar, style conventions, and consistency (e.g., notation, katakana usage, punctuation, and terminology).

-
Skilled at simplifying complex information into clear, actionable content. You enjoy making technical or abstract ideas accessible and engaging.

-
Familiar with SEO fundamentals and how to write for both readers and search engines. You know how to format, structure, and optimize without sounding robotic.

-
Comfortable writing for different audiences, from technical practitioners to business decision-makers.

-
Organized and self-motivated. You can manage your own workload, hit deadlines, and juggle multiple assignments reliably.

-
Open to feedback and collaborative by nature. You see feedback as a tool for growth, not a critique of your ability.

-
Friendly, curious, and passionate about producing truly valuable content. You care about the craft and want your work to matter.

-
A degree in journalism, Japanese language or literature, linguistics, translation, creative writing, marketing, or a related field is preferred but not required.

Portfolio Requirement
Please submit 3–5 samples of written or edited content in Japanese. At least 2 should focus on B2B, SaaS, or technical topics. We'd especially like to see editing work, such as a before-and-after example or a piece you substantially revised. Older samples are fine if paired with more recent work.

Our Hiring Process
We read every application and aim to get back to you within a few weeks of submission. Response times may vary depending on the time of year, number of applicants, and other factors. However, we are urgently hiring for this role. If we're interested in moving forward with your application, we'll likely reach out sooner via email.

Benefits of working with us
We're here to enable you to do great work and grow.

-
We're a 100% remote company, so you can work from anywhere

-
You'll improve your SEO, editorial, marketing, and project management skills

-
Ownership: there are ample opportunities to take on more responsibility

We know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. But there’s no such thing as a "perfect" candidate. Omniscient Digital is a place where everyone can grow. However you identify and whatever background you bring, please apply if the idea of this role excites you.

The Robinhood Chain team designs and scales the underlying decentralized infrastructure across Robinhood. title: Marketing Manager, Lifecycle
description:
About Abacum

Abacum is the leading Business Planning solution for finance teams to drive performance. By automating reporting, enabling collaboration, and simplifying planning and forecasting, we help finance teams shift from number crunching to driving strategic decisions.

Founded in 2020 by two former CFOs, we’ve grown into a global team of 100+ people across 30+ nationalities. Headquartered in New York, we have offices in Toronto and Barcelona. We’re trusted by industry leaders such as Dish Networks, Strava, BetterUp, Kajabi, JG Wentworth, Abridge, Cortex, and hundreds more.

We have raised over $100m, closing in June 2025 our $60M Series B, led by Scale Venture Partners, with the strong participation of Cathay Innovation, Y Combinator, Atomico, Creandum, and angel operators from Adyen, Zapier, and Twitch.

Our mission is ambitious and we can’t do it alone - join Abacum as we build the future of Business Planning!

About the role

You own lifecycle marketing at Abacum: the path a lead takes from first interest through high intent to conversion, and the programs that carry them along it. You will design the nurture tracks, the segmentation and the scoring that decide what a lead sees next, and you will own the numbers that say whether any of it worked.

This is a build role. You are the first person here dedicated to this surface, so the programs, the measurement and the handoff to sales are yours to design rather than inherit. That means real latitude over what gets built first, and real accountability for the result.

What you will do

-
Own the lifecycle programs that carry a lead from first interest through to a sales conversation.

-
Design nurture tracks that match where someone is in their evaluation

-
Define what makes a lead ready for sales and where it routes once it is.

-
Connect account-level engagement signals to the follow-up programs that act on them.

-
Run the marketing automation stack day to day, including flows, lists, data hygiene and deliverability.

-
Report on conversion between lifecycle stages so the team can see which programs are producing pipeline.

-
Test offers, timing and audience cuts continuously so the program mix keeps improving.

What you bring

-
Lifecycle marketing expert with hands on experience: You have run lifecycle marketing at a seed to Series B B2B company where you were both the strategy and the execution.

-
Or marketing ops that grew into it: You came from marketing with analytical acumen, so you understand the data model underneath the programs and not only the campaign layer.

-
Hands on the tools: You have experience building Hubspot flows yourself rather than briefing someone else to build them.

-
Not specialized away from execution: You want the whole lifecycle surface rather than one slice of it divided between an email team, an ops team and an agency.

-
Conversion as the measure: You judge your own work on stage-to-stage conversion and contribution to pipeline.

-
Clear about the handoff: You have worked closely enough with sales to know that a lead marketing calls ready and a lead a rep calls ready are not always the same thing.

-
Based in New York: You are in NYC and want to work hybrid alongside the rest of the marketing team.

Bonus points

-
You have marketed to finance teams or another technical buyer where credibility matters more than volume.

-
You can write SQL or work directly in a data warehouse to answer your own questions about funnel performance.

Benefits

-
Competitive compensation including equity package

-
Competitive vacation policy

-
Medical Insurance

-
L&D budget

-
Access to Meditopia (wellbeing platform)

-
Language courses (English / Spanish)

Our Values

Customer Obsession: We share the understanding that Abacum's sole purpose is to create value for customers and relentlessly deploy all creativity and energy to that end.

Audacious Ambition: We dream big and embrace discomfort. We assume risks, make on-time mistakes and learn how to methodically accomplish our goals.

Good People: We are self-reflective and praise diversity of thought. We don't justify the end with the means and know where to draw the line. We have fun every day.

Tough Love: We truly care for everyone in the team and embrace honest feedback and radical candor as ways to genuinely help each other.

We are seeking a Pricing Analyst to join our Finance team. This is a hands-on, detail-oriented role embedded within our Commercial organization. - Partner with Commercial, Clinical/Operations, and Actuarial teams to develop pricing models and present summaries to senior leadership

title: Lead, GTM Analytics & Applied AI
description:
About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.

Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.

Our vision

We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.

But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.

Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.

In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.

Our traction

Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com website.

More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.

Our team

Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.

We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.

Where we work

Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!

Why we are looking for you

We're building the most data-driven GTM organization in SMB technology space, and we need dedicated analytics and applied AI leads to support our Sales and Marketing engines.

At Owner, the Business Operations team doesn't just analyze the business. We build products and systems that drive it. Our GTM analytics team has already built ML-powered lead scoring that 2x'd our LTV:CAC ratio, automated account research that doubled rep output, and intelligent routing systems that optimize pipeline for hundreds of reps. And we're just getting started.

Sales and Marketing are at an inflection point. We're expanding into new product verticals and AI-led offerings, scaling new acquisition channels, and standing up entirely new GTM motions. This role will be at the center of designing, measuring, and optimizing them.

As a Lead, GTM Analytics & Applied AI, you'll be a senior contributor who drives analytics and strategy end-to-end for either our Sales or Marketing org. You'll work directly with the CRO or CMO and their leadership team to identify the highest-impact opportunities, then build the analyses, tools, and AI-powered systems that turn them into results.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the US or Canada.

You should definitely apply if you…

-
Have felt torn about whether to pursue a business vs. technical/analytical career path (at Owner we believe these must merge)

-
Get more energy from building and shipping than from analyzing and presenting

-
Are excited about applied AI: building AI-powered products, and using AI to change how analytics and building gets done

-
Get energized by new frontiers — defining the next version of our GTM strategy, not just optimizing existing playbooks

-
When solving problems, dive deep to understand root causes and become a subject matter expert. You don't stop at surface-level insights

-
Aren't afraid to pick up new tools and skills, from Claude Code to custom machine learning pipelines, whatever the problem requires

-
Want to build lasting systems and products, not one-off analyses

-
Thrive in ambiguity and don't need a playbook to figure out what to work on next

The impact you will have

-
Own GTM analytics for your function: Build the visibility into performance metrics across the funnel that Sales or Marketing run on. Power the weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews with the analyses and metrics that matter

-
Strategize across the funnel: Work directly with the CRO or CMO to support spend allocation decisions, shape our GTM motion, and bring rigor and a point of view to the biggest strategic questions

-
Direct the pod: Set the priorities and direction for the analytics and applied AI work supporting your function. Guide the work happening in your pod, partnering with Associates to shape analyses and recommendations

-
Build AI-powered tools that drive incremental value: Ship things like automated outbound campaigns, intelligent engagement cadences, and other AI-powered workflows to engage customers more efficiently and effectively

-
Experiment with new channels: Stand up new channels and motions, then build playbooks for repeatable experimentation so wins compound over time

-
Accelerate impact with AI: Establish how your function and the broader BizOps team uses AI to multiply output across analytics and operating workflows

Who you'll work with

Reporting Structure: This role reports to Meera Singh, Director of GTM Analytics and Applied AI

Cross-functional Partners: You'll partner most closely with leadership in your function — either Sales (CRO, Sales leadership, RevOps) or Marketing (CMO, Growth, Lifecycle, Brand) — and collaborate across the broader GTM org on shared initiatives.

Technical Collaboration: You will collaborate with Analytics Engineers on all technical aspects, including data modeling, data quality, and the use of tools like DBT and Snowflake.

Executive Visibility: This work directly drives GTM strategy, which means regular exposure to senior and executive leadership, including the CRO and CMO.

What we're looking for

-
7+ years in analytics, strategy, or ops - whether that's management consulting, startup ops & analytics, or a hybrid path that's hard to label

-
You've personally shipped data products, models, or AI-powered systems into production — not just delivered insights

-
Excellent numerical skills, with additional technical background or education strongly preferred. Claude is a must and SQL/Python skills are a plus!

-
Familiarity with how Sales or Marketing teams actually operate. Deep functional pedigree not required, but you should be able to come up to speed quickly

-
You've worked in the messy middle between business strategy and technical execution. Consulting, startup analytics, BizOps, or a hybrid path that's hard to label

-
Self-sufficient operator. You can run an end-to-end workstream without needing scaffolding

-
Have managed a team of analysts before, or are excited about the opportunity to do so — you take satisfaction in helping others do their best work

-
Comfortable with ambiguity — you don't need a playbook to figure out what to work on next

-
Experience with marketplaces, AI software, and/or high-growth startups preferred

-
Restaurant industry experience is a plus!

Compensation & Benefits

The estimated starting base salary range for this role is $190,000 - $210,000 USD per year, plus a generous pre-IPO equity package.

Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, remote-first workplace, unlimited PTO, plus extra fun perks!

title: Senior Software Engineer | Cloud
description:
At ExtraHop, we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise. We reveal what is happening in the very infrastructure that sustains businesses, lives, and communities, and ensure the integrity of networks, data, systems, and processes. Organizations rely on ExtraHop to provide visibility into the cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and network performance issues that evade their existing security and IT tools. With this insight, organizations can investigate smarter, stop threats faster, and keep operations running.

Our mission is fueled by a profound social and moral responsibility to be the best at what we do, ensuring a secure world where everyone can thrive. If this sounds like a place you’d like to spend the next chapter of your career, we’d love to hear from you.

Position Summary

At the heart of our Cloud team is a mission to build a secure, scalable, and high-performance platform that powers our cybersecurity products. As a Senior Software Engineer, Cloud, you will own the design, delivery, and operation of critical cloud services, driving architectural decisions and ensuring systems meet the highest standards of reliability, security, and scalability.

This role goes beyond implementation. You will lead complex technical initiatives end-to-end, influence system design across teams, and set the standard for engineering excellence within the cloud domain. You’ll partner closely with engineering, security, and product teams to solve deeply technical challenges and evolve our cloud platform to meet the demands of a rapidly growing business.

Key Responsibilities

- Own the architecture, development, and operation of scalable, secure, and fault-tolerant cloud services, with accountability for performance and reliability in production.

- Drive technical design and architectural decisions for distributed systems, influencing patterns, standards, and long-term platform evolution.

- Lead complex initiatives end-to-end, from design through deployment and ongoing optimization, ensuring alignment with business and technical priorities.

- Build and scale cloud infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm) and container orchestration (Kubernetes), improving system resilience and efficiency.

- Advance cloud security and compliance practices, embedding secure design principles, IAM controls, and encryption into all layers of the platform.

- Improve system observability and operational excellence, implementing robust monitoring, alerting, and incident response strategies.

- Drive DevOps maturity, optimizing CI/CD pipelines and deployment strategies to support rapid, reliable delivery.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, product, and security teams to define solutions and resolve complex system-level challenges.

- Mentor and guide engineers, providing technical direction, code reviews, and support for skill development while raising the bar for engineering quality.

- Continuously evaluate and adopt new technologies, making pragmatic decisions that improve system performance, scalability, and developer productivity.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).

- 6–8+ years of software engineering experience, with significant focus on cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

- Proven ability to independently design, build, and operate production-grade systems at scale.

- Strong proficiency in Go, Python, or similar languages, with experience building distributed services.

- Deep expertise in Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm).

- Strong experience with AWS services (EKS, EC2, RDS, S3, SQS, IAM), including designing and operating systems in production.

- Demonstrated ownership of systems, including on-call, incident response, and long-term reliability improvements.

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to navigate ambiguous, complex technical challenges.

- Effective communication skills with the ability to influence technical decisions across teams.

- Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder) or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

- Expertise in cloud security best practices, including identity, encryption, and compliance frameworks.

- Experience designing and scaling high-availability distributed systems with automated failover and self-healing capabilities.

- Strong knowledge of observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK).

- Experience with event-driven architectures and microservices.

- Familiarity with HashiCorp ecosystem tools (Vault, Consul, Packer).

- Experience contributing to or defining engineering standards, patterns, or platform strategy.

The salary range for this role is $160,000 - $180,000 + bonus + benefits.

ABOUT EXTRAHOP

ExtraHop is reinventing Network Detection and Response (NDR) to offer enterprises unparalleled visibility, context, and control against emerging threats. The platform integrates NDR with Network Performance Management (NPM), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and forensics, providing a single, comprehensive solution. By decrypting and analyzing complete packet-level data at wire speed and leveraging cloud-scale machine learning, ExtraHop empowers Security Operations Centers (SOCs) to detect, investigate, and remediate modern cyber risks in real time across their entire hybrid infrastructure, including data center, cloud, and SASE environments.

This comprehensive approach and market innovation have earned ExtraHop unique recognition as the only NDR vendor acknowledged as a leader by all major analyst firms, including the 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant for Network Detection and Response™, the 2025 Forrester® Wave for Network Analysis and Visibility, the 2024 IDC® Marketscape for NDR, and the 2025 Gigamon® Radar Report for Network Detection and Response. Since 2007, ExtraHop has consistently helped organizations worldwide extract in-depth network telemetry and contextual insights, affirming its commitment to protecting and empowering the connected enterprise.

OUR VALUES

Our culture is rooted in our five Values. These set the expectations for how we work individually and collectively as a team.

Lead with Purpose: We are driven to deliver results that create a positive impact for our customers, partners, and colleagues.

Act with Integrity: We operate with transparency, authenticity, and always in the best interest of the company.

Find a Way: We are resourceful, tackle hard problems with a sense of urgency and ownership, and do what it takes to get the job done.

Innovate: We listen to customers, partners, and the market, and respectfully push boundaries and challenge the status quo.

Share Success: We run together, we win together. We value diverse perspectives, hold space for all voices, and achieve the best results as a team.

BENEFITS

Employees' wellbeing is top of mind for the ExtraHop team. Employees and their families will have the option to participate in the following benefits:

title: Staff Security Architect
description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

*Note: This position requires presence in our Bellevue, San Francisco, or San Jose office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

About the Role

Lambda Security protects some of the world's most valuable digital assets: invaluable training data, model weights representing immense computational investments, and the sensitive inputs required to leverage best of breed AI models. We're responsible for securing every byte that powers breakthrough artificial intelligence.

Reporting to the CISO, you'll be a principal technical leader responsible for shaping Lambda's overall security architecture, with a primary focus on Data Protection and Platform Security. Your work will define secure-by-default foundational patterns across our core AI infrastructure, hardware/GPU platform layers, multi-cloud control planes, and end-to-end data lifecycles.

You will directly impact the security posture of our high-performance computing environment by architecting robust data loss prevention (DLP), encryption at rest and in transit, key management (KMS/HSM), confidential computing, and tenant isolation models. Leveraging Lambda's hosted LLMs, you'll pioneer AI-driven security architecture capabilities—such as automated threat modeling, sensitive data discovery, and platform policy verification.

If you're excited about setting the architectural vision for data protection and platform security in the world's most demanding AI infrastructure, we want to talk.

We value diverse backgrounds, experiences, and skills, and we are excited to hear from candidates who can bring unique perspectives to our team. If you do not exactly meet this description but believe you may be a good fit, please still apply and help us understand your readiness for a Staff Security Architect role. Your application is not a waste of our time.

Data Protection Architecture:

-
Architect, design, and standardize end-to-end data protection strategy, encompassing data classification, cryptographic key management (KMS/HSM), data loss prevention (DLP), and privacy-preserving controls across customer data and AI model weights

-
Define data lifecycle security controls for training datasets, checkpoint storage, and model artifacts across cloud and on-premises storage layers

-
Drive confidential computing architectures, envelope encryption, and hardware-backed data security guarantees for high-consequence customer workloads

-
Establish robust zero-trust data access policies and fine-grained authorization frameworks for sensitive platform APIs and data repositories

Platform Security & Infrastructure Hardening:

Design and enforce core platform security architectures across multi-tenant GPU infrastructure, bare-metal clusters, hypervisors, and container orchestration platforms (Kubernetes)

-
Define strong tenant isolation, sandboxing, and secure virtualization controls to protect against cross-tenant side-channel and platform escape vulnerabilities

-
Conduct comprehensive threat models, architectural reviews, and risk assessments for core platform services and platform control planes

Automation & Strategic Innovation:

-
Prototype reference implementations and security controls in Python or Go to demonstrate secure platform integration patterns

-
Pioneer AI-powered architectural security capabilities leveraging Lambda's hosted LLMs for automated threat modeling, automated policy validation, and data discovery

-
Assess third-party vendor risks and build automated tooling to evaluate SaaS vendor security postures

Strategic Leadership & Alignment:

-
Partner closely with Platform, Engineering, Product, and Infrastructure leaders to embed security architecture into long-term product roadmaps

-
Author technical whitepapers, architectural blueprints, and customer-facing trust documentation highlighting Lambda's platform security and data protection posture

-
Mentor senior engineering talent across the organization on secure design principles, platform security patterns, and threat modeling

What We Think a Candidate Needs to Demonstrate to Succeed

-
10+ years of total engineering experience with 5+ years specializing in security architecture, platform security, or data protection at cloud/infrastructure scale

-
Deep expertise in data security concepts including encryption key management (KMS/HSM), cryptographic protocols, DLP, and confidential computing primitives

Proven track record of designing multi-tenant platform security architecture across heterogeneous infrastructure (bare-metal GPU clusters, hypervisors, KVM, Kubernetes, and public cloud)

Strong technical skills in prototyping security designs and reference code in Python, Go, or similar languages

Demonstrated experience with threat modeling methodologies (STRIDE, PASTA, etc.) and security design reviews for high-consequence systems

Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with a track record of partnering effectively with IT, Legal, and HR

Ability to balance robust enterprise security controls with employee experience and productivity

Thrives in fast-moving, high-growth startup environments where building scalable structure is required

In this fast-paced, agile environment, you will lead projects from concept through delivery, collaborating closely with product, design, engineering, finance, and customer success teams to ensure alignment and success. You will set the standard for engineering excellence by mentoring engineers at all levels and championing a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and technical rigor.

A key part of this role is to ensure development teams follow best practices, coding standards, and technical requirements. You will provide hands-on technical guidance and architectural direction, including code and design reviews, while creating and maintaining design and code standards. Understanding, communicating, and enforcing Redwood’s software architecture strategy will be fundamental.

You will proactively identify critical technical challenges related to quality, scalability, observability, and performance. Leveraging data analysis, code reviews, and collaboration with cross-functional teams, you ensure that solutions are robust, efficient, and scalable, driving Redwood’s platform forward with confidence.

You will work directly with the Engineering manager for your teams and collaborate closely with Redwood’s Architecture team to ensure technical alignment, consistency, and strategic direction across the platform. - CI/CD and Observability: Oversee and enhance automated build, test, and deployment pipelines (CI/CD, Kubernetes/Docker) in a cloud environment (AWS/Azure/GCP), leveraging AI tools for proactive anomaly detection and monitoring.

- Collaborating with the product management team to define, design, and implement new functionality that enhances Redwood's software solutions.

- Diagnosing and resolving complex technical challenges and system issues to ensure platform reliability.

YOUR EXPERIENCE

The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field. You should have over eight years of software development experience, with at least three to five years in a senior or staff software engineer role. This position requires proven experience in workload automation, job scheduling, and orchestration technologies.

- Deep proficiency in Java (11/17+), with strong experience in modern frameworks and libraries.

- Strong background in microservice architecture, containerisation (Docker, Kubernetes) and RESTful API design.

- Experience with frontend technologies including ReactJS, MobX, and TypeScript.

- Knowledge of cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

- Strong understanding of database technologies (SQL, NoSQL, data modelling).

- Familiarity with DevOps practices and CI/CD pipelines.

- Familiarity with tools like Git, GitHub, Jira and Bamboo from Atlassian.

- Proficiency in testing frameworks such as JUnit, Jest and Playwright with a focus on driving quality automation and testability by design.

- Commitment to engineering best practices, including code reviews, static analysis and continuous quality improvements.

- AI Tool Fluency: Demonstrated ability to proficiently use AI-powered developer tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, CodeWhisperer) in a production environment.

- Code Judgment: Proven track record of evaluating and overriding AI-generated suggestions that are technically correct but architecturally flawed or non-compliant with security and performance best practices.

- Prompting Proficiency: Experience writing clear, contextual, and effective prompts for generative AI to produce usable code, tests, or documentation.

- Adaptability & Learning: High degree of curiosity and a proactive approach to learning new AI tools and techniques that continuously reshape the development workflow.

- Domain & Architectural Focus: The capacity to abstract away from low-level coding details to focus on high-value business logic and systemic architectural integrity.

title: Senior AI Researcher
description:

· Build agents on frontier APIs that understand unfamiliar software and complete real business tasks
· Create the eval and benchmark system that tells the team when an agent truly got better

Python, frontier model APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), agent and eval tooling of your choice. The team has no fixed stack and builds its own when that works best.

description:

Our teams lead full-funnel marketing transformations—from strategy and go-to-market execution to experience design, performance measurement, and sustainable impact.

It’s an exciting time to join us. SiaX has long been the agency behind some of the world’s biggest brands—now we’re expanding, becoming one of the most recognizable names for companies that demand bold, business-driving creative. We’re shaping SiaX into the go-to agency of the future. This is your chance to be part of that growth, working alongside top-tier creatives, consultants and agency leaders to continuously evolve what a modern, full-service agency can be. Opportunities like this don’t come around often—if you want in on the next level, this is it.

Job Description

Contract roles are geared toward independent professionals interested in temporary or project-based work.

Sia Title: Project Consultant (Exempt Contractor)

Project Title: AI Product Community Manager

Project Length: This is a temporary position with an expected duration through 6/30/27, may extend

Project Hours: 40 hours per week

Rate: $75-95/hour

The expected compensation for this contract is per year. The exact pay rate will vary depending on a wide array of factors, which may include but are not limited to skills, experience, and location.

Location: Open to remote candidates

About the Role

Sia is partnering with one of the world's leading technology companies to help build the community around a next-generation consumer AI product at the frontier of artificial intelligence.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape a new community experience from the ground up, powered by cutting-edge AI and designed for people looking to get more out of life with the help of AI agents. The product is already generating real organic energy: users are showing up, experimenting, sharing what they create, and forming their own pockets of culture without much prompting. Now, the opportunity is to turn that momentum into a community that lasts, scales globally, and meaningfully influences where the product goes next.

You'll play a critical role in defining how people connect, collaborate, learn, and create value within an AI-enabled ecosystem with the potential to reach millions. You'll work at the intersection of AI, consumer technology, community, product, and culture, combining the creative freedom of building something new with the reach and resources of one of the world's largest technology companies.

We're looking for someone who thinks like both a strategist and a builder. Someone who is equally energized by understanding community behavior through data, designing engagement programs, testing new ideas, and leveraging AI to create smarter, more personalized community experiences.

This isn't just about managing a community. It's about helping define what community looks like for a new generation of AI products and creating a direct connection between some of the product's most engaged users and the teams building its future.

If you're passionate about emerging technology, human behavior, community growth, and creating experiences people genuinely love, we'd love to meet you.

What You'll Do

Own the Community Strategy

-
Define what community means for an emerging AI product: who it's for, what members get out of it, and how it grows

-
Build a home for the most engaged users that remains valuable, trusted, and well-run as the community scales

-
Develop ambassador, advocate, and power-user programs that give highly engaged users a meaningful role in the community

-
Design and test engagement programs that deepen participation, connection, and long-term community value

-
Make it simple for members to run their own events and meetups through scalable programs and toolkits

-
Partner closely with social, brand, and creative teams to bring what the community is creating to a broader audience

-
Drive adoption in new markets through community-led outreach, adapting the approach as the product expands internationally

-
Explore how AI can enable smarter, more personalized, and more scalable community experiences

Build the Growth Loop

-
Partner with growth teams on referral and invite mechanics that feel organic to the community

-
Identify creators, advocates, and early adopters producing compelling content and help them continue building

-
Turn community participation into sustainable product advocacy, referrals, and organic growth

-
Use community behavior, engagement data, and experimentation to understand what drives participation, retention, and advocacy

-
Keep authentic user stories, use cases, and emerging behaviors flowing back to marketing and product teams

-
Test new ideas quickly, learn from the results, and scale the programs that resonate most with members

Connect the Community to the Product

-
Serve as the internal voice of the community, translating user behavior, feedback, emerging AI use cases, requests, and friction into insights Product and Engineering can act on quickly

-
Identify how people are actually using and experimenting with the product, including behaviors and use cases the team may not have anticipated

-
Build feedback loops between early adopters and the teams shaping the product roadmap

-
Own community health metrics including activity, retention, sentiment, advocacy, and community-driven growth

-
Combine qualitative feedback with participation and behavioral data to identify patterns, opportunities, and emerging needs

-
Help ensure the path from product to community, and from community back to product, actually works

Qualifications

What You Bring

-
8+ years of experience across community, social, developer relations, creator programs, product advocacy, or related areas

-
Experience supporting at least one consumer technology product at meaningful scale

-
Demonstrated experience building an ambassador, advocate, creator, or superuser program from the ground up

-
A builder mindset with experience taking community programs from idea to launch, testing what works, and iterating quickly

-
Strong interest in artificial intelligence and how AI products are changing the way people create, communicate, and interact with technology

-
Experience building community around an AI, generative AI, emerging technology, or highly technical product is strongly preferred

-
Ideally, experience engaging early adopters or technically curious users around rapidly evolving products

-
Experience scaling an online community beyond manual moderation through automation, community roles, governance, escalation paths, and scalable processes

-
Strong analytical instincts and the ability to use community behavior, engagement data, and qualitative feedback to inform strategy

-
Ability to translate community insights into clear, actionable recommendations for Product and Engineering

-
Strong writing skills and a distinct, authentic voice. You understand internet culture, can read a room, and know how to communicate in a way that feels human rather than corporate

-
Comfort operating in an early-stage environment where the product, community, and playbook are still evolving

-
A track record of building trust as a core part of the community experience

Nice to Have

-
Direct experience with AI, generative AI, AI-powered consumer products, AI agents, or emerging technology communities

-
Experience launching or managing beta, early-access, or design-partner programs

-
Experience working with highly engaged early adopters and translating their feedback into product insights

-
Experience using AI, automation, or personalization to improve community engagement or operations

-
Experience building community internationally

-
Experience with creator-led or user-generated content ecosystems

-
Experience working with a product built around a distinct character, identity, or persona

What Success Looks Like

-
A thriving community that grows organically, where people initially show up for the AI product and stay for the community around it

-
A community experience that helps people connect, collaborate, learn, and discover new ways to get value from AI

-
A recognizable power-user or ambassador program that members genuinely want to join

-
Early adopters and highly engaged users consistently influencing the product roadmap

-
A steady flow of emerging AI use cases, user behaviors, and community insights reaching Product and Engineering

-
Community programs that are continuously tested and improved using engagement data, member behavior, and feedback

-
The most engaged users becoming some of the product's strongest advocates and sources of organic growth

-
A scalable community model that can grow alongside the product as it reaches millions of users across new markets

title: Monetization Strategy Manager
description:

Our products help people make powerful connections, discover exciting opportunities, build necessary skills, and gain valuable insights every day. We're also committed to providing transformational opportunities for our own employees by investing in their growth. We aspire to create a culture that's built on trust, care, inclusion, and fun – where everyone can succeed.

Join us to transform the way the world works.

Go-to-market and monetization strategies for next-generation of consumer subscription products as Premium rolls out new AI-based features and products

Evolution of the current product portfolio, pricing and offers to accelerate growth in emerging markets and high growth segments

Pricing and packaging strategy that best serves LinkedIn's member base across evolving audiences like Creators, Entrepreneurs, Thought Leaders and Gamers

Measure and track monetization performance to enable continuous improvements to our pricing and packaging.

Drive recommendations and partner with stakeholders to turn opportunities into realized value by providing guidance and support throughout the go-to-market processes.

4+ Years of Pricing, Strategy & Operations, Business Strategy, Finance, Business Analytics and/or Go-To-Market Strategy experience at a SaaS company or similar experience in an analytical role.

-
BA/BS degree in economics, management science, business, applied math, statistics, finance, analytics or related field.

-
Experience leveraging AI-based tools and solutions to conduct market research, quantitative assessments to drive process improvements and analysis

-
Experience conducting end-to-end market research for willingness-to-pay assessments (e.g. Van Westendorp, Gabor Granger, Conjoint etc.).

-
Experience operating in a cross-functional work environment with a consistent record of delivering impact.

-
Proven track record in developing the business case for changes in Go-To-Market strategy for a global senior executive audience (Senior Directors/VPs/LOB C-Suite).

-
Comfortable building and interpreting subscription and product performance reports, running own SQL analyses and building financial models.

-
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, “get it done” entrepreneurial environment.

-
Ability to structure and communicate complex information in a simplified manner both written and verbally.

-
Relevant graduate level degree in business (i.e., MBA), economics or a related field.

-
Comfortable with developing creative solutions under ambiguity and uncertainty.

-
Strategic and creative problem-solver who loves to tackle complex challenges in a collaborative team environment.

-
Intellectually curious and adaptable to different environments and team settings.

-
Monetization strategy skills. Ability to understand member needs/perceived value, drive customer value creation, and develop go-to-market and growth strategies to accelerate subscription growth.

Suggested Skills

-
Communication skills

-
Analytical Skills

-

title: Intermediate Site Reliability Engineer
description:
Hey there! We're ContactMonkey 👋

Our mission is to power measurable employee engagement worldwide, and we're looking for an Intermediate Site Reliability Engineer to join our Engineering team.

About the job

We're looking for someone who enjoys running production systems, understands how applications work, and brings practical application security experience.

You'll work closely with our SRE and development teams to maintain our infrastructure, improve deployments, investigate production issues, and address security risks. You'll also contribute to the technical controls that support SOC 2 audits and GDPR compliance.

Our environment includes AWS, Kubernetes on EKS, Terraform, Terragrunt, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, and CloudWatch. Our applications use Ruby on Rails, Vue.js, and Node.js, with MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Sidekiq supporting the backend.

You'll take ownership of defined projects and operational improvements, with senior engineers available for guidance and review. There's room to develop deeper expertise in reliability, infrastructure automation, and application security.

- Terraform & Terragrunt: Build and maintain infrastructure as code, review plans, manage environment configuration, and address infrastructure drift.

- Deployments & developer experience: Improve CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, release checks, and rollback procedures.

- Monitoring & incidents: Improve monitoring and alerts, join the on-call rotation, and contribute to incident reviews.

- Application security: Work with developers to assess vulnerabilities, review security risks, and validate fixes.

- CI/CD security: Maintain code, dependency, secrets, container, and infrastructure scanning.

- Cloud security: Strengthen IAM, secrets management, network controls, and Kubernetes security.

- SOC 2 & GDPR: Support technical controls, audit evidence, and personal data protection.

- Recovery: Test backups and recovery procedures, maintain runbooks, and support production readiness.

- Collaboration: Participate in code reviews, document changes, and support application, AI, and data engineering teams.

About you

- Around 3–5 years of experience in SRE, DevOps, platform engineering, cloud operations, or a related engineering role. Equivalent practical experience is welcome.

- Hands-on experience supporting production workloads in AWS.

- Experience writing and maintaining Terraform modules and Terragrunt configuration, including reviewing plans and working with remote state.

- Experience with Docker and Kubernetes, including troubleshooting deployments, services, health checks, and resource limits.

- A solid understanding of Linux, networking, DNS, HTTP, and TLS.

- Ability to write automation in Python, Bash, Ruby, JavaScript, or another suitable language.

- Experience with Git, pull requests, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment workflows.

- Experience using logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerts to investigate production problems.

- Practical application security experience through vulnerability remediation, secure code review, threat modelling, or security tooling.

- Understanding of common web application risks, including broken access control, injection, authentication weaknesses, and sensitive data exposure.

- Familiarity with IAM, least privilege, secrets management, and encryption.

- Working knowledge of SOC 2 controls and GDPR principles relevant to engineering, including access restrictions, data minimization, retention, and deletion.

- Clear communication skills and good judgment about when to work independently, request a review, or escalate an issue.

How you can stand out

- Supported Ruby on Rails or Node.js applications in production

- Worked with MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis or Valkey, and Sidekiq

- Experience with GitHub Actions, Argo CD, Helm, Karpenter, or KEDA

- Built useful monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, or CloudWatch

- Supported services across multiple AWS regions

- Helped remediate penetration-test findings or contributed technical evidence to a SOC 2 audit

Working with the team

You'll work closely with SRE and application engineers, and support AI and data initiatives where they depend on shared infrastructure.

We value people who ask questions, explain their reasoning, and leave systems easier for others to understand. You'll take part in technical discussions and code reviews, share what you learn, and help improve how we operate.

ContactMonkey helps organizations create, send, and measure internal communications directly within Outlook and Gmail.

title: Associate Director, Clinical Data Management
description:
About Summit:

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.

Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

-

HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

-

HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

-

HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC)

-

HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland.

Overview of Role:

We are looking for an experienced Associate Director, Clinical Data Management that will contribute to and support the company's research and development efforts to create high value therapeutics to address unmet medical needs. The Associate Director, Clinical Data Management independently leads the data management components of a clinical trial ranging from small early phase to large global and late phase programs. This role will direct the planning, implementation and overall direction of executing/achieving clinical trial data management activities including CRF/eCRF design, database development, validation programming, data review, discrepancy management, and database lock. Additionally, the position will manage data management staff, Contract Research Organizations (CROs) and service providers' activities in overseeing the data management process life cycle in coordination with internal Biostatistics, Clinical, and Regulatory teams to ensure the accurate, efficient, and complete data collection for clinical trials.

Role and Responsibilities:

- Provide expertise and contribute to the strategy and development of the Clinical Data Management Portfolios to ensure data quality in support of clinical study data milestones and deliverables

- Lead and support establishment of systems and processes to help ensure clinical data security, integrity, and long-term goals of the business function, in alignment with company priorities

- Leads the data management of overall drug development process with early and late phase clinical trials in large or complex development program(s)

- Provides technical expertise to develop and implement clinical data standards, data management plans, data transfer agreements, and data flow processes to ensure timely and quality data delivery for analysis purpose

- Oversees the process to identify, evaluate and select CROs, vendors and technology for CDM activities

- Leads, designs and/or oversees eCRF design, eCRF specifications, eCRF completion guidelines, annotated CRFs, User Acceptance Testing, query logic, edit checks, data query resolution, SAE reconciliation between clinical and pharmacovigilance databases, vendor data reconciliation & cleaning, data migration and database closeout for clinical trials

- Represents Data Management and promotes productive collaboration with other functions (e.g., Clinical Operations, Clinical Development, Biostatistics, Statistical Programming, Translational Science, Project Management, Regulatory, QA, and IT) to ensure proper alignment around data management activities & deliverables, operational excellence, compliance with regulations, policies, procedures, and clinical objectives

- Supports cross functional teams and studies to handle data management questions, troubleshoot, help resolve issues and mitigate risks. Initiates continuous efforts in reviewing and identifying best practices among study teams and enforcing standardization among teams and studies

- Works with the Director of Clinical Data Science (CDS) to enhance efficiency, optimize costs, and drive excellence

- Works with the Director of Clinical Data Science to establish CDM processes and procedures including SOPs to ensure highest data quality/integrity/security and regulatory. compliance with FDA regulations, GCP, ICH guidelines and Good Clinical DM Practices.

- Leads clinical data management activities during regulatory audits, ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulations, and providing expert input throughout the audit process

- Works with the Head of Statistical Programming & CDS to manage departmental budget and execute resource planning across multiple projects

- Works with the Director of Clinical Data Science to provide oversight and guidance, as well as establish key performance metrics with CROs to ensure the highest data quality/integrity and regulatory compliance

- Accommodate ad hoc data requests between clinical team members, scientists, and vendors to support data cleaning, data entry requirements and exploratory data review if needed

- Uses scientific and drug development knowledge to anticipate and mitigate data management-related challenges during clinical trial execution

- Reviews and contributes to clinical protocols and amendments, study manuals, and other study conduct related clinical documents; review clinical data according to these documents

title: Senior Consultant
description:
Who We Are

Workhelix is an enterprise SaaS company with a single goal: helping organizations get the most out of their AI investments.

Our people and software combine to give leaders answers to the three critical questions about the business value of AI:

- Where are our top opportunities to create value with AI?

- Are our current efforts actually delivering? What’s their ROI?

- How can we accelerate and increase the benefits of our AI?

To find answers for each customer, Workhelix applies our unmatched expertise in economics, AI, and data science. We have pioneered a task-scoring method to identify top GenAI opportunities, ensuring clear, data-driven deployment strategies. Our ROI monitoring suite applies Nobel Prize-winning economics to provide accurate, ongoing insights into the impact of GenAI implementations. Renowned AI and Economics thinkers including Andrew Ng, and cofounders Andy McAfee and Erik Brynjolfsson stand proudly behind our mission.

We maintain a culture established on five key principles. For more information on our leadership principles, please visit the careers page of our website.

Role

At Workhelix, the Senior Consultant is pivotal in transforming complex business challenges into actionable solutions. You'll be the bridge between customer needs, data insights, and service execution, ensuring that organizations can make better, faster, and smarter decisions with our expertise. This role combines analytical problem-solving, deep user empathy, and strategic execution.

Key Responsibilities

- Engage deeply with customers to understand their strategic goals, operational challenges, and data landscapes.

- Identify critical workflows and data sources that drive AI adoption and business transformation.

- Build quantified business cases that connect Workhelix insights to measurable customer outcomes - giving client executives a clear, defensible case for action.

- Spearhead client workstreams with our Engineering and Product teams to design and deploy scalable, customized solutions that meet client needs.

- Lead customer onboarding and enablement sessions to the Workhelix Nucleus platform to ensure adoption and empower users to generate actionable insights.

- Present data-driven insights and strategic recommendations to client executives, ensuring alignment on value realization.

- Work cross-functionally to influence product enhancements based on field insights.

- Scope new and expansion engagement opportunities and assess how Workhelix can drive transformation across diverse industries.

- Work closely with sales colleagues to continuously deliver value for the customer and grow the ACV for Workhelix.

- Drive execution by running SteerCo meetings, managing agendas, documenting decisions, and sharing clear follow-ups to keep projects on track.

- Bring structure to ambiguous environments by organizing workstreams, maintaining alignment across stakeholders, and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.

What We Value

- Analytical thinkers who can hold their own with data and engineering teams and who know how to translate a finding into something an executive can act on.

- Customer-centric problem solvers who dig past what a client explicitly asks for to understand what they actually need, and who bring structure to messy, ambiguous situations without being told what to look for.

- Product-minded, even without the title. You have a strong sense of what's worth building and can prioritize customer requests in a way that keeps trust intact, even when the answer is no.

- Outcome-driven people. You don't stop at the insight, you translate it into a quantified business case that gives a customer's leadership a concrete reason to act.

- Low-ego and highly accountable people. When something goes wrong in front of a client, you own it, fix it, and move on rather than pointing to the work you did.

- Proactive learners who get up to speed in unfamiliar domains without waiting to be taught, and who find shifting scope energizing rather than destabilizing.

- Natural relationship builders across functions. You can align engineering, data science, product, and sales toward a shared outcome without having formal authority over any of them.

- People comfortable driving change without direct authority. You can diagnose why adoption is stalling inside a client organization and create pull rather than waiting for someone to ask.

- Builders of process, not just followers of it. You're comfortable designing an operating rhythm from scratch: agendas, documentation, follow-through.

- Exceptional communicators who read a room and adjust instinctively, whether it's a Head of Engineering, a CIO, or a CFO on the other side of the table.

- Meticulous individuals. You catch the small thing in a deliverable or a follow-up email before it becomes the client's reason to lose confidence.

What you bring

- 6+ years of experience in client-facing roles, particularly in strategy, consulting, SaaS customer-facing environments (e.g., customer success, implementation, or professional services), or similar, with experience coordinating internal engineering and data science teams.

- A demonstrated ability to deliver results in complex organizational environments like B2B enterprise.

- Experience building quantified business cases, or a demonstrated ability to pick this up quickly, translating an insight into something a customer's finance or executive stakeholders will act on.

- Comfort navigating complex data ecosystems and identifying insights that drive business value. You don't need to be a SQL or Python practitioner, but you need to think quantitatively and know how to credibly translate into customer insights.

- Experience developing novel, software-led solutions to drive business outcomes for enterprise customers.

- A track record of driving adoption and behavior change with stakeholders you don't formally manage.

- Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to shift register across technical and executive audiences.

- Comfort with ad-hoc data analysis.

- Ability to travel (up to ~25%) as required by client and business needs.

- Based in or willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area for in-office collaboration.

Nice to have

- Working SQL proficiency

- Prior experience in an early-stage, high-growth SaaS environment.

- Experience building or scaling internal processes from scratch in an ambiguous org.

- Experience working with SaaS sales teams and a history of recognizing expansion opportunities.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days:

- You understand the Workhelix product and methodology and can confidently answer common customer questions.

- You understand how we engage customers across pilot and pull engagements, including how Senior Consultants collaborate with Sales, Product, and Engineering.

- You understand how Workhelix creates value for customers and can clearly articulate our value proposition.

By 60 days:

- You are running customer engagements end-to-end, effectively coordinating customer stakeholders and internal resources.

- You are identifying meaningful product signals from customers and bringing those insights back to Product and Sales while advocating for customer needs.

- You can tell a compelling, data-driven story to customer stakeholders at multiple levels—from managers and directors to the C-suite—and clearly articulate the value Workhelix is delivering.

By 90 days:

- You are independently managing a portfolio of customer accounts and driving engagements forward with minimal oversight.

- You are identifying and deploying novel solutions that help customers get more value from their AI investments.

- You are proactively identifying opportunities for additional value and engaging customers in expansion and renewal conversations.

Pay range and compensation package $145,000- $225,000 + Equity + Health Benefits

What You’ll Get

- Competitive compensation package and benefits.

- Chance to learn and collaborate with some of the most famous researchers in the AI and digital economy space: Andrew Ng, Erik Brynjolfsson, Andy McAfee, and Daniel Rock.

- The unique opportunity to help build a company, culture, and products from the ground up with a team that values healthy working practices.

- A high-trust, high-autonomy work environment.

At Workhelix, we stand committed to ensuring an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available without any discrimination. We believe diversity is critical to our success. Selection for employment will solely be based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply!

title: Head of Legal, Commercial
description:
About OLIX

AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The industry is still leaning on a ten-year-old hardware blueprint that has reached its limit. A new paradigm that is faster and more efficient will be the biggest economic opportunity of the next century and create the most important company of the next decade. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance.

The Role

We are hiring our Head of Legal, Commercial to lead and scale the commercial legal function at OLIX. Reporting to the Chief Legal Officer, you will own commercial contracting end to end as OLIX moves from a small legal team to a function that supports a rapidly scaling business. You will be the lead lawyer on some of our most important projects and largest and most complex deals, the person the business comes to to help them make clear and quick risk decisions and, as the company grows, you will have the opportunity to recruit team members. You will define the playbooks, standards, and tooling that let OLIX scale faster than legal headcount.

This is a player-coach role for a technically excellent, experienced lawyer who wants to own a function in an environment accelerating and changing quickly, work hands-on with engineers and commercial leaders, and shape how commercial legal works at one of the most ambitious deep-tech companies in Europe. You will not be sitting above the work. You will be leading the toughest negotiations yourself, making judgement calls where the law, the facts, and the commercial picture are all still moving, and building the team that handles everything else. OLIX moves quickly, priorities shift, and there is often no precedent to lean on. You need to have worked in an environment like this before, or be able to show you would thrive in one.

Open to UK-based candidates and US-qualified attorneys willing to relocate to London. We provide full visa sponsorship and relocation support.

Responsibilities

-
Lead the commercial legal function end to end: strategy, team, deal flow, tooling, and standards.

-
Personally lead negotiations on OLIX’s largest and most complex commercial deals, including customer agreements with hyperscalers, manufacturing, and other supply chain agreements with contract manufacturing partners, NREs, JDAs, technology licences, and strategic partnerships.

-
Build and scale the commercial legal team as OLIX grows. You will be hands-on as the main lawyer on your own projects from day one and, in time, hire, develop, and line-manage additional team members.

-
Set commercial legal standards, playbooks, fallback positions, and templates across the function.

-
Working with the CLO, make risk decisions, and help the business make them. Cut through ambiguity, frame legal and commercial risk in plain terms, recommend a position, and own the call, including where the facts, the law, or the commercial context are developing and moving quickly.

-
Design and build scalable legal workflows using AI tooling and automation, so the legal function scales faster than headcount.

-
Integrate AI deeply into day-to-day contracting: triage, first-pass review, redline generation, clause extraction, precedent search, and playbook enforcement.

-
Set OLIX’s positions on key commercial terms including liability caps, indemnities, IP ownership and licensing, data protection, warranties, termination, and service levels.

-
Own the IP dimension of commercial work: structure and negotiate IP ownership, background and foreground IP, licensing, confidentiality, and know-how provisions in JDAs, NREs, and manufacturing and supply arrangements, working closely with engineering and IP counsel to protect OLIX’s core technology, working closely with the CLO and other senior leaders to define and implement IP strategy.

-
Partner with Sales, Supply Chain, Procurement, Operations, and Engineering to align legal with business strategy.

-
Manage external counsel for specialist workstreams including US contracting, specialist IP, data, and export controls.

-
Partner with the CLO and other team members on cross-functional matters including corporate, governance, and regulatory work that touches commercial contracting.

-
Contribute to legal tooling selection, CLM implementation, and internal enablement across the broader legal team.

Skills & Experience

-
Qualified solicitor in England and Wales, or US-qualified attorney (admitted to a US state bar), guidance being at least 8 to 12 years of post-qualification experience.

-
Trained at a top-tier City, US, or comparable international firm.

-
Technically excellent lawyer. Rigorous legal analysis, precise drafting, and a structured approach to playbooks and standard forms. You know when precision matters and when speed does, and you are the person more junior lawyers check their work with.

-
Demonstrable track record leading complex commercial contract negotiations end to end as the responsible lawyer, not just supporting a partner, and of being the main lawyer on multi-workstream projects (a manufacturing ramp, a major customer deployment, a strategic partnership) rather than on a single contract.

-
Technical IP experience. You have negotiated IP ownership, background and foreground IP, licensing, confidentiality, and know-how provisions in technology development, manufacturing, and supply arrangements (JDAs, NREs, foundry and supply agreements), ideally involving semiconductors, hardware, or other deep technology. You do not need to be a patent attorney, but you need to understand what is being created and licensed and how to protect it.

-
Comfortable operating in ambiguity and making risk decisions. You can take an incomplete picture, work out what matters, give a clear recommendation, and own it. You help the business make good risk calls rather than handing it a list of issues.

-
Proper, relevant experience of an environment like OLIX: you have built, scaled, or meaningfully contributed to a commercial legal function in a fast-moving technology or hardware business, ideally a venture-backed scale-up, working directly with founders, engineers, and commercial teams.

-
Line-management or mentoring experience with junior counsel, paralegals, or secondees. Does not need to be extensive but needs to be real, and you want to manage and grow a team as the function scales.

-
Comfortable with technical subject matter. You can get to grips with OLIX’s technology well enough to draft and negotiate around it credibly and to hold your own with engineers.

-
AI-native approach to legal work. You actively use AI tools in your day-to-day practice, have strong instincts for what AI does well and where it fails, and treat AI fluency as a core craft skill rather than a novelty.

-
Bias toward building scalable systems over doing work manually. You look for the automation, template, or workflow that solves the problem ten times, not just once.

-
Commercially pragmatic, able to move at pace, and comfortable owning positions without constant supervision.

-
Direct, plain-language communicator.

-
The right fit for how OLIX works: hands-on, direct, high ownership, and comfortable being part of the team rather than a gatekeeper. You would rather solve the problem than write the memo.

Nice to have

-
Experience in technology or in technical manufacturing more broadly, ideally B2B hardware, semiconductors, or infrastructure. Highly desirable.

-
Supply chain experience: supply, manufacturing, component, and logistics arrangements, and the issues that come with scaling a hardware supply chain (capacity and volume commitments, allocation, lead times, quality, tooling, dual-sourcing). Highly desirable.

-
Familiarity with enterprise or cloud customer contracting, including bespoke negotiations with hyperscalers.

-
Understanding of export controls (particularly the US and UK regimes for advanced computing and semiconductors) and data protection as they arise in commercial contracts.

-
Experience implementing or selecting CLM or legal AI tooling (Ironclad, Harvey, Legora, Spellbook, Robin, Eve, etc.).

-
Light coding or low-code fluency (Python, SQL, Zapier, n8n, or similar) for building internal workflows.

Compensation & Equity

-
Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience, skills, and location

-
Equity & Ownership: Meaningful stock options. You’re not just joining the mission; you’re owning a piece of it

-
Proximity Bonus: We value your time. To minimise your commute and maximise your life, we offer an annual Living-Local Bonus if your residence is within 20 minutes of the office

-
Retirement Benefits: Employer-contributed retirement plans to help you build long-term financial security.

Due to U.S. export control regulations, candidates’ eligibility to work at OLIX depends on their most recent citizenship or permanent residency status. We are generally unable to consider applicants whose most recent citizenship or permanent residence is in certain restricted countries (currently including Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Belarus, China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Venezuela). Applicants who have subsequently obtained citizenship or permanent residency in another country not subject to these restrictions may still be eligible.

title: Lead Analyst - Business Operations - Wise Business
description:

title: Software Engineer
description:
We are the platform turning browsing into shopping. We connect 200 million shoppers with deals they love while boosting local sales for hundreds of top retailers and brands.

We help consumers save time and money while making smart shopping decisions, and we support retailers and brands in engaging customers from online research to in-store purchases.

Ready to spark your growth with us?

WHO WE LOOK FOR 🦄

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our Content Platform team.

You will maintain and evolve FAdmin, our core flyer processing system, together with the other systems the team owns: workflow executor, vendors, merchant admin, FTP sync and store admin.

You will deliver roadmap work end to end, support the team on our service desk and stakeholder request boards, and work AI-first: using Claude Code and agentic coding every day to ship faster, and helping make FAdmin easier for AI agents to work on safely.

If you enjoy owning a mission-critical production system, shipping quality code with a tight feedback loop, and shaping how a team develops software with AI agents, this role is for you!

WHAT YOU WILL DO 🏄

- Maintain, evolve, and deliver roadmap features end-to-end for FAdmin and Content Platform ecosystem tools.

- Work with an AI-first approach every day using tools like Claude Code and agentic workflows to accelerate delivery, improve code quality, and refactor codebase architecture to be agent-friendly.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED 🪄
