- Proven production experience building and maintaining applications with Ruby on Rails.

- 2 to 5 years of solid experience working with relational databases and SQL query design.

- Daily experience using AI coding agents (Claude Code or similar) for planning tasks, reviewing/testing AI-generated code, and maintaining strict quality standards.

- Experience with automated testing, code reviews, and CI/CD practices.

- History of shipping quality code and features reliably to production.

- Fluent English: Strong written and spoken communication skills.

👉 At our company, we value diversity and actively encourage it — we believe a variety of perspectives and backgrounds makes us stronger. We focus on potential rather than on having a “perfect” CV. If this role excites you and you believe you could grow into it — even if you don’t tick every single box in the requirements — we’d love to hear from you!

NICE TO HAVE 🎆

- Deep understanding of skills, MCP servers, subagents, CLAUDE.md, and context engineering.

- Experience with Kafka or message broker systems.

- Exposure to Docker, Kubernetes (EKS), and AWS.

- Experience with Datadog and participating in production on-call rotations.

- Hands-on experience with JavaScript / TypeScript.

- Familiarity with LLM-powered product features or content/catalog data pipelines.

SALARY RANGE ⚖️ : €45,000 – €55,000 fixed gross salary per year.

LOCATION 🌐

While we have offices in Milan and Barcelona you can benefit from our flexible hybrid model, empowering you to work where you’re most effective in Europe.
Full remote available from Europe.

WHAT YOU WILL FIND AT SHOPFULLY 🤗

🌎 An opportunity to thrive in a rapidly scaling multinational company

🕶️ A vibrant, informal, and inclusive work environment

🧠 We champion autonomy, flexibility, and a hybrid work model, empowering you to own your work

📚 Access to learning opportunities and regular feedback sessions

🍓 Enjoy our central, modern offices featuring fresh snacks, coffee (including vegan options!), and ergonomic setups

🎉 Engage in meaningful team events: offsites, happy hours, company parties and celebrations that unite us beyond daily tasks

💻We provide all the necessary equipment for you to work effectively and set up your workspace, wherever you are

🧰 Benefit from additional country-specific advantages based on local contracts and practices

WHO WE ARE 💜

We’re a team of 450 people (and counting!), from 30 different nationalities. We’re on a mission to innovate, and we believe the key to that is seeing the world through a variety of perspectives. That’s why building a more diverse team, as well as bringing in even more talent, is so important for us.

Always Build Better: We are builders—of products, systems, and ideas. But more than that, we are builders of better. Better has no finish line. It’s a mindset.

title: Software Engineer - AI Systems
description:
About XBOW

Build the future of offensive security with XBOW. Attackers are already using AI to move faster than defenders can react—we’re creating the platform that puts security ahead in the arms race. Our AI-powered system autonomously discovers, validates, and even exploits vulnerabilities, giving organizations proof-backed results in hours instead of weeks.

Founded by Oege de Moor, creator of GitHub Copilot, and backed by Sequoia, Altimeter, and other leading investors, XBOW is applying cutting-edge AI to one of the world’s most urgent problems. In just over a year, our AI, built by a world-class AI team and legendary security researchers — has uncovered thousands of real-world zero-days across the software billions rely on, and became the first autonomous system to reach number 1 on HackerOne.

We’re a team of builders, hackers, and researchers who thrive on solving problems others think are impossible. If you want to push the boundaries of AI, reshape how security is done, and join the group defining this new era of defense — we’d love to talk.

Your Role

We’re looking for a Software Engineer with deep expertise in LLM prompting, orchestration, and software engineering. In this role, you’ll design and implement systems that coordinate large language models with real-world tasks, advancing the intelligence at the heart of our platform. You’ll collaborate with our AI, Engineering and Security teams to create novel prompting strategies, build orchestration layers, and deliver production-ready systems in TypeScript.

This role is for someone who thrives in a fast-moving, research-driven environment and enjoys turning ambiguous ideas into robust, scalable solutions.

What You'll Do

-
Build LLM-powered software that actually works, by designing prompt flows and orchestrations that ensures great performance with no false positives.

-
Architect and build an AI-powered software stack that is production-grade, testable and maintainable.

-
Design and build experiments and evaluation frameworks for performance testing of the system at scale. Conduct data analysis to draw conclusions.

-
Collaborate with the rest of the AI team, with security experts, and both frontend and backend developers to create end-to-end systems that work and customers love.

-
Own projects end-to-end: from basic ideation and experimentation to deployment and production monitoring.

-
Continuously conduct research on how to harness the advancements in LLMs to make our system better and faster.

Who You Are

-
Strong experience with building software around LLMs: prompting, agentic orchestration, fault-tolerance, and integration of LLM parts with hard-coded logic.

-
Strong software engineering skills: architecting and building production-grade software that runs reliably and can be maintained.

-
Experience with TypeScript or proven ability to learn a new programming language quickly.

-
Strong skills in structured and independently-driven problem-solving. Able to work with incomplete information and rapidly testing hypotheses.

-
Comfortable with an energetic environment that mixes the fast-paced agile prioritisation of a startup with the curiosity mentality of a research lab.

-
Eager to own projects and jump into the deep end, learning as you go. Curious, adaptable and collaborative.

-
MSc or equivalent or higher in computer science, math, physics or machine learning.

Bonus If You Have

-
Prior experience with the security sector, especially involving offensive security and/or applying LLMs in a security context.

-
Contributions to open-source software, particularly within applications of or frameworks for LLMs.

-
Strong theoretical background, e.g. a Ph.D in machine learning, computer science or math.

-
Startup experience and comfort with ambiguity.

What We Offer

-
Compensation & Equity: Competitive salary and a generous equity package, making you a true owner of the company.

-
Career Growth: Shape your role, lead the function, and grow with the company as we redefine cybersecurity.

-
Meaningful Work: You will tackle technically complex challenges and play a pivotal role in the growth of our business, working alongside an amazing team and some of the world’s experts to shape how AI transforms cybersecurity.

What Else You Should Know

-
Location: Remote (all team members are remote but we meet regularly and you’re supported to travel to collaborate with colleagues in person)

-
Contract: Full-time.

-
Hiring Process:

-
45-min introductory chat with our Talent team.

-
45 minutes with one of our Engineering Leads.

-
2-3 hour technical deep dive around relevant case study.

(Yep, we think BIG.) We like to think of ourselves as more than a fintech; we're a catalyst for economic mobility.

Clasp Finance equips colleges and universities with lending technology to launch and operate their own private student loan programs, enabling schools to step in and support their students directly with financial aid. Recent federal financial aid changes are reshaping how institutions think about supporting their students, and Clasp Finance is poised to meet this moment.

We are looking for someone who cares about building technology that expands access to education and economic mobility, and that shows in how you work and persevere through the challenges of this changing industry

title: QA Engineer, Voice AI Agents
description:

We optimize complex healthcare workflows that interface with patients using the latest Agentic AI approaches, and we combine it with a sophisticated platform to serve this Agentic layer at scale.

Backed by one of the largest seed rounds in health tech history and operators who bring the expertise and distribution to scale nationally, we're building the connected infrastructure healthcare should have had all along.

Our Culture & Values

We are a high-performing group of engineers dedicated to delivering innovative, high-quality solutions to our clients and business partners. We believe in:

-
Excellence: Taking immense pride in our craft and the products we build, treating both with utmost respect and care.

-
Impact-Driven Development: Firmly committed to engineering high-quality, fault-tolerant, and highly scalable systems that evolve seamlessly with business needs, minimizing disruption.

-
Collaboration Over Ego: Valuing exceptional work and groundbreaking ideas above all else. We seek talented individuals who are accustomed to working in a fast-paced environment and are driven to ship often to achieve significant impact.

-
Continuous Growth: Fostering an environment of continuous learning, mentorship, and professional development, where you can deepen your expertise and grow your career.

Responsibilities

As a QA Engineer reporting to the Head of Product, you will be the person who digs into calls and platform issues. You will review conversations, trace failures through transcripts, logs, and campaign configuration, find the root cause, and work with engineering and deployment teams to fix it. Work cross-functionally with engineers, deployment managers, and clinical and nurse operations staff. This role combines hands-on investigation, structured QA process, and growing automation.

Call and issue debugging:

-
Investigate reported and detected issues on live campaigns, including dropped calls, wrong agent responses, failed handoffs, incorrect scheduling outcomes, and data mismatches.

-
Trace problems across call recordings, transcripts, system logs, campaign configuration, and integration data to find the actual root cause.

-
Write clear, reproducible bug reports that engineers can act on right away, with severity, member impact, and supporting evidence.

-
Triage incoming issues, separating agent behavior from configuration errors, data problems, and platform bugs, and route each to the right owner.

Campaign QA:

-
Run pre-launch QA on new campaigns and workflow changes: test scripts, edge cases, escalation paths, and handoffs to nurses or live staff.

-
Carry out ongoing conversation QA on live campaigns against defined quality standards, and flag trends before they turn into customer issues.

-
Check that campaigns behave as designed: correct targeting, sequencing, disposition logic, and outcome capture.

Process and automation:

-
Help build and maintain the QA framework: test cases, scoring rubrics, regression suites, and release checklists.

-
Automate repetitive checks where it makes sense, such as transcript analysis, config validation, and outcome reconciliation.

-
Track quality metrics and report patterns to deployment, product, and engineering so issues get fixed at the source.

Minimum Qualifications

-
3 to 5 years in QA, support engineering, technical operations, or a similar role on a production software platform.

-
A strong debugging instinct. You like finding out why something broke, and you don't stop at the first plausible answer.

-
Comfort reading logs, querying data with SQL, and working with APIs and JSON or YAML configuration.

-
Experience writing test plans and bug reports that engineers trust.

-
Clear written communication and precise documentation habits.

-
Good judgment on severity and prioritization when several issues are live at once.

Preferred Qualifications

-
Experience with voice AI, conversational AI, IVR, or contact center platforms.

-
Scripting ability in Python or similar for automating checks and analysis.

-
Exposure to LLM evaluation, prompt testing, or conversation quality scoring.

-
Healthcare experience, especially payer or provider outreach, and familiarity with HIPAA and PHI handling.

-
Experience with observability tools or with call analytics tools.

This role will be remote or onsite in our New York City or Boca Raton office, a fast-paced, collaborative environment where great ideas move quickly from whiteboard to production.

Generous Paid Time Off (PTO): To ensure a healthy work-life balance.

Life and Disability Insurance: Providing financial security.

Professional Development Budget: Support for conferences, courses, and certifications to fuel your continuous learning.

title: Software Engineer III | Framework
description:
At ExtraHop, we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise. We reveal what is happening in the very infrastructure that sustains businesses, lives, and communities, and ensure the integrity of networks, data, systems, and processes. Organizations rely on ExtraHop to provide visibility into the cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and network performance issues that evade their existing security and IT tools. With this insight, organizations can investigate smarter, stop threats faster, and keep operations running.

Our mission is fueled by a profound social and moral responsibility to be the best at what we do, ensuring a secure world where everyone can thrive. If this sounds like a place you’d like to spend the next chapter of your career, we’d love to hear from you.

Position Summary

As a Software Engineer III, you will drive key architectural and technical decisions, lead the design and execution of complex engineering initiatives, and elevate technical standards across the Framework team. You’ll partner closely with principal engineers, product leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver resilient, scalable, and secure systems that power core ExtraHop products. This role is designed for an experienced engineer who combines deep technical expertise with strong ownership and is motivated to grow their impact through excellent engineering and active collaboration.

Our team builds high-performance network detection and monitoring systems that operate at scale across increasingly complex protocols and data volumes.Our services and features are written primarily in C and C++ with a focus on security, scalability, stability, and reliability. Our team is focussed on enhancing, maintaining and optimizing core components of the system and functional areas related to protocol parsing, metrics publishing, continuous packet capture and Time Series DB.

This role focuses on designing and optimizing these core systems with an emphasis on performance, reliability and deep protocol awareness. You will work on next generation initiatives including scaling and performance improvement efforts, evolution of our data storage architecture (custom to open-source based) and early steps towards a cloud enabled model.

Key Responsibilities

- Design, develop, and maintain high-performance services for ExtraHop's core Framework systems, taking ownership of moderately complex to complex features with limited guidance.

- Work across networking layers to implement and enhance protocol support

- Participate actively in technical design discussions, contribute to architecture decisions within your team, and author clear technical documentation for your work.

- Engage fully in agile development processes, including sprint planning, code reviews, and retrospectives; hold a high bar for code quality and test coverage.

- Collaborate with Product and cross-functional engineering partners such as platform , infrastructure and cloud teams to to define technical roadmaps, break down ambiguous problems, and balance technical debt with delivery.

- Investigate, diagnose, and resolve production and performance issues independently; conduct root-cause analysis and implement preventive measures.

- Contribute to platform modernization efforts and help evaluate and adopt new technologies or frameworks in partnership with senior and principal engineers.

- Participate in on-call rotations and improve system observability, reliability and operational readiness.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in STEM field, Computer Science, Engineering, or related degree requiring systematic/analytical thinking

- 4+ years of professional software engineering experience designing, building, and operating production systems at scale

- Strong expertise in C and C++

- Experience developing on Linux Systems (multi threading, memory management, IPC etc)

- Proven ability to build and maintain performance critical systems.

- Proven ability to debug complex issues (eg. using gdb, coredumps, performance tools)

- Strong understanding of networking fundamentals

- Strong command of data structures, algorithms, and software design principles, with the ability to decompose complex problems into clear, actionable engineering tasks.

- Self-starter who can operate independently, manage competing priorities, and drive work to completion with minimal oversight.

- Excellent collaborator and communicator with a growth mindset and customer-first orientation.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

- Experience with network protocols (eg. HTTP, SMB, Kerberos, TLS, Microsoft protocols or similar)

- Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS preferred) or distributed systems

- Experience with observability, on-call practices and production systems

- Scripting experience (Python or similar)

ABOUT EXTRAHOP

ExtraHop is reinventing Network Detection and Response (NDR) to offer enterprises unparalleled visibility, context, and control against emerging threats. The platform integrates NDR with Network Performance Management (NPM), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and forensics, providing a single, comprehensive solution. By decrypting and analyzing complete packet-level data at wire speed and leveraging cloud-scale machine learning, ExtraHop empowers Security Operations Centers (SOCs) to detect, investigate, and remediate modern cyber risks in real time across their entire hybrid infrastructure, including data center, cloud, and SASE environments.

Our mission is to unlock the world's generosity potential by optimizing how people give.

About the Role

AI is only as good as the data underneath it. This role makes ours trustworthy.

As our Head of Data, you'll build and guarantee the data foundation the whole company builds on: the pipelines, the models, the definitions, and the contracts that let people and AI agents trust what they're looking at. You'll report to our CFO, which keeps you neutral to any single function and close to how the business actually runs and measures itself. This is a player-coach seat. You'll write code and do the hardest technical work yourself, ship a major internal AI-powered initiative every quarter alongside our AI Transformation team, and grow this into a full function as it proves its value.

Key Responsibilities

- Own the data infrastructure, hands-on. Design, build, and run the pipelines and ETL/ELT that feed our warehouse. Own freshness, reliability, and cost. Treat the infrastructure as never finished, and keep making measurable gains in coverage, latency, and reliability.

- Build the trusted data layer everyone relies on. Own the data models, tests, validation, observability, and lineage that prove the data is accurate, plus the consistent metrics that give two teams the same answer to the same question. Make it self-serve and document it well enough that PMs, analysts, internal builders, and AI agents can answer their own questions.

- Own the definitions library. Teams own their definitions; you give them a single standardized, versioned home.

- Set the data contracts for internal AI and programmatic access, including MCP. Decide which data and actions AI agents and internal builders can reach, on what terms, with what semantics, and with what freshness and correctness guarantees. You own the requirements; Engineering builds and runs the servers and APIs.

- Be the source of truth for business and finance data. What Finance closes on, what Sales forecasts against, and what Product measures should all trace back to the same underlying data.

- Be the dependable upstream for Product Analytics, Product ML, and AI builders across the company. Work with them on their roadmaps so the foundation stays ahead of what they need. They own their products; you speed them up.

- Lead as a player-coach. Set the technical bar and review the work of a two-person team, then grow the team and the function as demand and trust build.

- Ship one major internal AI-powered initiative every quarter. Judge which ideas justify the build, then get them into production.

- At Fundraise Up, AI is a default tool, not an experimental one. We expect every team member to actively use AI in their day-to-day work, identify where AI can change the shape of problems in their function, and grow their fluency as the tools evolve.

Skills and Qualifications

- You've personally built and run production pipelines/ELT into a cloud data warehouse. You have strong SQL and Python, orchestration, and warehouse modeling skills, and you still want to be hands-on.

- You've built a trusted, self-serve data layer that people actually relied on: tests, observability, lineage, a metrics or semantic layer, and documentation good enough that questions stopped routing back to you.

- You've defined the contract between a data platform and the systems that consume it programmatically (schemas, semantics, guarantees, scoped access), and you held engineering partners to it.

- You've shipped AI/ML to production, not just prototypes, and you can tell which ideas are worth building.

- You've been the dependable data provider for analytics and ML teams, and you've reconciled revenue, finance, and GTM data so leadership worked from one set of numbers.

- You've built or scaled a data capability from a small base as its founding technical leader.

- You can explain a modeling decision to non-technical executives in terms of what it means for the business, without jargon or condescension.

Nice to Have

- Deeper LLM/agentic experience: orchestration frameworks, evals, RAG

- Hands-on experience building MCP servers or internal APIs

- Analytics engineering (dbt) and BI enablement

- Salesforce and GTM systems data

- Payments, fintech, or nonprofit-sector exposure

You'll Thrive Here If You…

- Would rather be the person who debugs the broken pipeline than the person who asks who owns it.

- Measure your success by how rarely people have to double-check the numbers.

- Want teams to build their own dashboards and AI tools, and see your job as making that safe rather than doing it for them.

- Think no piece of infrastructure is ever finished and keep looking for the next measurable improvement.

- Push back candidly when a definition is fuzzy or a request would break trust in the data, and then help fix it.

title: Senior Director, Mortgage Forecasting & Analytics
description:
Playing an essential role in the U.S. economy, Fannie Mae is foundational to housing finance. Here, your expertise can help fuel purpose-driven innovation that expands access to homeownership and affordable rental housing across the country. Join Fannie Mae to grow your career and help people find a place to call home.

Job Description

In this Senior Director position, you will lead the development of Finance’s forecasts and analytical assessments for mortgage related trading and portfolio strategies. The role will evaluate expected performance across agency MBS, structured mortgage products, and performing and non performing mortgage loans; assess how results may change under different market and macroeconomic environments; and provide an informed Finance perspective on the assumptions and expected outcomes of existing and proposed strategies.

The position will report to the Vice President and Capital Markets CFO and will lead a dedicated mortgage forecasting and analytics team. The role will work closely with the Capital Markets CFO teams responsible for corporate liquidity forecasting and analysis, hedge accounting, and broader GAAP profit and loss reporting, as well as with the trading desk, portfolio management, risk, modeling, accounting, and other Finance partners.

THE IMPACT YOU WILL MAKE

The Senior Director, Mortgage Forecasting & Analytics role will offer you the flexibility to make each day your own, while working alongside people who care so that you can deliver on the following responsibilities:

Develop Mortgage Strategy Forecasts and Scenario Analyses

- Lead the preparation and ongoing enhancement of forecasts for the expected financial and economic performance of mortgage trading and portfolio strategies.
- Forecast income, returns, cash flows, market value changes, financing costs, credit performance, and other relevant performance measures for existing mortgage positions and strategies.
- Analyze how expected performance changes under different interest rate, yield curve, spread, volatility, housing, liquidity, prepayment, delinquency, default, and loss severity assumptions.
- Evaluate the expected behavior of agency MBS, TBAs, specified pools, structured mortgage securities, credit risk transfer instruments, and whole mortgage loans.
- Produce base case and alternative scenario views that highlight key assumptions, sensitivities, risks, and potential ranges of outcomes.
- Perform forecast to actual and period over period analyses and identify the primary reasons actual performance differed from expectations.

Provide Finance Analysis and Challenge of Mortgage Assumptions

- Develop Finance’s perspective on the assumptions used to forecast and evaluate mortgage strategies.
- Review and challenge assumptions used by the trading desk and other business partners, including prepayment speeds, refinancing behavior, turnover, buyouts, defaults, recoveries, loss severity, spreads, volatility, financing costs, and hedge performance.
- Compare outputs and assumptions across Finance, trading, risk, valuation, accounting, and modeling teams and identify the primary drivers of differences.
- Facilitate discussions with the trading desk and other stakeholders to evaluate alternative assumptions and determine the most appropriate inputs for Finance forecasting.
- Document key assumptions, judgments, uncertainties, and changes in outlook for use in management reporting and forecast governance.

Assess New and Evolving Mortgage Portfolio Strategies

- Evaluate the expected financial contribution and portfolio implications of proposed trades, investments, structures, and strategy changes.
- Assess the expected return, earnings profile, cash flow characteristics, funding requirements, market sensitivity, credit exposure, and downside risk of proposed strategies.
- Evaluate how new strategies may complement or detract from the existing mortgage portfolio, including their effects on diversification, concentration, optionality, convexity, basis risk, liquidity, and tail exposure.
- Analyze complex transactions at the collateral, security, tranche, strategy, and portfolio levels.
- Prepare clear Finance assessments that compare proposed strategies with existing positions and alternative uses of balance sheet, liquidity, or risk capacity.

Partner with P&L Teams to Evaluate and Explain Mortgage Performance

- Partner with P&L teams across both Finance and Capital Markets to evaluate and explain mortgage performance and its key economic drivers.
- Assist in measuring mortgage strategy performance using relevant economic and financial metrics, such as income, total return, carry, spread performance, realized and unrealized gains or losses, financing costs, and risk adjusted return, while challenging the underlying analysis and assumptions.
- Perform forecast-to-actual and period-over-period analyses and identify the primary reasons actual performance differed from expectations.
- Partner with both the Capital Markets CFO organization and Capital Markets desk P&L teams to distinguish economic performance drivers from accounting classification, timing, and presentation effects and to ensure appropriate Finance and business interpretations of results.

Lead the Mortgage Forecasting and Analytics Team and Operating Framework

- Build and manage the team, processes, tools, data, and controls required to support mortgage forecasting and strategy analysis.
- Lead, develop, and prioritize the work of a team of mortgage analytics and Finance professionals.
- Establish repeatable forecasting, scenario analysis, performance measurement, review, documentation, and reporting processes.
- Partner with data, technology, modeling, risk, and Finance teams to improve analytical tools, data quality, automation, controls, and reporting efficiency.
- Coordinate with the corporate liquidity forecasting, hedge accounting, and Capital Markets P&L teams to ensure mortgage assumptions and analyses are appropriately reflected across related Finance processes.

THE EXPERIENCE YOU BRING TO THE TEAM

Minimum Required Experiences:

- 8 or more years of experience in mortgage finance, fixed income or mortgage analytics, capital markets Finance, portfolio analysis, risk management, valuation, financial planning and analysis, trading support, or a related field.
- Strong knowledge of agency mortgage backed securities, including TBAs, specified pools, passthrough securities, CMOs, embedded prepayment optionality, and structured mortgage products.
- Experience developing financial forecasts, scenario analyses, cash flow projections, performance attribution, and sensitivity analyses for mortgage or other complex fixed income portfolios.
- Working knowledge of mortgage cash flow modeling, duration, convexity, spread and basis risk, option adjusted analysis, financing economics, and hedge performance.
- Experience leading or supervising analytical professionals and the ability to work effectively with trading, portfolio management, risk, modeling, accounting, liquidity, and senior Finance stakeholders.
- Strong ability to evaluate and challenge assumptions, synthesize complex or conflicting analyses, exercise sound judgment, and communicate conclusions clearly to both technical and senior management audiences.
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field required.
- Shows curiosity and adaptability in learning and responsibly applying new technologies, including artificial intelligence, to reimagine how we work.

Desired Experiences:

- Understanding of performing and non performing residential mortgage loans, including prepayments, delinquencies, defaults, modifications, cures, liquidations, recoveries, and loss severity.
- Experience with mortgage analytics platforms, large datasets, SQL, Python, or other quantitative analytical tools.
- CFA designation, FRM certification, or advanced degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
- Experience with credit risk transfer securities, non agency RMBS, mortgage derivatives, or other structured credit products.

title: Associate AI Data Strategist

title: Digital Member Experience Manager
description:
WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

The Recording Academy’s mission is to recognize musical excellence, advocate for the well-being of music makers and ensure music remains an indelible part of our culture. The Academy is a professional membership organization of musicians, producers, engineers, and recording professionals. Our Membership & Industry Relations team delivers services across a national network of 12 Chapters who each serve local music communities.

We're looking for a highly motivated, idea-generating professional to serve as the central execution and delivery lead for member-facing digital campaigns, content, and touchpoints, both nationally and across our chapter markets. Reporting to the Director, Member Experience, the Digital Member Experience Manager operationalizes the broader Member Experience strategy across content, campaigns, and digital touchpoints throughout the member ecosystem, and plays a key part in marketing high-impact programs and member-wide initiatives. You will work closely with Lifecycle Marketing (which owns audience segmentation and marketing automation strategy) and coordinate cross-functionally with Digital Experience, IT, Creative Services, and Chapter teams to ensure cohesive execution of member-facing campaigns and communications.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Execute and support membership engagement initiatives across national and chapter-specific programming, awards, advocacy, education, partnerships, and marketing campaigns, including content development, email communications, and updates to GRAMMY.com and other digital platforms.
- Develop and execute copy for member-facing campaigns, translating awards process information, program goals, and promotional priorities into clear, engaging content across email, web, app, and event platforms, aligned with brand voice and communications standards.
- Partner with Chapter teams and internal stakeholders to gather inputs, including event materials submitted via ticket (text, images, info), and shape messaging for member programs, events, and initiatives.
- Manage and update public-facing membership pages and member-related content in the GRAMMY app and member portal, including chapter programming, awards, promotional messaging, and key communications.
- Manage the department's use of event and digital platforms (e.g., Blackthorn registration, web CMS, and related tools), reviewing chapter event builds through a marketing and brand lens to confirm messaging alignment and ensure timely, accurate publication (technical build and system integrations remain owned by IT).
- Partner with the Member Experience data lead to ensure chapter events are integrated and surfaced on the Member Portal, including input on which events are highlighted.
- Develop and maintain standardized, reusable event templates chapters can adapt for their own builds, and help establish turnaround-time expectations for chapter event requests, including guidance for high-volume periods.
- Coordinate execution across email, web, app, and event platforms, serving as a quality control checkpoint to ensure accuracy, clarity, and a cohesive member experience.
- Support rollout and ongoing management of member community platforms (e.g., Slack), including hands-on moderation during beta phases and establishing engagement standards and best practices for long-term growth.
- Support post-event evaluation, including reporting, stakeholder summaries, and data analysis, and ensure post-event communications are executed across appropriate channels.
- Maintain advanced knowledge base of the Grammy awards calendar, criteria, and processes to ensure effective and clear communication around the Recording Academy’s marquee event.
- Develop and maintain clear systems for member communication that have the ability to scale to meet the Academy’s global membership goals.
- Ensure all execution aligns with established Member Experience standards, direction, and priorities.

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

- Bachelor’s Degree preferred.
- 4+ years of digital marketing, event production/management, and customer service experience, preferrably in entertainment or media.
- Previous experience and connections in music business, music production or music education preferred.
- Knowledge of event and marketing platforms such as Blackthorn, Swoogo or similar tools (reviewing builds for brand and messaging alignment, not configuring technical integrations), and familiarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud or comparable CRM platforms.
- Strong copywriting and content development skills with the ability to translate defined priorities into clear, engaging member-facing messaging.
- Strong understanding of brand voice, messaging consistency, and content standards with the ability to apply them across channels.
- Experience managing website content using content management systems (CMS), such as WordPress or similar platforms.
- Experience executing campaigns across multiple digital channels, including email, web, app, and event platforms.
- Familiarity with community platforms such as Slack, Discord, or similar tools preferred including basic moderation and community engagement best practices preferred.
- Comfort working across multiple digital platforms and tools, with the ability to learn new systems quickly and support evolving workflows.
- Experience working cross-functionally with marketing, creative, digital, and program teams to deliver coordinated campaigns and initiatives.
- Basic understanding of campaign performance metrics, with the ability to interpret insights and apply learnings to improve execution.
- Proficiency in digital tools including Zoom, Canva, Adobe, and Microsoft applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Ability to communicate ideas clearly with excellent interpersonal skills.
- Must be proactive and highly organized with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to work under pressure of tight deadlines with strong organizational and decision-making skills.

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States.

À certains stades de notre processus de recrutement, nous comptons sur l’IA pour améliorer votre expérience. Bien que l’IA facilite certaines étapes de notre processus de recrutement, les décisions finales d’embauche sont toujours prises par des personnes. title: Senior Health Economics & Outcomes Research Analyst
description:

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life
Peripheral Vascular Health (PVH) is a dynamic business with annual revenue exceeding $1 billion across multiple high-growth therapy areas. PVH focuses on diagnosing and treating diseases of the peripheral arteries and veins, helping patients restore blood flow and reduce the risk of limb loss and other serious complications. The portfolio includes minimally invasive technologies such as drug-coated balloons, stents, atherectomy, thrombectomy, embolization, vein ablation, and embolic protection, designed to address complex peripheral vascular disease across a range of patient anatomies. By combining innovation, clinical evidence, and physician partnership, PVH aims to improve procedural outcomes and quality of life for patients worldwide.

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. This position is remote to enhance our competitive edge and expand our cross-functional collaboration efforts. This role will require 10% of travel to enhance collaboration and ensure successful completion of projects.

The Senior Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Analyst will be a critical contributor on the Cardiovascular HEOR team. The Senior HEOR Analyst is responsible for providing analytical and methodological expertise to support the development and execution of global health economic and outcomes evidence for Cardiovascular products, with an emphasis on the Peripheral Vascular Health portfolio. This position may be called upon to support multiple therapies, with a specific focus area on leading the execution of studies using administrative data to generate regulatory-grade evidence.

Role and Responsibilities:

- Designs and conducts studies using administrative health care claims data and device-derived data to assess outcomes, health services utilization, treatment patterns and costs associated with the use of PVH therapies. Analysis may be used to support evidence development, federal and global agency (FDA, CMS, EU MDD/MDR) requests, clinical trial design, and reimbursement market trends.
- Designs and conducts observational and economic research studies that provide value, perspective and evidence for clinical and/or pre-clinical product portfolio decisions, marketing, regulatory agency submissions, and product reimbursement strategies.
- Compares and evaluates the value of products and therapies with the clinical, economic, and quality of life outcomes data from clinical trials and/or epidemiology studies, registries, observational studies, modeling, surveys, and meta-analysis.
- Prepare observational and economic research study results for dissemination via abstract, presentation, and/or peer-reviewed publication.
- Develops country specific evidence to meet requirements for optimal reimbursement coverage and usage.
- Works closely with Reimbursement staff to determine the global economic evidence needs and potential impact of evidence on therapy coverage, payment, and adoption.
- Works with clinical research to add relevant health outcomes and economic endpoints to clinical trials and biostatisticians to analyze and report study results.

Must Have; Minimum Requirements

- Baccalaureate degree
- Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in healthcare industry working with health care data (medical device, pharmaceutical, biotech, insurance, hospital, health system) or advanced degree and 2 years of post-graduate experience in healthcare industry working with health care data (medical device, pharmaceutical, biotech, insurance, hospital, health system) preferred

Nice To Have

- Advanced degree in health policy, health services research, health economics, epidemiology, or related field of study
- Experience working with administrative claims data
- Experience designing, modifying, or implementing decision analysis models (i.e., cost-effectiveness, budget impact)

- Experience working with large databases including health care claims, administrative, or patient discharge data as a health service researcher, epidemiologist, data programmer or economist
- Proficiency programming using statistical software (e.g. SAS, STATA, R, etc.)
- Demonstrated competency in database file manipulation, data analysis and graphical presentation
- Strong quantitative skills, preferably with training in econometrics or statistics
- An understanding of health insurance and the U.S. health care system
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, especially the ability to communicate complex analytical techniques in a way that is understandable by non-quantitative audiences
- Experience in the development of regulatory-grade analysis, synthesis, and presentation of complex data from multiple sources
- Project management experience; demonstrated consultative mindset
- Proven ability to work effectively in a highly matrixed organization
- Proven relationship-building and maintaining skills with internal and external stakeholders including physician customers, hospital administrators or payers

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

title: Senior Program Officer, Software & AI
description:
The Foundation

We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

The Team
The Gender Equality Division’s mission is to ensure women and girls in Africa and South Asia can enjoy good health, make their own choices, earn their own money, and be leaders in their societies. When women and girls have an equal chance to thrive and lead, everyone benefits. We know that women and girls are not a monolith. A woman’s experience and the barriers she faces are different depending on factors like where she lives, how old she is, and how much money her family has, alongside other factors including her race, caste, and education level. We seek to address these compounding barriers through deep partnership with our grantees. As a philanthropy, our role is to listen to and learn from these experts. We take risks in new areas, prove concepts, and bring these ideas to governments, partner organizations, and private sector companies to scale. The Gender Equality Division builds off our existing strengths as a foundation in areas like global health and data, partnering closely with all our global divisions.

The Maternal, Newborn, Child Nutrition & Health (MNCNH) team works to eliminate preventable mortality and morbidity among women, newborns, and children in low-resource settings. We do this by funding and accelerating a portfolio of high-impact products targeted at the moments of greatest biological vulnerability across the life-course. Our portfolio addresses pregnancy risk, maternal undernutrition, prematurity, neonatal encephalopathy, child wasting, neurodevelopment, and maternal morbidity through drugs, foods, microbes, devices, risk algorithms, and increasingly through AI and connected device technologies that extend the reach of these interventions where health systems are weakest. The portfolio spans the full development continuum from early discovery through implementation research and country introduction. A multidisciplinary team of physician scientists, epidemiologists, engineers, nutritionists, and commercialization experts works alongside in-country partners to integrate local context into research, development, and scale.

Your Role

The Senior Program Officer (SPO), Software & AI, will serve as a technical and strategic lead for software, digital health, and AI-enabled products across the MNCNH portfolio. The role will help translate high-priority health use cases into products and platforms that are technically sound, user-centered, interoperable, and deployable in low-resource settings. The portfolio may include clinical decision support, risk-stratification tools, AI-enabled applications, digital workflows, software that connects to medical devices, and other data- and software-driven approaches that improve individual-level care and health-system performance. A flagship priority for this role is accelerating risk-stratification software layered on top of the foundation's AI-enabled hardware investments — spanning antenatal ultrasound, intrapartum monitoring, and postpartum/neonatal care — turning imaging and physiologic signal data into clinically actionable outputs. The SPO will hold grantmaking responsibility for a defined portfolio of investments and work closely with MNCNH technical leads, country teams, and partners to move promising concepts from prototype through validation, productization, integration, and scale.

While primarily anchored in MNCNH, this role will also serve as a shared technical resource for selected software and AI use cases across the broader Women’s Health portfolio. Success will require strong product and software-development judgment, fluency in rapidly evolving AI technologies — equally at ease with classical/deterministic modeling and generative AI methods, and able to judge which approach a given clinical use case actually calls for, and the ability to connect technical choices to real-world implementation constraints. The SPO will work across internal teams and with grantees, technology companies, software developers, researchers, implementing partners, governments, and other stakeholders to ensure that solutions are designed for local workflows, data environments, connectivity constraints, and sustainable country ownership.

What You’ll Do

• Lead and manage a portfolio of grants, contracts, and other investments focused on software, digital health, and AI-enabled products, from sourcing and diligence through structuring, execution, monitoring, and reporting.

• Translate MNCNH and selected broader Women’s Health priorities into clear software and AI product roadmaps, identifying the highest-value use cases, portfolio gaps, technical dependencies, and build-versus-partner decisions.

• Provide technical leadership across the software product lifecycle, including product requirements, user-centered design, architecture, software development, testing, deployment, maintenance, and product iteration.

• Guide the development and productization of AI-enabled tools, including clinical decision support, risk stratification, workflow automation, multimodal and generative AI applications, and software that connects to medical devices or other digital platforms.

• Define how imaging (e.g., ultrasound) and physiologic signal data (e.g., intrapartum and neonatal monitoring) pools are structured, labeled, and converted into validated, productized software outputs, partnering with the foundation's data team on shared standards and infrastructure.

• Assess technical architecture and integration requirements, including APIs, interoperability, data flows, identity and access, cloud/edge/local deployment, offline and low-bandwidth operation, and integration with existing health information systems and digital public infrastructure.

• Partner with grantees, developers, researchers, country stakeholders, and implementation partners, working closely with other Program Officers across the hardware and clinical portfolio and the foundation's data team, to ensure products are designed around frontline workflows and can move from prototype or pilot to reliable, maintainable, scalable use, including at regional deployment and pilot sites.

• Apply strong judgment on responsible AI, data governance, privacy, security, clinical safety, model performance, and human oversight, and establish clear evidence and decision criteria for when products are ready to advance, scale, pause, or stop.

• Stay closely connected to the evolving software and AI ecosystem, including emerging models, platforms, vendors, and technical approaches, and translate relevant developments into practical implications for the portfolio.

• Contribute to budgeting, risk management, and sequencing of investments, with clear milestones, decision points, technical deliverables, and outcomes that support effective stewardship of foundation resources.

• Track and communicate portfolio progress and translate complex technical, product, implementation, and market evidence into clear recommendations for team and foundation leadership.

• Foster coordination across MNCNH, Women’s Health, country teams, and relevant foundation-wide digital and AI teams so that use cases build on shared capabilities rather than creating duplicative or disconnected solutions.

• Build and sustain an external ecosystem of software developers, AI companies, researchers, digital-health experts, implementers, governments, and other partners needed to advance affordable and scalable solutions for low- and middle-income countries.

• Represent the Foundation externally, including at technical and industry meetings, partner convenings, advisory groups, and engagements with governments, technology companies, and implementing organizations.

Your Experience

• Advanced degree in computer science, software engineering, data science, biomedical informatics, engineering, medicine, public health, or another relevant technical or clinical discipline.

• Minimum 10 years of relevant experience developing, launching, and scaling software, digital-health, data, or AI-enabled products; experience with health or other high-stakes applications is strongly preferred.

• Deep technical and product knowledge in several of the following areas: software architecture, APIs and interoperability, mobile or web applications, cloud and edge computing, data platforms, artificial intelligence/machine learning, generative AI, clinical decision support, risk stratification, or software as a medical device.

• Demonstrated fluency in both classical/deterministic modeling (e.g., clinical risk scores, statistical and rules-based methods) and generative AI approaches, with sound judgment about which fits a given clinical use case. Experience working with imaging (e.g., ultrasound) and/or physiologic signal data (e.g., intrapartum or neonatal monitoring), and experience in a regulated medical device (SaMD) context, is strongly preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to translate user and program needs into product requirements and technical roadmaps, and to work effectively with engineering teams from early prototype through deployment and iteration.

• Strong understanding of responsible AI, data governance, privacy, security, model evaluation, clinical safety, and the evidence needed to support adoption and scale of software-enabled health products.

• Experience designing or deploying products in constrained environments, including low-connectivity settings, fragmented data ecosystems, limited device access, or complex government and health-system workflows.

• Demonstrated ability to set strategy, make portfolio and investment decisions, and manage complex programs with clear milestones, budgets, risk mitigation, and outcomes.

• Strong external network and demonstrated ability to stay current in a rapidly evolving technology landscape and distinguish durable capabilities from short-lived trends or vendor-specific solutions.

• Experience working across traditional disciplinary boundaries and with senior leaders, software engineers, data scientists, clinicians, researchers, governments, technology companies, and implementation partners.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences and build alignment across a highly matrixed environment.

• Proven ability to build and manage multi-stakeholder partnerships across technology, academia, industry, governments, and implementing organizations.

• Global health experience is strongly preferred; experience developing and deploying software or AI-enabled products in low- and middle-income countries and/or women’s, maternal, newborn, and child health is ideal.

• Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 30% of the time.

title: Research Scientist, Post-Training
description:
About the Company

Models are what they eat. But a large portion of training compute is wasted training on data that are already learned, irrelevant, or even harmful, leading to worse models that cost more to train and deploy.

At DatologyAI, we’ve built a state of the art data curation suite to automatically curate and optimize petabytes of data to create the best possible training data for your models. Training on curated data can dramatically reduce training time and cost (7-40x faster training depending on the use case), dramatically increase model performance as if you had trained on >10x more raw data without increasing the cost of training, and allow smaller models with fewer than half the parameters to outperform larger models despite using far less compute at inference time, substantially reducing the cost of deployment. For more details, check out our recent research on synthetic data scaling (BeyondWeb) and pretraining with domain-specific data (The Finetuner’s Fallacy).

We raised a total of $57.5M in two rounds, a Seed and Series A. Our investors include Felicis Ventures, Radical Ventures, Amplify Partners, Microsoft, Amazon, and AI visionaries like Geoff Hinton, Yann LeCun, Jeff Dean, and many others who deeply understand the importance and difficulty of identifying and optimizing the best possible training data for models. Our team has pioneered this frontier research area and has the deep expertise on both data research and data engineering necessary to solve this incredibly challenging problem and make data curation easy for anyone who wants to train their own model on their own data.

This role is based in San Mateo, CA. We are in office 4 days a week.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Research Scientist to lead work on post-training data curation for foundation models. You’ll design and implement algorithms to generate and improve instruction, preference, and other post-training datasets. You’ll also help bridge the gap between pre-training and post-training by exploring how to jointly optimize data across stages. This role requires strong scientific judgment, fluency with the deep learning literature, and a drive to turn research ideas into real-world impact. You’ll work autonomously, collaborate closely with engineers and product teams, and shape the future of data curation at DatologyAI.

What You'll Work On

-
Post-training data curation. You’ll conduct research on how to algorithmically curate post-training data—e.g., how to generate and refine preference and instruction-following data, how to curate capability- and domain-specific data, and make post-training more effective, controllable, and generalizable.

-
Unifying pre-training and post-training data curation. Pushing the bounds on model capabilities requires unifying post-training and pre-training data curation. You will pursue research on end-to-end data curation: how to curate pre-training data to improve the post-trainability of models and how to jointly optimize pre- and post-training data curation, all in service of maximizing the final performance of post-trained models.

-
Transform messy literature into practical improvements. The research literature is vast, rife with ambiguity, and constantly evolving. You will use your skills as a scientist to source, vet, implement, and improve promising ideas from the literature and of your own creation.

-
Conduct science driven by real-world needs. At DatologyAI, we understand that conference reviewers and academic benchmarks don’t always incentivize the most impactful research. Your research will be guided by concrete customer needs and product improvements.

How You'll Work

-
Nobody knows how to do your work better than you. We believe that scientists do their best work when they have the autonomy to pursue problems in the manner they prefer, and we will ensure that you are equipped with the context and resources you need to succeed.

-
Science is more than just experiments. We expect our Research Scientists to collaborate closely with engineers, talk to customers, and shape the product vision.

About You

-
3+ years of deep learning research experience

-
Experience with post-training large vision, language, and multimodal models

-
Post-training algorithm development, data curation, and/or synthetic data methods for:

-
Preference-based tuning (e.g. DPO, RLVR, RRHF)

-
Alternative supervision & self-supervision techniques such as self-training and chain-of-thought distillation

-
SFT (e.g. instruction tuning and demonstration fine-tuning)

-
Post-training tooling development and engineering experience

-
Strong understanding of the fundamentals of deep learning

-
Sufficient software engineering + deep learning framework (PyTorch or a willingness to learn PyTorch) skills to conduct large-scale research experiments and build production prototypes.

-
Demonstrated track record of success in deep learning research, whether papers, tools, or other research artifacts.

Nice to have

-
Experience with data management and distributed data processing solutions (e.g. Spark, Snowflake, etc.)

-
Experience building + shipping ML products

Candidates do not need a PhD or extensive publications. Some of the best researchers we’ve worked with have no formal training in machine learning, and obtained all of their experience by working in industry and building products. We believe that adaptability, combined with exceptional communication and collaboration skills are the most important ingredients for successful research in a startup environment.

Compensation

At DatologyAI, we are dedicated to rewarding talent with competitive salary and meaningful equity. The salary for this position ranges from $180,000 to $300,000.

-
Starting pay is based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, and interview performance.

Daily lunches and snacks are provided in our office!

title: Senior Product Manager, Growth
description:
About KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

About The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to join KOHO’s Growth team. You’ll lead a dedicated growth pod focused on one of our highest-leverage problems: either converting more registered users into active customers, or building product-led channels that acquire users through the product itself.

This is a metrics-driven role with clear ownership and real P&L impact. You’ll run experiments at high velocity, own a specific set of growth KPIs, and work within a cross-functional pod (engineering, design, data) to move them. You won’t be maintaining a feature backlog — you’ll be solving growth problems end-to-end.

What You’ll Be Doing

-
Own growth metrics with clear accountability. You’ll be responsible for specific KPIs tied to user acquisition or activation — metrics that directly impact KOHO’s revenue and unit economics.

-
Run experiments at high velocity. Design, ship, and iterate on growth initiatives weekly. Maintain a rolling experiment backlog with clear hypotheses and success criteria. Learn fast from failures.

-
Build business cases grounded in data. Use quantitative analysis, financial modeling, and CAC/LTV economics to prioritize bets and defend investment decisions to leadership.

-
Lead a cross-functional pod. Work with engineering, design, data, and marketing to ship growth initiatives. Align your team around a single mission and keep execution tight.

-
Identify and reduce friction across the user journey. Whether it’s funnel drop-offs, onboarding bottlenecks, or underperforming growth channels — diagnose root causes and ship solutions.

-
Design and scale growth loops. Think beyond linear funnels. Identify opportunities for compounding, product-led mechanics that reduce acquisition costs over time.

-
Collaborate across the growth org. Work closely with the other growth pod to ensure the full user journey — from first touch to active customer — works as a connected system.

-
Communicate strategy to leadership. Present growth strategy, experiment results, and roadmap decisions to executive audiences through quarterly strategy reviews.

Who You Are

-
3–5+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years focused on growth, activation, acquisition, or product-led growth at a consumer or fintech company.

-
Track record of moving growth metrics — whether that’s conversion funnels, referral programs, onboarding flows, or acquisition loops. We want to see specific numbers you’ve moved.

-
Deeply data-driven. You can write SQL when needed, design experiments with statistical rigor, and make decisions based on CAC/LTV modeling rather than intuition.

-
High experiment velocity. You’re comfortable shipping multiple experiments per sprint, learning quickly from failures, and iterating without over-engineering.

-
Cross-functional leader. You’ve led pods or squads (engineering, design, marketing, data) and know how to align a team around a single metric.

-
Strong strategic communicator. You can articulate growth strategy to executives, write compelling business cases, and translate data into narratives that drive alignment.

-
AI-native. You actively use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) in your daily work — for analysis, writing, research, and prototyping.

Nice to Have

-
Experience at a Canadian fintech or a regulated financial services company.

-
Familiarity with product analytics, martech, and BI tools — our core product and growth stack.

-
Experience with A/B testing platforms (Eppo, Optimizely, or similar) and experiment governance.

-
Background in behavioural economics, incentive design, or conversion optimization.

-
Experience with fintech onboarding and KYC optimization — reducing friction in regulated sign-up flows.

-
Experience building product-led acquisition at scale.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

Description de poste en français

À propos du poste

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) gestionnaire de produits principal(e) pour se joindre à l’équipe Croissance de KOHO. Vous dirigerez une cellule de croissance dédiée à l’un de nos enjeux à plus fort effet de levier : soit convertir davantage d’utilisateurs inscrits en clients actifs, soit bâtir des canaux axés sur le produit qui permettent d’acquérir des utilisateurs par l’entremise du produit lui-même.

Il s’agit d’un poste axé sur les indicateurs, assorti de responsabilités claires et d’une incidence réelle sur les résultats financiers. Vous mènerez des expérimentations à un rythme soutenu, serez responsable d’un ensemble précis d’indicateurs clés de croissance et travaillerez au sein d’une cellule interfonctionnelle (ingénierie, design, données) pour les faire progresser. Vous ne gérerez pas un carnet de fonctionnalités : vous résoudrez des problèmes de croissance de bout en bout.

Ce que vous ferez

-
Prendre en charge des indicateurs de croissance avec une responsabilité claire. Vous serez responsable d’indicateurs clés de performance précis liés à l’acquisition ou à l’activation des utilisateurs, des indicateurs qui ont une incidence directe sur les revenus et l’économie unitaire de KOHO.

-
Mener des expérimentations à un rythme soutenu. Concevoir, lancer et itérer des initiatives de croissance chaque semaine. Tenir à jour un carnet d’expérimentations continu, assorti d’hypothèses et de critères de réussite clairs. Tirer rapidement des leçons des échecs.

-
Élaborer des analyses de rentabilité fondées sur les données. Utiliser l’analyse quantitative, la modélisation financière et l’économie CAC/VVC (coût d’acquisition client et valeur vie client) pour prioriser les paris et défendre les décisions d’investissement auprès de la direction.

-
Diriger une cellule interfonctionnelle. Travailler avec les équipes d’ingénierie, de design, de données et de marketing pour lancer des initiatives de croissance. Rallier votre équipe autour d’une mission unique et assurer une exécution rigoureuse.

-
Cerner et réduire les points de friction tout au long du parcours utilisateur. Qu’il s’agisse d’abandons dans l’entonnoir, de goulots d’étranglement à l’intégration ou de canaux de croissance peu performants, diagnostiquer les causes profondes et mettre en œuvre des solutions.

-
Concevoir et déployer à grande échelle des boucles de croissance. Penser au-delà des entonnoirs linéaires. Repérer les occasions de mécanismes cumulatifs axés sur le produit qui réduisent les coûts d’acquisition au fil du temps.

-
Collaborer avec l’ensemble de l’organisation Croissance. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec l’autre cellule de croissance afin que l’ensemble du parcours utilisateur, du premier contact jusqu’au client actif, fonctionne comme un système intégré.

-
Communiquer la stratégie à la direction. Présenter la stratégie de croissance, les résultats des expérimentations et les décisions relatives à la feuille de route aux membres de la haute direction dans le cadre de revues stratégiques trimestrielles.

Votre profil

-
De 3 à 5 ans ou plus d’expérience en gestion de produits, dont au moins 2 ans axés sur la croissance, l’activation, l’acquisition ou la croissance axée sur le produit au sein d’une entreprise grand public ou de technologie financière (fintech).

-
Feuille de route démontrée en matière d’amélioration des indicateurs de croissance, qu’il s’agisse d’entonnoirs de conversion, de programmes de recommandation, de parcours d’intégration ou de boucles d’acquisition. Nous voulons connaître les chiffres précis que vous avez fait progresser.

-
Approche résolument axée sur les données. Vous savez écrire des requêtes SQL au besoin, concevoir des expérimentations avec rigueur statistique et prendre des décisions fondées sur la modélisation CAC/VVC plutôt que sur l’intuition.

-
Rythme d’expérimentation élevé. Vous êtes à l’aise de lancer plusieurs expérimentations par sprint, de tirer rapidement des leçons des échecs et d’itérer sans complexifier inutilement.

-
Leader interfonctionnel(le). Vous avez dirigé des cellules ou des équipes (ingénierie, design, marketing, données) et savez rallier une équipe autour d’un indicateur unique.

-
Communicateur(trice) stratégique hors pair. Vous savez exposer une stratégie de croissance à la haute direction, rédiger des analyses de rentabilité convaincantes et traduire les données en récits qui favorisent l’adhésion.

-
Adepte de l’IA. Vous utilisez activement des outils d’IA (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) dans votre travail quotidien, que ce soit pour l’analyse, la rédaction, la recherche ou le prototypage.

Atouts

-
Expérience au sein d’une entreprise canadienne de technologie financière ou d’une société de services financiers réglementée.

-
Connaissance des outils d’analyse de produits, de technologie marketing (martech) et d’informatique décisionnelle (BI), qui forment le cœur de notre pile technologique produit et croissance.

-
Expérience des plateformes de tests A/B (Eppo, Optimizely ou autres) et de la gouvernance des expérimentations.

-
Formation en économie comportementale, en conception de mesures incitatives ou en optimisation de la conversion.

-
Expérience de l’intégration des clients en technologie financière et de l’optimisation des processus de vérification d’identité (KYC), afin de réduire la friction dans les parcours d’inscription réglementés.

-
Expérience dans la mise en place d’une acquisition axée sur le produit à grande échelle.

Rémunération

L’échelle salariale prévue pour ce poste se situe entre 160 000 $ et 200 000 $ CA par année.

Chez KOHO, nous nous engageons à offrir une transparence salariale à tous les candidats. La rémunération est déterminée en fonction de plusieurs facteurs, notamment les données comparatives du marché canadien, l’évaluation des compétences techniques, l’expérience professionnelle globale du candidat ainsi que l’équité salariale interne au sein de l’équipe KOHO.

KOHO is for builders.

If you’re energized by challenge, motivated by mission, and want to be part of a team that punches above its weight - we want to hear from you.

The KOHO culture is one of collaboration, creativity, and diverse perspectives. We are committed to building and fostering an inclusive, accessible environment for everyone. If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding accessibility needs, please contact [email removed] and the People and Culture team will be happy to help.
