title: Staff Product Manager, Moderation
description:
Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com.

What You'll Do:

Reddit is a community of communities, built around the conversations, interests, and experiences people share with one another. Moderators are the heart of that ecosystem: they shape community norms, keep spaces healthy, and help communities grow.

As Reddit continues to scale globally, this role will help define how we support moderators, reduce the burden of running healthy communities, and evolve moderation from reactive manual work into proactive, intelligent systems.

We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to help define the future of moderation on Reddit. This is a rare opportunity to lead zero-to-one product work at the intersection of user-facing experience, community governance, and cutting-edge LLM systems. You will help Reddit move beyond legacy moderation approaches toward proactive, intelligent, and scalable community enforcement.

This role is for a PM with exceptional product judgment, strong user intuition, and enough AI/ML depth to partner closely with Engineering, Data Science, Design, and Safety. The right person can shape compelling user experiences, reason about model quality and tradeoffs, and create clarity in a high-stakes, high-visibility space where the product, technical, and ecosystem decisions all matter.

Responsibilities

- Identify Reddit’s highest-impact opportunities to evolve evolve community enforcement and moderator workflows, and turn them into a clear product strategy and roadmap.

- Lead zero-to-one development of LLM-powered moderation experiences that are critical to how Reddit scales healthy communities globally.

- Build a deep understanding of moderators, community members, and healthy community dynamics, and translate those insights into high-quality product experiences.

- Define success metrics and model/product evaluation criteria that connect user value, community health, and Reddit’s broader strategy.

- Reason about AI/ML quality, including precision, recall, error costs, coverage, latency, failure modes, human review, and feedback loops.

- Assess high-stakes ecosystem tradeoffs across community health, moderator trust, user trust, safety, and product quality.

- Partner with Engineering, Data Science/ML, Design, Safety, Consumer, and senior leaders to drive execution in a highly visible company priority.

- Communicate strategy, decisions, tradeoffs, and learning clearly to executive stakeholders.

Must Haves:

- Staff-level product experience owning meaningful consumer surfaces or systems with measurable user impact.

- Exceptional product sense across user intuition, problem framing, prioritization, UX judgment, and product taste.

- Track record leading ambiguous zero-to-one or major product-evolution work from strategy through launch and learning.

- Experience building AI/ML-powered products, with fluency in model evaluation and product/model tradeoffs.

- Strong analytical judgment, including defining metrics, interpreting evidence, and changing direction when needed.

- Excellent cross-functional leadership with Engineering, Data Science/ML, Design, Safety, and partner teams in ambiguous, technically complex spaces.

Nice-to-Haves:

- Experience with community, social, creator, UGC, trust/safety, or moderation products.

- Experience with ML-heavy consumer surfaces or policy-sensitive AI experiences.

- Experience replacing mature systems with a new product paradigm in complex, matrixed organizations.

Benefits:

- 401k with Employer Match

- Global Benefit programs that fit your lifestyle, from workspace to professional development to caregiving support

- Family Planning Support

- Gender-Affirming Care

- Mental Health & Coaching Benefits

- Flexible Vacation & Paid Volunteer Time Off

- Generous Paid Parental Leave

In addition to base salary, this job is eligible to receive equity in the form of restricted stock units, and depending on the position offered, it may also be eligible to receive a commission. Additionally, Reddit offers a wide range of benefits to U.S.-based employees, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) program with employer match, generous time off for vacation, and parental leave. title: Technical Account Manager
description:
About the role

The TAM is Sift's technical product expertise pushed out to the edge, embedded with the customer rather than sitting back in engineering. You're the person who knows the product deeply enough to catch what's about to go wrong in someone's actual environment. We serve as the named, persistent technical partner for Sift's strategic and premium accounts, working in close lockstep with Customer Success so customers get one seamless, aligned strategy rather than a handoff between silos. We connect across Customer Success, Support, Customer Engineering, Trust & Safety Advisory (TASA), Managed Operations, and Product/Engineering to keep every account's technical health ahead of the next escalation.

Operating primarily as a technical diagnostician rather than a builder or purely relationship owner, you excel at reading workflows, analyzing labeling practices, observing score behavior, and catching drift before it becomes an escalation.

You'll build deep, lasting familiarity with each customer's implementation, architecture, workflows, labeling practices, signals, and roadmap, calling out patterns drawn from other customer engagements and your technical expertise. Working in close partnership with Customer Success Managers (CSMs), you translate complex technical findings into meaningful value stories for stakeholders, ensuring you never work in a silo. You are a technical strategy owner and diagnostician, connecting across Customer Success, Support, Customer Engineering, Trust & Safety Advisory (TASA), Managed Operations, and Product/Engineering.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a Technical Account Manager who operates as a technical diagnostician first: someone who reads workflows, labeling practices, and score behavior closely enough to catch drift before it becomes a fire. You'll build deep, lasting familiarity with each customer's implementation, architecture, and roadmap, and you'll translate what you find into value stories that land with both hands-on engineers and executive stakeholders. This is a partnership role by design — you'll work in close alignment with your paired CSM on every account, never in a silo.

What you'll do

-
Serve as the named, persistent technical partner for a portfolio of strategic and premium accounts in close alignment with the CSM, acting as a collaborative team player rather than working in a silo.

-
Build and maintain a technical success plan for each account alongside the CSM, translating technical diagnostics into clear business value stories and executive roadmaps.

-
Diagnose and guide customers on ongoing best practices for workflow design, labeling strategy, and configuration hygiene, leveraging pattern recognition across your book of business in tandem with the CSM.

-
Own implementation continuity after go-live in partnership with the CSM, ensuring deep account context survives the handoff from onboarding and technical drift is caught early.

-
Run recurring technical health reviews and diagnostic readouts with the CSM, surfacing risks early and turning observations into actionable optimization plans.

-
Act as the voice of the customer internally by spotting recurring technical patterns, feature requests, and workflow trends across your book of business and feeding them directly to Product and Engineering.

-
Act as the primary technical partner to the CSM across Support, Customer Engineering, TASA, Managed Operations, and Product/Engineering so customers receive one seamless, aligned strategy.

-
Contribute to account retention and growth by catching technical risk early, keeping accounts model-release ready, and cutting down repeat issues, in partnership with the CSM who owns the relationship and renewal conversation.

What you'll bring

Prior experience in fraud or payments.

Working SQL and data analysis skills, or the ability to quickly get there, for pulling and interpreting account-specific data.

Experience running formal technical health reviews, QBR-style technical readouts, or success planning cadences.

title: Security Research Engineer, Attack Surface & Risk Signals
description:
About CyberCube:

CyberCube delivers the world's leading analytics to quantify digital risk, helping the largest global carriers, reinsurers and brokers understand, price and manage cyber risk in financial terms.

-
AI at our foundation, cyber risk at our core. We don't just use AI, we shape it.

Built on AI from day one. Artificial intelligence has been part of our strategy since the beginning, blended with deep cybersecurity and insurance expertise and backed by rigorous testing.

Trusted by more than 100 clients, including 75% of the top 40 European and US cyber insurance carriers and 70% of the top ten reinsurance brokers.

Backed for global growth. In 2025 Spectrum Equity joined some of CyberCube’s financial partners as a new cornerstone investor, accelerating our global growth and fueling innovation across our end-to-end cyber risk analytics for the insurance industry.

A truly global team across San Francisco, New York, London, and Tallinn.

-
A culture of collaboration, openness, intellectual rigor, and ownership for excellence.

-
People at the forefront. We encourage CyberCubers to challenge themselves, push boundaries, and do the best work of their careers.

Quantitative Cyber Risk Engineer

About the Role Are you fascinated by the underlying architecture of the internet? Do you look at complex network configurations and immediately see the quantitative risk exposure?

As a Quantitative Cyber Risk Engineer, you will play a critical role at the intersection of network engineering, cybersecurity, and data science. We are looking for an expert who deeply understands how the internet is wired—down to the protocol level—and possesses the quantitative prowess to translate that knowledge into computable risk metrics.

In this role, you will analyze how global businesses configure their internet-facing assets and design mathematical signals that accurately quantify their exposure to cyber attacks. Working alongside Data Scientists, Engineers, and Product teams, your research and models will directly drive the next generation of risk-scoring and analytical engines for the cyber insurance industry.

If you are passionate about turning theoretical network vulnerabilities into actionable, real-world risk signals that influence a global industry, this is the role for you.

Key Responsibilities

-
Design Risk Signals: Develop innovative, quantitative signals that accurately measure a company’s exposure to cyber attacks based on their network architecture, asset configurations, and internet footprint.

-
Quantify the Unquantifiable: Translate theoretical cybersecurity concepts and complex network topologies into empirical, actionable risk metrics and assumptions.

-
Architectural Deep-Dives: Evaluate and extract meaningful insights from how organizations deploy and configure internet-facing protocols, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise networks.

-
Threat Landscape Research: Conduct in-depth research on emerging cyber threats (e.g., critical vulnerabilities, ransomware, trending exploits, data breach techniques) and map them to underlying asset configurations.

-
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the subject matter expert on internet architecture, working closely with product, analytics, and engineering teams to integrate your risk signals into production models.

Must-Have Skills & Qualifications

-
Deep Internet & Networking Expertise: Expert-level understanding of how the internet works at a foundational level. You should be intimately familiar with network protocols (TCP/IP, BGP, DNS, HTTP/S, TLS), routing, ASN ecosystems, and complex enterprise network configurations.

-
Strong Quantitative Acumen: Proven ability to apply mathematical and statistical concepts to real-world problems. You must be able to design quantitative metrics and build logic that scores and sizes risk exposure accurately.

-
Analytical Mindset: Exceptional problem-solving skills with a track record of conceptualizing complex, abstract security concepts and breaking them down into measurable data points.

-
Educational Background: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related highly quantitative/technical field.

-
Experience: 3–5+ years of relevant work experience in network engineering, cyber threat research, risk modeling, or a related domain.

Good-to-Have (Preferred) Skills

-
Coding for Signal Creation: Proficiency in Python or R to prototype algorithms and turn your theoretical risk concepts into actual programmatic outputs.

-
Data Querying: Experience with SQL and relational databases to pull, manipulate, and analyze large datasets of asset and configuration data.

-
Big Data Exposure: Familiarity with big data frameworks (Spark / Hadoop), flat files, complex data types (JSON, XML), and working with APIs.

-
Industry Context: Experience working in or adjacent to the cyber insurance, risk modeling, or data science industries.

-
Certifications: Advanced technical or security certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, or advanced Cisco/networking certifications) are a plus, but hands-on expertise matters most.

Who might thrive here
This role is a fit for people from many backgrounds. You might be a Security Researcher, Threat Researcher, Penetration Tester or Offensive Security Engineer who knows how attackers find and exploit exposed assets. Or you might come from network engineering, detection engineering, or attack surface management and know exactly how internet-facing infrastructure gets set up and misconfigured. If you've done bug bounty or red team work, or built security data and risk models, and you want to turn that experience into signals that shape a global industry, we'd love to hear from you.

AI Fluency at CyberCube

AI is reshaping how work gets done across every function. We value people who are curious about AI, eager to learn, and thoughtful about applying AI tools to work more effectively. AI fluency is part of how we assess every role in our hiring process.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway.

Research shows the best candidates rarely match a job description point for point. If you're excited about this role and believe you could make an impact, we'd love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn't line up perfectly with everything listed above.

We don’t tolerate discrimination against age, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, race, color, nationality, ethnicity, religion, disability, veteran status, protected genetic information or political affiliation.

Cobalt is a private equity-backed company aiming to build the most impactful business in the commercial access and security industry (access control systems, video surveillance systems, intrusion detection systems and other low voltage systems integration). Cobalt is backed by Alpine Investors, a private equity firm specializing in middle market companies in the services and software industries and with $15bn+ of AUM. Just two years after launching, Cobalt has successfully acquired 21 partner companies and established itself as one of the leading platforms in a highly attractive and fragmented industry that is benefitting from substantial secular growth tailwinds.

As Cobalt continues to acquire new companies, this role is the linchpin that turns a signed deal into a fully operating, data-accurate part of the platform.

- Run end-to-end data migration for technology implementations: be the main point person for data migrations from legacy systems to new systems, including data discovery calls, data extraction, cleansing, mapping, validation, and import into new systems

- 2 to 5 years in an operations analyst, business intelligence, data, or chief-of-staff role, or in consulting environment with hands-on data work.

- Experience contributing pharmacology data and recommendations to development candidate nomination, coordinating external research partners, and supporting IND-enabling activities.

title: Strategic WFM Analyst
description:
About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

Role Overview

The Strategic WFM Analyst lives in the Core Workforce Management (WFM) Planning & Operations Strategy team and is responsible for owning centralized forecast, capacity planning, workforce cost optimization, and strategic headcount trade-offs across all lines of business (LOBs). Moving beyond traditional scheduling and intraday monitoring, this role acts as a high-judgment governance function, translating complex demand forecasts into defensible FTE, BPO, and overtime spend strategies, modeling capacity risks, and aligning executive stakeholders across Finance, Product, and Operations. You are exceptionally strong in WFM math and financial analytics, exhibit deep strategic curiosity, navigate messy raw data effortlessly, and communicate recommendations with executive-level clarity.

What You’ll Do

-
Translating multi-LOB demand forecasts into monthly and quarterly capacity, headcount, and budget requirements.

-
Modeling workforce and financial trade-offs across internal FTEs, BPO partners, overtime spend, bonus hours, productivity shifts, and shrinkage.

-
Analyzing demand-funnel changes (e.g., product feature rollouts, AI bot deflection shifts) and quantifying their exact capacity and dollar blast radius.

-
Partnering directly with Finance, Product, and Operations to validate baseline assumptions, enforce input SLAs, and align on staffing commitments.

-
Drafting concise, decision-ready executive memos and Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs) for Directors and leadership.

-
Conducting deep-dive root-cause analyses whenever operational actuals deviate from capacity plans and establishing corrective action paths.

-
Standardizing capacity planning frameworks, modeling templates, and operating standards across LOBs.

-
Maintaining deep forecasting competency to audit models, challenge underlying assumptions, and provide seamless coverage across the broader central WFM engine.

What We’re Looking For

-
Strategic WFM Math: Exceptionally strong quantitative background with deep expertise in WFM fundamentals (capacity modeling, Erlang, shrinkage, AHT, SLA/ASA trade-offs) and advanced proficiency in Google Sheets, SQL, or Python.

-
Business & Financial Judgment: Demonstrated ability to connect operational queue dynamics directly to dollar exposure, hiring velocity, BPO costs, and SLA risk.

-
Executive Communication: Superior strategic writing skills with a natural instinct to distill complex, multi-variable workforce analytics into scannable, 1-2 page decision memos.

-
Cross-Functional Influence: Proven ability to establish governance frameworks, challenge bad assumptions with backtested data, and align Finance, Product, and Operations leadership without formal authority.

-
Blank-Page Ownership: High comfort operating in ambiguous environments with incomplete data, verifiably isolating what materially matters without requiring step-by-step direction.

-
WFM Analyst Profile: Strong core WFM domain expertise with a strategic/Ops spike, not a generalist and not a passive traditional scheduler.

Hiring Process

-
Application

-
Diagnostic Case Study (7-Day Strategic Diagnostic & Modeling Exercise)

-
Technical & Capacity Interview (Francesco Vitone – WFM)

-
Executive Judgment & Strategic Interview (Connor Garrett – Core Operations)

-
Culture Interview (People Ops)

-
Offer

That means driving our Credit Risk Framework, defining the risk appetite, challenging and shaping our credit strategy, and overseeing how the business executes it within that appetite, right across the credit lifecycle. You'll spot the risks inthe portfolio before they show up in the numbers, so Monzo Bank Europe can grow fast and keep growing.

You'll also lead our credit risk analytics and measurement. You'll direct the development of our IFRS 9 expected credit loss models, make sure our impairment provisions hold up, and turn portfolio data into insight the business acts on. You'll do that with modern methods and technology, including artificial intelligence, and set the standard for how we use and control them.

This role reports to the Director of Credit Risk, Monzo Bank Europe.

The role you are applying for is a Controlled Function (CF-2) within the meaning of the Central Bank Reform Act, 2010. For this role, appointment will be conditional on Monzo being fully satisfied that the appointee meets the requirements as set out in the Fitness and Probity Standards 2018 issued by the Central Bank of Ireland. As a CF, the role holder will be subject to Conduct Standards under the Central Bank of Ireland Individual Accountability Framework and will be required to take reasonable steps to ensure that the relevant conduct standards are met.

🔑 You’ll play a key role by...

- Credit Risk Framework and Appetite

- Developing, implementing and continuously improving our Credit Risk Framework in Europe, keeping it aligned to the entity's strategy.

- Formulating and overseeing the Credit Risk Appetite Statement and its limit structure, so lending growth stays inside agreed boundaries.

- Turning appetite into practical limits, triggers and escalation paths, and overseeing how the First Line of Defence (1st LoD) puts them into practice.

- Embedding group-wide credit risk frameworks locally, with clear escalation between global standards and local policy.

- 2nd LoD oversight of credit risk activities

- Giving independent oversight and challenge across credit policy, underwriting and credit decisioning strategies, affordability, pricing, and collections and recovery.

- Issuing formal 2nd LoD opinions on new products, policy and strategy changes, and material lending decisions.

- Reviewing portfolio asset quality regularly, including performance trends, vintage analysis and emerging pockets of risk.

- Overseeing the adequacy assessment of IFRS 9 impairment provisions, and giving a clear 2nd LoD view on whether provisions are appropriate.

- Credit risk measurement

- Leading the measurement of our credit risk end to end, from data and methodology through to the loss estimates we report.

- Owning the development and maintenance of the IFRS 9 expected credit loss models, including the PD, LGD, EAD and forward-looking information (FLI) inputs behind them.

- Setting the methodology for staging, significant increase in credit risk, macroeconomic scenarios and post-model adjustments.

- Keeping model documentation and evidence in good shape, and closing validation findings on time.

- Bringing advanced techniques and artificial intelligence into how we build and run these models, with the controls and transparency that come with them.

- Supplying credit risk parameters and expert input to capital, stress testing and financial planning work.

- Monitoring, early warning and MI

- Building credit risk monitoring and early warning processes that spot problems early.

- Delivering high quality, timely credit risk management information and insight to senior internal and external stakeholders.

- Making the numbers tell a clear story, so people can make decisions quickly and confidently.

- Committee governance and independent challenge

- Acting as Secretariat and Deputy Chair of the Credit Risk Oversight Committee, shaping agendas, tracking actions, and presenting 2nd LoD reports and opinions.

- Escalating credit risk appetite breaches and material risks promptly to the Executive Risk Committee and the Board Risk Committee.

- Giving clear, evidence-based challenge to 1st LoD credit, analytics and product teams, and to accountable executives.

- Regulatory compliance and engagement

- Making sure credit risk management meets the legal and regulatory requirements of the markets we operate in, including Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) requirements, Irish and European Union law, and European Banking Authority (EBA) and European Central Bank (ECB) guidelines.

- Leading the 2nd LoD assessment of changing and new credit regulation.

- Supporting regulatory reporting and engagement, and supporting the Director of Credit Risk on executing their PCF-22 obligations.

- Acting as a key point of contact for the CBI, internal audit and external auditors on credit risk matters.

- Leadership and stakeholder management

- Building the credit risk oversight function from the ground up. You'll start hands-on, then hire and lead a team as the business grows.

- Putting cutting-edge technology at the heart of how the function works from day one, including generative and agentic artificial intelligence, and making sure we control those tools as carefully as we control everything else.

- Balancing commercial ambition with rigorous risk boundaries, and helping the business grow safely.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…

- You have a degree in a quantitative or financial discipline, such as Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, Mathematics, Finance or Financial Engineering. Further qualifications like the CFA, FRM or PRM are a strong plus.

- You've led credit risk oversight or credit risk measurement in a retail bank, challenger bank or a top financial regulatory consulting practice, ideally in a regulated European Union entity.

- You know retail credit risk modelling inside out: PD, LGD, EAD, IFRS 9 staging and expected credit loss, affordability and forward-looking information.

- You've owned or independently challenged credit risk appetite, credit policy, underwriting and collections strategies, and you can tell a strong one from a weak one.

- You understand European regulation well, including EBA and ECB guidelines, IFRS 9, the CCD2 and GDPR, and how they apply day to day.

- You have proven experience in independent engagement with with internal and external auditors and supervisory authorities, preferably the CBI and/or ECB

- You're tech-fluent, with hands-on SQL and Python, and keen to use generative and agentic artificial intelligence to speed up risk work, with clear eyes on the controls that need to come with it.

- You give clear, structured, objective challenge to 1st LoD teams, and people listen because your evidence is strong.

- You've built credit risk frameworks, models or governance from scratch, including where data is sparse.

- You can turn complex analysis into simple, useful insight for senior management and the board.

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 A salary range of €121,000 - €163,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance.

📍This role will have a hybrid working model, based in our Dublin office 2 - 3 days a week. You will also travel to Monzo’s head office in London from time to time.

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.

🏝 Annual Leave - 34 days including public holidays (24 holiday days + 10 public holidays)

📚€1,200 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

🏥 Private healthcare scheme

💰Pension scheme: the minimum contribution is 4% and Monzo matches any additional contributions that you make up to a maximum of 6%

💛 Wellbeing benefits: financial education, women’s and men’s health support, mental health benefits, including coaching and counselling

🌈 The application journey has 3 key steps

This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. You can read them here.

We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out.

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. title: Strategic Customer Success Manager
description:
A Better Built World

At Miter, we’re on a mission to help construction contractors build with confidence. If we’re successful, we’ll make it easier and faster to build critical physical infrastructure - roads, bridges, utilities, data centers, housing, etc.

For decades, construction and field services contractors have had to run their businesses on outdated software: clunky, on-premise systems created in the 1980s and 1990s.

That’s where Miter comes in. We’re using AI and embedded payments to rebuild the core HR, finance, and operations systems that underpin our physical economy. Using Miter, contractors like Marathon Electrical, W.J. O’Neil, and Truebeck Construction are building stronger teams, controlling job costs, and accelerating jobsite execution.

This idea is resonating. Since we launched in 2021, we’ve grown to thousands of customers and tens of millions in ARR, making us one of the fastest growing vertical software companies ever. To double-down on our momentum, we’ve raised $50M+ from top investors (Bessemer, Coatue, and Battery) who share our belief that we’re just getting started.

About the Role

As Miter moves up-market, we’re looking for a Strategic Customer Success Manager to own our largest and most complex customer relationships post-launch. You’ll manage a book of business in the $2–$3M ARR range — multi-entity accounts, large field workforces, and PE-backed, high-growth contractors where executive stakeholders are deeply invested in outcomes.

This is an outcomes-driven role. You’ll be measured on gross and net revenue retention, product adoption and health, and the expansion pipeline you generate. You’ll build C-suite relationships, construct and execute strategic account plans, navigate escalations with calm and credibility, and drive every initiative to completion. You’ll partner closely with Launch, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Support, and Product to turn customers into long-term advocates and help define what world-class customer success looks like at Miter.

Our team is collaborative, detail-oriented, and energized by solving complex problems together. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, love ownership, and enjoy turning ambiguity into structure, you’ll fit right in.

What You’ll Own

-
Book of business & retention. Own a portfolio of strategic accounts (~$2–$3M in ARR) and carry the number for both gross revenue retention (GRR) and net revenue retention (NRR), proactively forecasting and de-risking every renewal.

-
Adoption & customer health. Drive deep, durable adoption of the Miter platform across payroll, HR, and finance workflows — monitoring health signals, building success plans, and intervening early to keep accounts on track to value.

-
Expansion & CSQLs. Identify, qualify, and advance Customer Success Qualified Leads (CSQLs) — surfacing upsell and cross-sell opportunities and partnering with Sales to convert them into expansion revenue.

-
C-suite relationships. Establish and deepen trusted-advisor relationships with executive sponsors (CEO, CFO, COO, VP of HR/Operations), running executive business reviews that tie Miter to measurable business outcomes.

-
Strategic account planning. Build and maintain account plans for each customer — stakeholder maps, success metrics, value-realization roadmaps, and risk registers — and execute against them with clear milestones.

-
Escalation management. Serve as the point of accountability when issues arise, coordinating cross-functional response, communicating clearly with executives, and driving escalations to resolution.

-
Drive to completion. Operate with minimal oversight to push initiatives, renewals, and expansion efforts across the finish line — owning outcomes end-to-end, not just activities.

-
Cross-functional partnership. Work closely with Launch, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Support, Product, and Engineering to ensure seamless handoffs, relay customer insights, and advocate for improvements that reflect customer needs and industry trends.

-
Scale the function. Contribute to playbooks, process improvements, and team best practices — turning learnings into leverage as we grow the Strategic CS motion.

What You’ll Need

-
6+ years in customer success, account management, consulting, or a fast-growing services/ops role — ideally owning enterprise or strategic accounts

-
Demonstrated ownership of an Enterprise book of business with a track record of strong gross and net revenue retention and expansion against quota

-
Experience building relationships with and presenting to C-suite and senior executive stakeholders

-
Experience with payroll, accounting, tax, HCM, ERP, or other financial/operational products

-
Strong account-planning and project-management skills; able to manage multi-month initiatives and drive them to completion

-
Comfort working with data (Excel/Sheets) to diagnose health, quantify value, and build the business case for expansion

-
Ability to understand integrations, APIs, and technical documentation well enough to unblock customers

-
Consistently handle escalated account situations and drive them to resolution while keeping internal executives and client stakeholders aligned.

-
Highly organized, detail-driven, and adaptable when things aren’t fully defined

-
HCM, ERP, and/or construction industry exposure (a plus)

Our Interview Process

-
Recruiter Pre-Screen

-
Hiring Manager Interview

-
Miter Values Interview

-
Presentation

-
Final 1:1 Interview

Our Benefits:

-
Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive (well above “market”) salary, commission, and equity packages.

-
Medical Insurance: Comprehensive medical, dental, FSA, vision plans to suit you and your family’s needs.

-
401(k) Retirement Plan: Company-matched contributions to help you plan for your future.

-
Flexible PTO: Take the time you need to recharge and be your best self.

-
Parental Leave: Generous 16-week paid leave for all parents, including adoptive and foster parents.

-
Learning & Development: We offer every employee an annual educational allowance to explore external professional development.

-
Office Extras: Snacks, coffee, lunch, and commuter benefits for in-office Mitosaurs.

-
Community: Company-wide and team-specific off-sites per year.

Hybrid vs. Remote Approach:

We believe the magic of Miter comes from working side by side. We also believe in work flexibility. For roles that are listed as hybrid, our approach is 3 days a week in the office giving us the chance to connect, brainstorm, and build stronger relationships. If you live within a reasonable commute to either our New York City or San Francisco offices, we ask that you work in our hybrid approach.

Otherwise, for roles listed as remote or in other cities where we don't have an office location, there is no requirement to work in our hybrid approach. We do travel a few times a year for onboarding, company-wide and team specific off-sites!

Join our Talent Community

Not seeing a role that matches your background right now? Apply to our Talent Community, and we’ll reach out if a role opens up that aligns with your experience!

Equal Opportunity:

Miter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Use of Artificial Intelligence in Our Hiring Process:

Miter uses AI-assisted tools as part of our hiring process to help our recruiting team manage and review applications more efficiently. We want to be transparent about how this works.

What the AI does: When you apply to a role at Miter, an AI tool may review your application against the specific qualifications and requirements posted for that job. This tool identifies whether your experience appears to meet, partially meet, or not meet each stated requirement, and it provides supporting evidence from your application for every assessment it makes.

What the AI does not do: The AI does not make hiring decisions. It does not reject, advance, or rank candidates on its own, and it does not assign you a numerical score. Every application is reviewed by a member of our recruiting team, who makes the final call on whether you move forward. The AI is a tool that helps our team prioritize their time across a high volume of applications. It is not a substitute for human judgment.

What information it uses: The tool evaluates the application materials you submit (your resume and any other application content) against role-specific criteria our team has defined. It does not pull information from external sources such as social media or professional networking profiles, and personal identifying information is removed from your materials before any AI review takes place.

Human oversight: Our recruiting team periodically reviews how these tools are performing to check for unintended patterns in outcomes, and we retain the ability to override any AI-generated assessment at any time.

You will join a collaborative, inclusive culture where your strengths have room to grow and your ideas can drive real impact. We are actively hiring for an Enterprise Risk Management Specialist Lead!

Your Role:

The Enterprise Risk Management Lead supports the organization’s risk management framework and provides complex risk analysis, reporting, and advisory support to senior management and internal stakeholders. Operating with a high degree of independence, the role applies sound judgment to medium- and high-complexity matters, including new and ambiguous situations where precedent may be limited.

The role’s primary emphasis is the implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of enterprise risk management processes. As a secondary accountability, the role supports the enterprise approach to responsible artificial intelligence by coordinating AI governance activities, facilitating cross-functional reviews, and helping ensure AI-related risks and controls are proportionate to each use case’s impact and maturity.

Your Work:

- Implement and continuously improve enterprise risk management processes, including risk identification, ownership, assessment, scoring, monitoring, reporting, mitigation quantification, and action planning across established and emerging risk areas.

- Support the annual ERM planning cycle by helping define risk priorities, assessment activities, reporting expectations, governance calendars, and areas requiring deeper review, including AI and emerging technology risks.

- Establish and maintain processes to monitor enterprise risks on an ongoing basis, with clear ownership, escalation paths, mitigation actions, approval conditions, and follow-up requirements.

- Identify and evaluate emerging risks and trends, including risks associated with generative AI, machine learning, AI-enabled workflows, autonomous or agentic systems, data use, cybersecurity, model performance, third parties, and technology architecture.

- Apply a consistent, proportionate risk methodology to evaluate business impact, autonomy, data sensitivity, external exposure, regulatory considerations, reversibility, control effectiveness, residual risk, and lifecycle stage.

- Manage risk intake and assessment activities for enterprise initiatives and AI use cases, including initial risk analysis, review routing, case readiness, documentation requirements, decision materials, and governance follow-up.

- Coordinate cross-functional risk reviews with Enterprise Risk Management, Compliance, Legal, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Model Governance, Data Governance, Enterprise Architecture, technology teams, and business partners.

- Help determine the appropriate level and pathway of governance review based on materiality and risk, including whether matters qualify for streamlined review or require broader committee, executive, or Board-level consideration.

- Distinguish controls appropriate for experimentation and pilots from requirements needed before production, external deployment, regulated use, or implementation of more autonomous capabilities.

- Assess whether proposed safeguards and human oversight are meaningful, timely, supported by appropriate information and authority, and sufficient for the nature and significance of the risk.

- Identify material evidence gaps, conflicting recommendations, unclear ownership, duplicative requirements, control weaknesses, and requirements that are not proportionate to the underlying risk or decision consequence.

- Develop timely, accurate, and decision-ready risk reports, analyses, dashboards, executive briefings, and recommendations that clearly describe risk exposure, safeguards, residual risk, required decisions, and accountable owners.

- Prepare standard Board and committee risk materials, including quarterly Audit Committee updates, annual reports to the full Board, and information related to material or emerging risks such as AI.

- Support the leader accountable for enterprise AI governance and coordinate the day-to-day activities of the cross-functional AI Council as part of the organization’s broader risk-governance structure.

- Draft risk acceptance or approval conditions, escalation recommendations, decision records, and practical guidance for business and technical teams.

- Develop and maintain enterprise risk and AI governance policies, procedures, standards, playbooks, templates, risk tiers, intake criteria, review methods, and control documentation.

- Ensure governance documentation clearly distinguishes mandatory requirements, conditional controls, and informational guidance, and accurately reflects accountable owners, approval status, effective dates, version history, and superseded materials.

- Respond to external ERM compliance, information, and reporting requirements in coordination with accountable subject-matter experts, including requirements affecting AI and emerging technologies.

- Provide complex risk analysis and practical recommendations that support business decisions and responsible innovation while protecting the enterprise and avoiding unnecessary governance burden.

- Promote clear risk ownership, consistent governance practices, reusable evidence, meaningful accountability, and effective coordination across business, risk, compliance, legal, technology, and control functions.

Required Experience, Education and Skills:

- Bachelor’s degree in a related field or an equivalent combination or education and experience.
- 6+ years of proven experience in risk management, insurance, financial analysis, actuarial, underwriting, product management or related experience required.

What would make us excited about you?

- Prior experience in Enterprise Risk Management strongly preferred.
- Strong organizational and project management skills and ability to accurately complete complex projects within tight deadlines, including leading multiple projects simultaneously.
- A solution-oriented problem solver with strong analytical skills. Able to quickly gain a solid understanding of the company's operations and overall business goals and objectives.
- Experience working with operational / product / financial measures and models, including analysis of results.
- Ability to collaborate with all levels of personnel from end users to executive management.
- Ability to influence outcomes with or without formal authority, often delivering results through others.
- Ability to build business case scenarios.
- People-oriented with excellent communication skills (oral and written modes).
- Relevant certifications are preferred, including: Associate in Risk Management (ARM), Associate in Reinsurance (ARe), Chartered Property/Casualty Underwriter (CPCU), Financial Risk Management (FRM), or Associate of Casualty Actuary Society (ACAS).
- Understanding of CSAA IG business strategy.
- Broad actuarial skillset with deep understanding of pricing, reserving, ERM, statutory accounting, and risk and return concepts.
- Actively shapes our company culture (e.g., participating in employee resource groups, volunteering, etc.).
- Lives into cultural norms (e.g., willing to have cameras on when it matters: helping onboard new team members, building relationships, etc.).

description:
Job Description

Are you looking for your next opportunity?

Sompo has a unique opportunity for a Data Quality Assurance in our IT team.

The Quality Assurance Lead will be responsible for leading QA activities for enterprise data warehouse data validation, Strategy and Power BI report testing. This role will oversee a QA team, including onshore and offshore team members, and will be accountable for defining, maintaining, and enforcing QA standards, policies, procedures, documentation, and testing best practices.

This role requires strong experience in data warehouse testing, data reconciliation, SQL-based validation, report testing, test planning, defect management, and stakeholder communication.

Location: This position will be based out of our Purchase, NY; Conshohocken, PA; or Charlotte, NC office. We strive for collaboration which is why we offer a work environment where our employees thrive and develop long lasting careers.

Our business, your impact, our opportunity:

What you’ll be doing:

- Lead end-to-end quality assurance activities for enterprise data warehouse, Strategy, and Power BI reporting initiatives. Manage and coordinate the work of the QA resources, including assigning work, reviewing deliverables, tracking progress, and ensuring adherence to QA standards.
- Develop, maintain, and enforce QA policies, procedures, testing standards, templates, documentation practices, and quality gates.
- Define QA strategy, test plans, test scenarios, test cases, test data requirements, and traceability matrices for data warehouse and reporting projects.
- Perform and oversee data validation, data reconciliation, source-to-target testing, ETL testing, regression testing, integration testing, user acceptance testing support, and production validation. Validate data movement across source systems, staging areas, enterprise data warehouse layers, semantic/reporting layers, Strategy outputs, and Power BI reports.
- Review source-to-target mappings, business requirements, technical specifications, report requirements, and data models to identify test coverage needs and quality risks. Develop and execute SQL queries to validate data completeness, accuracy, transformation logic, aggregations, calculations, and reconciliation results. Lead testing of Power BI reports, including validation of report visuals, filters, slicers, measures, KPIs, calculations, drill-throughs, row-level security, refresh results, and alignment with business requirements.
- Support testing of Strategy-related data outputs and reporting processes to ensure consistency, accuracy, completeness, and usability. Manage defect identification, documentation, prioritization, triage, tracking, retesting, and closure across QA cycles.
- Partner with developers, ETL teams, data architects, reporting teams, business analysts, and business stakeholders to resolve data quality and reporting issues.
- Provide QA status reporting, test execution metrics, defect metrics, risk assessments, and quality dashboards to project and technology leadership. Identify testing risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and data quality concerns, and escalate issues appropriately.
- Establish and maintain QA documentation, including test plans, test scripts, execution evidence, sign-off documentation, defect logs, test summary reports, and runbooks.
- Drive continuous improvement of QA processes, automation opportunities, documentation standards, and data validation practices.
- Mentor QA team members and provide guidance on data warehouse testing, SQL validation, report testing, defect management, and quality assurance best practices.

What you’ll bring:

- 7+ years of experience in quality assurance, with significant experience testing enterprise data warehouse, business intelligence, reporting, or analytics solutions.
- 5+ years of experience leading QA teams, preferably teams of approximately 10 or more resources across onshore and offshore delivery models.
- Strong hands-on experience with data warehouse testing, ETL testing, data reconciliation, source-to-target validation, data quality testing, and production validation.
- Advanced SQL skills, including the ability to write complex queries for data validation, reconciliation, aggregation testing, transformation testing, and root-cause analysis.
- Experience testing reports, dashboards, semantic models, datasets, measures, KPIs, filters, slicers, calculations, drill-through functionality, and report refresh results. Experience with PowerBI and Strategy preferred
- Experience validating reports and analytics outputs against business requirements, source data, warehouse data, and defined business logic.
- Strong understanding of enterprise data warehouse concepts, including dimensional modeling, fact and dimension tables, data marts, staging layers, semantic layers, and reporting layers.
- Experience reviewing source-to-target mappings, data models, technical specifications, report specifications, and business requirements to design effective test coverage.
- Experience with defect management and test management tools such as Azure DevOps, Fresh Service, or similar platforms.
- Experience establishing QA standards, policies, test templates, procedures, metrics, and governance practices.
- Familiarity with ETL tools, data integration processes, batch processing, scheduling, and production support concepts.
- Experience with automated testing approaches for data validation, regression testing, or report testing is preferred.
- Experience in insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated data environments is preferred.

description:
About Wonder

Everything’s on the menu at Wonder. Except compromise.

About The Opportunity
We are hiring a Associate Director, Inventory Data to lead the integrity, governance, and financial correctness of the data that underpins inventory, cost of goods sold, and product costing. This is a senior cross-functional role for someone who can operate at the intersection of finance, operations, systems, product, and analytics to help ensure that inventory-related data is accurate, auditable, explainable, and trusted across the business. The right candidate brings a combination of inventory process fluency, financial rigor, systems thinking, and hands-on analytical capability. You know how operational events become financial outcomes, and you know how to design the controls, validations, and governance needed to make that process reliable at scale.

The Impact You'll Make

- Represent Finance Data & Systems in evaluating and shaping decisions that impact the financial integrity of core inventory-related datasets, including inventory transactions and balances, purchase orders, receiving, bill of materials, product and vendor master data, and unit-of-measure logic
- Design and maintain robust validation routines that keep inventory data complete, accurate, and consistent across systems
- Investigate data anomalies, quantify business and financial impact, identify root causes, and drive issues through to resolution
- Build scalable exception management processes that reduce recurring problems and improve upstream data quality
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, Procurement, Accounting, and Data teams on workflows and system changes that affect inventory, costing, invoicing, and reporting
- Review requirements and designs for inventory-related changes to ensure financial implications are understood and addressed before launch
- Develop reconciliations, dashboards, and reporting that improve visibility into inventory accuracy, waste, costing and stock movements
- Help strengthen the company’s control environment, reporting reliability, and operational decision- making through better data ownership and governance
- What Success Looks Like : In this role, you will serve as the senior owner of inventory data as a source of financial truth. You will help the company move from reactive issue resolution and manual reconciliation toward a more proactive, governed, and scalable model. Success means:
- Confidence in inventory balances, costing, and margin data
- Faster detection and resolution of exceptions
- Better alignment between operational systems and financial reporting needs
- Stronger readiness for close, audit, and ongoing business scale
- Clearer ownership and accountability for one of the most critical data domains in the company

What You Bring To The Table

- 7+ years of experience across inventory finance, operations finance, inventory product ownership, or similar fields
- Deep understanding of how inventory activity flows through operational systems into accounting and financial reporting
- Strong accounting foundation in inventory and COGS, including standard costing, bills of materials, and inventory valuation
- Strong experience with reconciliations, exception management, and data quality controls in complex or fast-changing environments, including building automated reconciliations, KPI frameworks, dashboards, and data quality monitoring
- Hands-on SQL proficiency sufficient to investigate and reconcile large inventory datasets independently - multi-table joins across transactional and master data, common table expressions, window functions (running balances, deduplication, period-over-period movement), conditional aggregation, date and period logic, point-in-time cost and price lookups, and multi-level bill of materials
- Experience with a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, or similar) and authoring automated data quality tests, together with fluency in modern reporting and data tools and advanced Excel
- Experience in fast-growing, operationally complex environments that involve manufacturing or multi-site production
- Exposure to audit readiness, internal controls, or pre-IPO environments
- Proven ability to work effectively across Finance, Operations, Product, and Data teams
- Ability to translate complex system behavior into clear business and financial insight for senior stakeholders
- A track record of bringing structure and clarity to ambiguous, high-impact problems
- You are comfortable moving between executive-level conversations, detailed operational workflows, and technical data discussions. You can see both the operational reality and the financial consequence—and you know how to connect the two.

Got These? Even Better

- Strong accounting foundation within the domain
- Experience in fast-growing, operationally complex environments such as food, retail, consumer, manufacturing, logistics, or marketplace businesses
- Experience inventory, procurement, finance systems
- Intermediate to Advanced proficiency in SQL, Big Query, advanced Excel
- Experience building automated reconciliations, KPI frameworks, dashboards, and data quality monitoring
- Exposure to audit readiness, internal controls, or pre-IPO environments is a plus

title: Wetland and Waterway Permit and Enforcement Coordinator - 2 Openings!
description:

10/07/2026

Position Title:
Wetland and Waterway Permit and Enforcement Coordinator - 2 Openings!

Job Description:

Are you experienced in natural resources and passionate about wetlands and waterways? Apply to be one of our next Wetland and Waterway Permit and Enforcement Coordinators (Natural Resource Specialist 3) by October 21st, 2026! Our agency has 2 (two) openings as well as an opening for a Wetland Ecologist, (REQ-207804). All are welcome to apply; current state employees are encouraged to apply to these positions as a job rotation by including written approval from their current supervisor.

These are both full-time, limited duration positions expected to last through June 30th, 2028, and there may be an opportunity to extend. These positions are eligible for a hybrid remote schedule based out of our Salem office, with required in-office days the first week and two (2) times per week (Tuesdays and Thursdays) for the following four weeks and then 2-3 times per month for the duration of the position. The successful candidates must be able to travel to site visits within Oregon on short notice and, within six months of hiring, live within a reasonable commuting distance to the Salem office.

Making a Difference for Oregon. The Department of State Lands manages the lands that help fund our public schools and protects the state’s waterways and wetlands for the many benefits they provide. Our stewardship ensures vital natural and financial resources contribute to a vibrant, healthy Oregon now and forever. The DSL team makes a difference for Oregonians every day. As a Wetland and Waterway Permit and Enforcement Coordinator, you will too.

The primary purpose of these positions is to represent the regulatory program of the Department of State Lands. This includes issuing Removal-Fill Permits, reviewing monitoring reports for compensatory mitigation, and conducting compliance for authorized and unauthorized activities.

What’s In It for You?

-
- Utilize your skills and experience in natural resources to protect Oregon’s waterways and wetlands through the state’s Removal-Fill Law while engaging the public, government agencies, and other interested parties.
- Receive 1-on-1 mentoring and support from natural resource experts.
- Join an organization with collaborative and engaged co-workers who care about Oregon’s economy, environment, communities, and their co-workers.
- Gain full benefits with 95% to 99% of medical insurance premiums paid by the agency for full-time employees, including mental health coverage.
- Accrue 8 hours of sick leave and 8 hours of vacation leave per month, with your vacation leave accruals increasing every 5 years.
- Receive 11 paid holidays, one (1) floating holiday, three (3) personal business days and other medical, vision and dental benefits, including flexible spending plans and mental health coverage.
- Automatically enrolled into the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS) after six (6) months of full-time service.
- Possibly qualify for the Student Loan Forgiveness Program.
- Earn the initial monthly salary range for this position starting at $5,320 - $8,141 for employees new to public service. After 6 months, you will receive a 6.95% increase with 6% going to your PERS retirement.
- Current PERS employees start at $5,690- $8,707. Please review the Classification and Compensation page for more details.
- NOTE: Starting pay is determined by a pay equity analysis, which is partly based on the number of years of relevant experience.

These positions will report directly to our main Salem office. They are full-time, limited duration positions represented by the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees (AFSCME).

Working Conditions

The successful candidates will primarily work in an office environment with regular and full day of computer use and periods of fast-paced activity and competing priorities. The positions require the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously, including meeting high-priority deadlines.

Travel is an essential function of the positions. They may require site visits performed on the same day as the request. Occasional fieldwork may involve walking along and within waterways, on uneven terrain, on wet and muddy ground, and without pathways in all types of weather. Occasional overnight stays and/or extended work hours may occur along with exposure to inclement weather, field, and road conditions. Work can at times be in remote locations. DSL provides agency-maintained vehicles, field gear reimbursement, and travel expenses for authorized work-related travel and fieldwork.

What You Will Be Doing

As our Wetland and Waterway Permit and Enforcement Coordinator, you will have the opportunity to:

- Regulatory Interpretation. Provide interpretation and explain laws, rules, regulations, policies, and procedures for the public, consultants, and other agency partners.

- Agency Representation. Serve as a DSL representative for entities including the Governor’s Office Regional Solutions Teams, permit applicants, other agencies, members of the public, and industry professionals.

- Review Removal-Fill Applications. Evaluate removal-fill permit applications and provide recommendations for DSL decisions. This includes reviewing and interpreting function and value assessments, alternatives analyses, compensatory mitigation plans, rectification plans, engineering drawings, and evaluating direct and indirect impacts to waters of this state.

- Perform Compliance Monitoring. Investigate projects, conduct site visits, and review reports to assess compliance with permit conditions and evaluate the functions and values of jurisdictional waters.

- Jurisdictional Determinations. Aid in state jurisdictional determinations within jurisdictional waters.

- Carrying Out Enforcement Responsibilities. Investigate wetland and waterway complaints and process violations of the Removal-Fill Law.

- undefined

For a full description of the duties and working conditions, please email us at [email removed] to request the position description.

Minimum Qualifications

To be considered for these positions, please ensure you have one of the following combinations of education and experience:

Three (3) years of experience in aquatic natural resources. At least one year of the experience must be at a technical level or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities.

AND

a bachelor’s degree in a natural resource field such as biology, ecology, natural resources, or environmental science, or

OR

three (3) additional years of related experience.

NOTE: A master’s degree in a natural resource field such as biology, ecology, or environmental science will substitute for up to one (1) year of the required experience.

A doctorate degree in a natural resource field such as biology, ecology, or environmental science will substitute for up to two (2) years of the required experience.

Desired Attributes

Tell us which of the following skills, experiences and related talents you have by highlighting them in your application materials:

- Permitting and Wetland/Waterway Field Experience. Conducting field surveys, wetland delineations, preparing applications and/or permits for wetland, waterway, or other aquatic natural resource projects.

- Ecosystem Dynamics. In-depth knowledge of ecosystem dynamics and services including experience in environmental science, fisheries, hydrology, geomorphology, or soil science.

- Technical & Professional Communication. Strong written and verbal communication skills including professional internal and external customer service and high-quality deliverables. Experience interpreting and explaining environmental regulations or programs to a wide variety of technical and non-technical audiences including public, private, and government entities.

- Compliance & Enforcement. Applying or evaluating compliance with wetland and waterway resource regulations or similar environmental laws.

- GPS/GIS Skills. Using GPS and GIS software, such as ArcGIS Pro, for data analysis and mapping.

- Teamwork & Problem Solving. Demonstrated ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team, including strong conflict resolution abilities.

- Professional Skills. Reliable, professional, self-motivated, and able to work under strict deadlines with strong organizational and time-management skills.

Please attach a cover letter of two (2) pages or less describing the above desired attributes that you bring to this position.

Complete the following steps to apply:

- Fill out the application or attach a resume. Please contact the recruiter if you have any questions about how to fill out the experience fields or to attach a document. Your submitted experience fields or attached resume must include dates (MM/YYYY) for each employer, and any relevant volunteer and/or internship experience.

- Attach a cover letter. Your cover letter should clearly demonstrate how your experience and training relates to the qualities that you have under the “Desired Attributes” section above.

- Your cover letter must be limited to no more than two (2) pages.

- Generic cover letters that do not address the qualities that you have under the “Desired Attributes” section may receive lower scores than those that addressed the desired qualities.

- Complete questionnaire. Answer the checkbox-style questions before submitting your application. If you are applying as an existing state employee for the job rotation option, please upload permission from your current supervisor.

- Respond to requests. After you submit your application, please respond to the public records request authorization and gender identity questionnaire. This screen will come after you submit and will complete the process. If you are a current State of Oregon employee, the tasks will come to your Workday inbox.

- Upload your documents to receive preference. If you are a veteran or current or former Oregon National Guard servicemember, you may receive preference. The task to upload your documents will be available after you submit your application. For privacy reasons, please do not attach your military service document(s) to your application or combine it with any other required document attachments.

The Oregon Department of State Lands is committed to seeking and sustaining a culturally, racially, ethnically, and linguistically diverse working environment. The Department hires staff interested in supporting environmental justice by including communities traditionally underrepresented in public processes. We encourage members of these communities to apply, even if they do not meet 100% of the desired attributes. The Oregon Department of State Lands understands that an authentic focus on equity, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace will in turn create a workforce aligned to meet the challenge of serving all Oregonians.

Additional Information

- This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

- If you need an accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) to participate in the application or selection process, please contact [email removed] and include the job requisition number.

- For more information about applying for positions with the State of Oregon via Workday, you may visit the Oregon job opportunities website.

- Eligible veterans who meet the qualifications will be given veterans' preference. For further information, please check out these Veteran’s Resources, or call the Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs at: [phone removed].

- After you apply, you may be asked to provide additional optional information. Please be sure to check your Workday account for pending tasks or actions under your “My Applications” section. Be sure to check both your email and Workday account for updates regarding this recruitment.

- The state of Oregon does not request or require your age, date of birth, attendance or graduation dates from an educational institution during the application process.

- As an employer, DSL complies with Oregon’s Pay Equity law.

- The use of outside resources such as Artificial Intelligence software during applicant skill assessments, examinations, and/or interviews is prohibited unless otherwise stated by the hiring agency.

- Agency does not offer visa sponsorship. Within three days of hire, applicants will be required to complete I-9 documentation and confirm authorization to work in the United States.

- Review and approve changes to financial master data and reporting structures to ensure consistency across Finance systems and reporting processes.

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer, Motorized Blower Development
description:
Design the technology that helps power better breathing.

Join Resmed’s motorized blower new product development team and help create the mechanical systems at the heart of products designed to improve people’s health. As a Senior Mechanical Engineer, you will design, develop, prototype and test motorized blowers and their components, turning engineering requirements into robust designs that can be manufactured at scale.

Your key deliverables will include mechanical specifications, tolerance analyses, layouts, engineering drawings, technical proposals, test protocols and verification evidence. You will guide project work, mentor junior colleagues and bring sound engineering judgement to decisions that affect product fit, form and function.

This is a hybrid role in Calabasas, California.

What You’ll Do

- Design motorized blower systems, components and assemblies for new products and improvements to existing products.
- Define mechanical specifications that support reliable manufacture and confirm that designs meet product requirements.
- Produce mechanical designs, tolerance analyses, layouts and engineering drawings using established document and change-control processes.
- Build and evaluate prototypes, then plan and execute engineering tests for blowers and related components.
- Analyse test data, document findings and communicate clear recommendations through reports and technical proposals.
- Author and execute protocols for product testing, verification and validation against defined requirements and specifications.
- Assess design risks and potential effects on product fit, form and function, using structured risk-management methods and FMEA.
- Collaborate with Systems Engineering to quantify how blower-level risks may affect the downstream flow generator.
- Apply engineering principles across motor design, rotor and structural dynamics, acoustics, vibration, machine design, fluid dynamics, statistics, numerical methods and engineering economics.
- Lead project-team activities, provide technical direction and formally mentor or train junior engineers.
- Work across manufacturing, quality, operations, procurement, supplier alliance and customer groups to gather input and ensure designs are appropriate for their intended requirements.
- Contribute to the development and refinement of manufacturing processes for the product.
- Use root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methods to investigate technical issues and support sound design decisions.
- Perform other related duties as required to support the team’s development priorities.

What You Bring

- Tertiary qualifications in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
- Expertise with plastic-part design and design for plastic injection moulding.
- Ability to use Creo or Pro/E CAD software and PDM or Intralink.
- Experience with risk management and FMEA.
- Experience working with controlled documents, engineering change processes, engineering drawings, and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing.
- Ability to apply statistical analysis techniques, including the use of Minitab or JMP.
- Familiarity in root-cause analysis and recognised structured problem-solving methods.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical findings to peers and management.

Nice to have

- Understanding of manufacturing operations, the product development lifecycle or the broader Resmed business.
- Knowledge of motors, rotary components, sound, noise and vibration theory, testing equipment and data analysis.
- Experience with FEA software such as ANSYS, high-volume manufacturing or a highly regulated industry, preferably medical devices.

What Sets You Apart

- Sound judgement: You weigh evidence, risk and product requirements before recommending a path forward.
- Constructive leadership: You give clear direction, share knowledge and help junior colleagues build confidence and capability.
- Collaborative approach: You seek input from different functions and turn varied perspectives into practical engineering decisions.
- Adaptability: You respond calmly when technical priorities shift and remain focused on the quality of the outcome.
- Positive challenge: You raise concerns directly, handle disagreement respectfully and work towards solutions that protect the product and the customer.
- Ownership: You work with a high level of autonomy, follow through on commitments and communicate issues early.

Why Join Resmed

At Resmed, your engineering work contributes to technology designed to help people breathe better and live healthier, longer lives. This role offers the chance to shape motorized blower products from design through testing and validation, while working with specialists across engineering and the wider business. You will have meaningful technical scope, opportunities to guide others and a clear connection between your decisions and the performance of products used in healthcare.

title: Principal, Corporate Information Security
description:
At Cotality, we are driven by a single mission—to make the property industry faster, smarter, and more people-centric. Cotality is the trusted source for property intelligence, with unmatched precision, depth, breadth, and insights across the entire ecosystem. Our talented team of 5,000 employees globally uses our network, scale, connectivity and technology to drive the largest asset class in the world. Cotality is committed to cultivating a diverse and inclusive work culture that inspires innovation and bold thinking; it's a place where you can collaborate, feel valued, develop skills and directly impact the real estate economy. We know our people are our greatest asset. At Cotality, you can be yourself, lift people up and make an impact. By putting clients first and continuously innovating, we're working together to set the pace for unlocking new possibilities that better serve the property industry.

Job Description:

Role Overview
We are looking for a Principal, Corporate Information Security to step in as a true Business Information Security Officer (BISO) for our internal business verticals. Think of this role as InfoSec Quality Assurance. You will sit directly between our technical security teams and business units—initially focusing on our Insurance business vertical—to evaluate security postures, assess risk maturity, and transition operations from an ad-hoc state to a defined, managed model. We want someone who can wear the CISO hat, guide executive teams to make smart risk decisions, and eventually expand coverage across additional business verticals. We are building a dynamic team and highly encourage professionals from all backgrounds to apply.

What You Will Do
You will act as the primary security advisor for business leaders across assigned verticals. For example, if a team wants to launch a new application or policy, you are the one reviewing architecture, assessing vulnerability data, and evaluating risk maturity before go-live. You will review internal security exceptions, track remediations, and translate technical vulnerabilities into actual business impact so executives understand the risk. You will also run governance reviews to ensure identity and access controls align with enterprise policies, while actively participating in incident response and change control oversight. It is all about finding ways to help the business move fast while staying completely secure.

Core Competencies and Skills

-
Enterprise Risk & Architecture
Deep hands on experience in enterprise risk management and internal security architecture. You know how to threat model internal applications, design compensating controls, and ensure defense in depth principles are applied before a system goes into production.

-
Executive Presence & Negotiation
You are comfortable sitting in a room with a VP who is pushing to launch a project quickly. You have the backbone to hold the line on critical security requirements, but the business acumen to help them find a "secure yes" rather than just saying "no."

-
Translation & Risk Articulation
You know how to explain complex highly technical concepts using everyday language. Instead of telling a non technical leader about a "CVSS 9.8 vulnerability," you can translate that into operational or financial risk so they actually understand the business impact.

-
Governance Frameworks
A strong working grasp of governance frameworks like COBIT, NIST CSF, or ISO 27001. More importantly, you know how to operationalize these frameworks so they are actively used by the business, not just sitting in a binder.

-
Security Design
Familiarity with security design models like SABSA is a huge plus. You know how to trace a high-level business objective down to a specific technical control, ensuring security serves the business strategy.

-
