title: Senior Staff AI Security Lead
description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Location: This role can work onsite or hybrid from one of our offices. We are open to a fully remote option for the right candidate.
Travel: Up to 10%
Job ID: 1915

The Role:

We are hiring a senior technical leader to build the AI foundation our security organization runs on — and to make sure it actually gets used. This is a dual-mandate role. You will stand up the enterprise AI infrastructure that lets security teams safely build with large language models and agents, and you will lead the adoption effort that turns that infrastructure into measurable gains across detection and response, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, GRC, and security engineering.

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role. You will write code, design systems, and set technical direction. You will not manage a team, but you will lead through influence: partnering with engineering leaders, coaching analysts and engineers, and building the coalitions that make org-wide change stick. Expect roughly an even split between platform building and enablement work.

You will report to the security leadership team and work closely with Platform Engineering, IT, Legal, Privacy, and the broader AI/ML organization.

Responsibilities:

Stand Up the Enterprise AI Infrastructure

- Build the platform. Design and build the shared platform security teams use to develop AI applications — model gateway and routing, authentication and authorization, secrets handling, rate limiting, cost attribution, and audit logging.

- Enable agentic systems. Establish patterns and reusable components for agentic workflows: tool and MCP server integration, sandboxed execution, human-in-the-loop approval gates, and least-privilege scoping for agent credentials.

- Wire in the data. Connect security's knowledge — runbooks, detection logic, past incidents, asset inventory, policy documents — to AI systems through well-governed retrieval pipelines with correct access controls and data classification enforcement.

- Make it measurable. Build the evaluation harness, regression suites, and observability that tell us whether an AI system is working: output quality, latency, cost, hallucination rate, and drift over time. Nothing ships to production without a baseline.

- Secure the stack itself. Implement guardrails against prompt injection, data exfiltration through model outputs, insecure tool use, and supply-chain risk in models and AI dependencies. Red-team the platform and the applications built on it.

- Set the standards. Own the reference architecture, golden paths, and internal documentation so that a security engineer can go from idea to reviewed prototype in days rather than months.

Drive AI Adoption Across the Security Organization

- Find the real use cases. Work directly with detection engineering, IR, threat intel, vulnerability management, GRC, and security operations to identify where AI meaningfully reduces toil or improves quality — and where it does not. Kill weak ideas early.

- Build the flagship applications. Deliver a small number of high-visibility wins yourself. Nothing drives adoption like a working tool that saves an analyst two hours a day.

- Teach the organization. Run enablement programs — office hours, workshops, internal documentation, prompt and agent design patterns, brown-bags — that raise the AI fluency of the entire security organization, not just the engineers.

- Measure adoption honestly. Define and report the metrics that show whether adoption is real: active users, workflows automated, analyst hours returned, time-to-detect and time-to-respond improvements, quality deltas against human baselines.

- Establish governance that enables. Partner with Legal, Privacy, and Compliance to establish the acceptable-use policy, review process, and risk framework for AI in security workflows — designed to unblock teams rather than stall them.

- Stay ahead of the field. Maintain the organization's point of view on where AI capability is heading and what it means for our security roadmap, staffing, and threat model. Evaluate vendors and open models on the merits.

Requirements:

- 8+ years in security engineering, platform engineering, or a closely related technical field, including significant hands-on software development.

- Demonstrated experience building and operating production systems with large language models — not prototypes or demos. You have shipped something real, dealt with its failure modes, and iterated on it.

- Strong software engineering fundamentals and fluency in Python (or an equivalent language), including API design, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

- Deep understanding of security engineering: identity and access management, secrets management, network boundaries, logging and detection, and secure software development practices.

- Working knowledge of AI-specific risk — prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage through model outputs, insecure agent tool use, model and dependency supply chain — and practical mitigations for each.

- A track record of driving technical change across an organization through influence rather than authority: building consensus, teaching, and shipping things people voluntarily adopt.

- Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a system design to an engineer and the business case for it to an executive, in the same week.

- Sound judgment about where AI is genuinely useful and where it is not. We want an advocate who is also a skeptic.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience with agent frameworks, orchestration, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or comparable tool-use standards.

- Experience building evaluation frameworks or LLM observability tooling.

- Background in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response — you have felt the toil firsthand.

- Experience with retrieval systems, embeddings, vector databases, and knowledge pipeline design.

- Familiarity with AI governance and assurance frameworks such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, or the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

- Experience fine-tuning or evaluating open-weight models for domain-specific tasks.

- Prior experience as a first or founding hire on a platform or capability that later scaled organization-wide.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 Days

- You have mapped the current state — what security teams are already doing with AI, sanctioned or not — and published a prioritized assessment of gaps, risks, and opportunities.

- A minimum viable AI platform is running: gateway, authentication, logging, and cost attribution, with at least one security team building on it.

- An acceptable-use policy and lightweight review process for AI in security workflows is drafted and socialized.

First 6 Months

- Two or more production AI applications are in daily use by security teams, with measured impact.

- The evaluation and observability layer is in place; no AI system reaches production without a quality baseline and monitoring.

- Enablement is operating on a regular cadence, and engineers outside your immediate orbit are shipping their own AI-assisted workflows on the golden paths you built.

First Year

- AI is a normal part of how the security organization works, with adoption and impact reported through metrics leadership trusts.

- The platform supports agentic workflows safely, with guardrails that have been tested adversarially.

- The role has clearly outgrown one person, and you have made the case for what the team around it should look like.

Why This Role

Security organizations are drowning in work that AI is genuinely good at, and most of them are still stuck at the pilot stage because nobody owns both halves of the problem — the infrastructure and the adoption. This role owns both. You will have executive sponsorship, real budget, and the latitude to set technical direction from a blank page. If you want to define how an entire security organization works with AI rather than tune someone else's system, this is that job.

title: Sr. Information Security Engineer
description:
Sr. Information Security Engineer

Hybrid/Remote

About Reveleer

Reveleer delivers a unified platform spanning risk adjustment, quality improvement, clinical intelligence, and member management for health plans and provider organizations navigating the complexity of value-based care. Trusted by 80+ customer organizations nationwide, the platform integrates data, analytics, and intelligent workflow automation into one governed system designed to support traceable documentation across diagnoses, quality measures, and submissions. With regulatory expertise and transparent, human-in-the-loop AI at its core, Reveleer supports organizations working to advance care quality, strengthen documentation integrity, and sustain the operational readiness needed to navigate audits with confidence.

Position Summary

- The Senior Information Security Engineer plays a key role in safeguarding Reveleer's cloud-based healthcare SaaS platforms, AI/ML systems, infrastructure, and customer data. This position designs, implements, and manages enterprise-grade security solutions aligned to HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST 800-53, and NIST AI RMF. Because Reveleer's platform relies heavily on AI and large language models to process clinical data, this role carries direct responsibility for securing AI pipelines, models, and the PHI that flows through them. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technologist with depth in cloud security, AI/LLM security, application security, DevSecOps, identity, and security automation.

Cloud and Infrastructure Security

- Design and maintain secure architectures across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with emphasis on infrastructure-as-code security (Terraform, CloudFormation) and policy-as-code enforcement (OPA, Sentinel, AWS SCPs).

- Implement guardrails using AWS Security Hub, GuardDuty, Macie, Inspector, Config, Azure Defender for Cloud, and native IAM controls.

- Operate CSPM/CNAPP tooling (e.g., Wiz, Prisma Cloud, Orca) to detect misconfigurations, toxic combinations, and exposed PHI data stores.

- Secure containerized and serverless workloads across EKS/ECS and Lambda, including image scanning, admission control, runtime protection, and least-privilege task roles.

- Enforce network segmentation, TLS/encryption standards, and centralized key and secrets management (AWS KMS, Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).

AI and Machine Learning Security

- Partner with Data Science and AI Engineering to secure model development, training, fine-tuning, inference, and RAG pipelines that handle PHI and PII.

- Apply the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and MITRE ATLAS to threat model AI features, addressing prompt injection, insecure output handling, training data poisoning, model and data exfiltration, and excessive agency in agentic workflows.

- Implement AI gateway, guardrail, and content-filtering controls (e.g., Bedrock Guardrails, Azure AI Content Safety, LLM firewalls) along with input/output validation, rate limiting, and prompt and completion logging for audit.

- Govern third-party and foundation model usage: vendor security review, data residency and retention terms, zero-retention and no-training contractual controls, and BAA coverage for any AI service touching PHI.

- Establish controls against shadow AI, including discovery of unsanctioned generative AI tools, DLP policies for AI endpoints, and enterprise-approved alternatives.

- Secure the ML supply chain: model and artifact provenance, signed models, dependency scanning for ML libraries, notebook and MLOps platform hardening (SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow).

- Contribute to AI governance alongside Compliance and Legal, mapping controls to NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, HITRUST AI assurance criteria, and emerging state and federal AI regulation.

Application and SaaS Security

- Embed security into CI/CD pipelines with SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets scanning, and IaC scanning (Snyk, StackHawk, Semgrep, etc).

- Perform threat modeling, secure design reviews, and code reviews for microservices, APIs, and AI-enabled features.

- Secure API and machine-to-machine authorization patterns (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, mTLS, scoped service tokens) across internal and partner integrations.

- Manage software supply chain risk through SBOM generation, dependency governance, and artifact signing.

- Drive penetration testing, bug bounty intake, and remediation validation; track findings to closure with Engineering.

- Ensure PHI and PII protection across SaaS platforms through data classification, tokenization, de-identification, and DLP.

Endpoint and Identity Security

- Manage and tune EDR/XDR platforms (Palo Alto Cortex XDR, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint), including detection engineering and response automation.

- Implement identity security through Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access, PIM, and risk-based authentication; advance phishing-resistant MFA and password less adoption.

- Govern non-human identities, service principals, workload identities, and AI agent credentials with least privilege and short-lived tokens.

- Support Intune and MDM compliance baselines for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android; apply CIS Benchmarks and configuration drift monitoring.

- Operate SaaS security posture management (SSPM) for third-party app integrations and OAuth grant risk.

Security Operations and Incident Response

- Monitor and triage alerts, investigate incidents, and coordinate response with the SOC and MDR partners.

- Build and maintain detection content in the SIEM, including detection-as-code, log pipeline coverage, and MITRE ATT&CK mapping.

- Develop incident response runbooks, playbooks, and forensic procedures, including scenarios specific to AI systems such as model misuse, data leakage through prompts, and compromised AI integrations.

- Automate response and enrichment through SOAR workflows, Python, and PowerShell.

- Participate in tabletop exercises, purple team activity, and post-incident reviews.

Governance, Risk, and Compliance

- Support audits and evidence collection for HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, NIST 800-53, and customer security assessments; leverage compliance automation platforms.

- Maintain asset and AI system inventories, risk registers, and remediation tracking with clear SLAs.

- Conduct vendor and third-party risk reviews, with added scrutiny for AI subprocessors and data flows.

- Partner with Compliance to keep technical controls, policies, and standards in alignment.

- Contribute to security awareness and training, including secure and responsible AI use guidance for employees and engineers.

Qualifications

Required:

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or equivalent experience.

- 5+ years of experience in security engineering or related technical security roles.

- Strong knowledge of cloud-native security (AWS, Azure, GCP) and modern SaaS architectures.

- Hands-on experience with SIEM, EDR/XDR, IAM, vulnerability management, and security automation.

- Familiarity with HIPAA, HITRUST, NIST, and SOC 2 requirements.

- Experience securing containerized and serverless workloads (e.g., EKS, Lambda).

Preferred:

- Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, or GIAC (GSEC, GCIA, GCIH).

- Experience with Terraform, Ansible, or CloudFormation for infrastructure-as-code security.

- Experience in DevSecOps pipelines and tools (e.g., Jenkins, Bitbucket).

- Strong scripting skills (Python, PowerShell, or Bash).

Key Competencies

- Analytical and detail-oriented with strong problem-solving skills.

- Ability to balance business needs with risk mitigation.

- Excellent communication skills, able to translate complex technical topics for non-technical stakeholders.

- Collaborative team player with a proactive approach to continuous improvement.

WHAT YOU’LL RECEIVE:

title: Software Engineer - Market Intelligence
description:
Why Patch, why now

Patch exists to put the planet back in balance by scaling unified climate action through software, market infrastructure, and culture-driven execution. Every day our platform not only curates the world's most trusted environmental datasets that includes carbon, renewable energy, sustainable aviation fuel and more, we’re helping companies both set and meet ambitious climate goals that are tied to true impact.

Our culture is built on three non-negotiables:

-
We build the future we want – we don't wait for permission; we shape the market.

-
We're all in this together – direct, empathetic teamwork inside Patch and across the climate ecosystem.

-
We amp it up – urgency and unreasonably high standards because the planet can't wait.

If that mindset energizes you, read on.

About the role

Patch is hiring a software engineer to bring together the disparate data and workflows we have built over time into a reliable market-intelligence foundation. That foundation will help Patch direct capital and action toward the highest-impact climate solutions.

You will ingest and structure messy climate-market data, expose it through internal MCP tools and APIs, and build AI-powered research workflows that help our Climate Strategists, Sales team, and Marketing team understand markets, companies, commitments, suppliers, buyers, and buying signals. The goal is to turn fragmented information and repeated manual research into reliable systems that improve how Patch advises, targets, and acts.

This is a software engineering role. You will build and operate production data systems, internal products, and AI-powered workflows. Climate Strategy, Sales, and Marketing will be your primary users and partners; Engineering will own the architecture, implementation, reliability, and evolution of the system.

This is not a marketing-operations, RevOps, CRM-administration, business-analysis, or content-research role. You will work closely with those functions, but your job is to build the underlying software, data products, and intelligence systems they rely on. You will spend time with users, understand how work happens in practice, and turn recurring needs into durable systems rather than increasingly elaborate point-to-point automations.

What you’ll tackle

-
Build Patch’s market-intelligence foundation: Design and operate systems that ingest, structure, enrich, and serve information about companies, carbon markets, registries, policies, suppliers, buyers, and climate commitments.

-
Ingest and model messy external data: Work with APIs, websites, registries, PDFs, spreadsheets, public disclosures, market sources, and other heterogeneous inputs. Turn fragmented information into reliable, refreshable data products.

-
Make the data trustworthy: Build schemas, entity-resolution workflows, validation checks, provenance, freshness tracking, confidence signals, monitoring, and documentation that make intelligence reliable enough for advisory and commercial use.

-
Build AI-powered research workflows: Develop retrieval systems, MCP tools, agents, and internal applications that help teams discover, compare, enrich, and act on market intelligence.

-
Put intelligence into real workflows: Build APIs, internal tools, lightweight interfaces, reports, and workflow integrations that make the right information available to Climate Strategists, Sales, and Marketing.

-
Move systems from prototype to production: Build software that is observable, testable, maintainable, and useful in real workflows—not just impressive demos.

-
Own projects end to end: Move from an ambiguous user need to a scoped project, design, implementation, rollout, monitoring, and iteration. You will own medium-sized projects independently and contribute to larger architectural decisions with the team.

What makes you a great match

-
You have shipped and maintained production software or data systems. We care more about what you have owned and delivered than a precise number of years of experience.

-
You are a strong software engineer in at least one of Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript, with solid SQL, API, and cloud-infrastructure experience.

-
You have worked with data ingestion, ETL/ELT, web scraping, data modeling, entity resolution, or external API integrations.

-
You understand what makes data trustworthy, including testing, monitoring, versioning, documentation, validation, provenance, and data-quality practices.

-
You have built or operated AI- or LLM-powered systems, ideally involving retrieval, tool calling, agents, workflow orchestration, evaluation, or human-in-the-loop review.

-
You are comfortable moving between backend services, data pipelines, internal tools, and lightweight user interfaces when that is what the problem requires.

-
You can move from an ambiguous user need to a working prototype, then turn the right prototypes into production-grade systems.

-
You have good systems instincts. You think about upstream and downstream dependencies, reusable components, observability, maintainability, and when to build versus buy.

-
You want to work directly with Climate Strategists and commercial users, understand their workflows, and build systems they actually adopt.

-
You are comfortable in a small, high-ownership environment where you will help shape the roadmap rather than execute only a pre-written backlog.

-
Experience with Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Zapier, n8n, BigQuery, dbt, enrichment platforms, climate markets, carbon markets, sustainability data, energy, finance, or research is a plus.

-
You are motivated by the opportunity to be one of the first engineers shaping how Patch captures, structures, and compounds knowledge about climate markets… and to use that intelligence to help direct capital and action toward the highest-impact climate solutions.

What you'll get

-
A mission-obsessed crew building with speed and sky-high standards

-
Competitive salary and meaningful equity

-
Onsite culture in San Francisco with annual global offsites for strategy and team bonding

-
Unlimited vacation and generous parental leave

-
Monthly wellness stipend (mental and physical)

If shaping the story of climate action — while using AI as a force multiplier — sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd love to meet you.

Let's rebalance the planet together.

Front Desk & Office Management

Portfolio Communication

Administrative & Stakeholder Support

title: Strategic Regional Finance Manager
description:
About the Company

At Current, everything starts with people. We believe that when you invest in talent through opportunity, development, and support, you unlock growth for individuals, firms, and clients alike. That’s why we’ve built a platform designed to give our people access to more: more learning, more collaboration, and more ways to grow their careers than any single firm could offer on its own.

Founded in 2023, Current has rapidly become one of the fastest-growing accounting platforms in the country, partnering with more than 40 leading accounting firms across the United States. Today, our community includes over 2,000 professionals, 30+ offices nationwide, and a growing global workforce that supports clients around the world. Backed by Thrive Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Springdale Industries, Current is investing heavily in technology, artificial intelligence, and workforce innovation to help modernize the profession. Our leadership team has a proven track record of building and scaling successful businesses, with prior ventures generating more than $3 billion in combined enterprise value.

We’re building something bigger than a traditional accounting firm: a platform where talented people can grow faster, learn more, and do more meaningful work. Whether you join Current, one of our partner firms, or our global team, you’ll be part of a community shaping the future of the profession.

About The Role

Current is seeking a hands-on, highly strategic Regional Finance Manager to serve as the embedded financial partner to regional leadership. You will function as a trusted advisor who understands the region’s operating environment at every level, from firm-wide business performance down to office-level detail, and who can distill that complexity into insight leadership can act on.

This role reports directly to the Director, Corporate FP&A at Current, while carrying direct, hands-on ownership and accountability for financial planning, reporting, analysis and related support for the Central region.

The ideal candidate brings deep FP&A experience in multi-entity or PE-backed environments and thrives in ambiguity. They are proactive, hands-on, and equally comfortable shaping a strategic recommendation for leadership or digging into the underlying data to understand what is driving performance. Success requires strong executive presence, sharp problem-solving instincts, and the ability to turn complex financial and operational issues into clear, actionable insights, then stay engaged through execution.

This role requires candidates to be based in the Central or West region. Proximity to the region’s firms gives this person the ability to be genuinely hands-on visiting offices regularly, building in-person relationships with firm leaders, and staying close to the office-level detail that drives the analysis. Just as important, this is a team player who integrates naturally with the regional leadership team: someone who earns trust through consistent presence and collaboration, not just the quality of the analysis delivered from a distance.

Key Responsibilities

Business Performance Reporting for the Region (35%)

-
Build deep fluency in the region’s operating environment across every level, from consolidated business performance to individual office economics, so recommendations are grounded in operating reality, not just the numbers

-
Own the region’s financial performance narrative delivering monthly and quarterly reporting packages that surface the “so what,” not just the variance

-
Define, track, and continuously refine the KPI framework across revenue, margins, utilization, realization, and client profitability

-
Understand variances to plan and prior year results. Build early warning systems and leading indicators that give leadership a forward-looking view before issues become trends

-
Go beyond variance commentary and standard reporting to investigate the underlying drivers behind performance digging into the data to understand root cause, not just outcome

-
Translate complex, sometimes messy financial and operational data into a clear, insightful narrative that leadership can act on quickly

-
Drive the annual budget, multi-year long-range plan, and rolling quarterly forecasts for the region, with full ownership from build to presentation.

Regional Financial Leadership & Support (35%)

-
Serve as the primary, embedded financial partner to regional leadership providing hands-on, proactive support across growth initiatives, operational performance, and day-to-day decision-making

-
Own follow-through on recommendations: track the actions that come out of an analysis and ensure they’re driven to completion, not just handed off

-
Act as a trusted sounding board to regional leadership, bringing an independent, well-reasoned point of view to strategic and operational questions

-
Perform ad hoc analysis as directed by the Regional leadership team to support both strategic and operational decisions to drive business performance

-
Develop and stress-test scenario models to evaluate strategic alternatives, growth investments, M&A targets, and market expansion opportunities

-
Shape investment decisions, resource allocation, and operational strategy through rigorous analysis and confident, well-supported recommendations

Business Partnering (15%)

-
Act as a trusted, embedded partner to firm and regional leaders, translating operational realities into financial projections and bridging strategy and execution

-
Support financial diligence, integration modeling, special projects, ad hoc analysis and synergy tracking for regional acquisitions, onboarding activity, and broader growth strategies

-
Collaborate cross-functionally and with other regional teams to ensure financial planning stays grounded in operational reality

-
Systems, Automation & Process Excellence (15%)

-
Continuously improve regional FP&A infrastructure forecasting cadence, reporting templates, data pipelines, and BI dashboards to enable faster, more scalable insight

-
Champion self-service analytics by building automation and performance dashboards that give firm and regional leaders real-time visibility into financial performance

-
Partner with Corporate FP&A and Finance Systems teams to drive consistency in planning tools, data definitions, and reporting standards across the platform

Qualifications

Education & Experience

-
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required; MBA or CPA strongly preferred

-
6+ years of progressive FP&A or corporate finance experience, including meaningful time operating in a hands-on, business-partnering capacity rather than a purely analytical one

-
Background in professional services, PE-backed platforms, or multi-entity / multi-location businesses required

Technical Skills

-
Expert-level financial modeling; able to build dynamic, audit-ready models from scratch

-
Hands-on experience with ERP and planning systems (NetSuite, Workday Adaptive, SAP, Anaplan, or equivalent) and BI tools (Power BI, Tableau or Databricks)

-
Strong command of GAAP, financial statement drivers, and the operational metrics that matter in services businesses

People Skills

-
Executive presence and the communication skill to translate complex financial and operational issues into a clear, cohesive story equally effective in a leadership meeting and a one-on-one working session

-
A problem-solver by instinct: comfortable digging into ambiguous or messy situations to find the root cause rather than stopping at the surface-level number

-
Proven ability to influence without authority and build credibility with senior stakeholders through the quality of your insight and your follow-through, not positional authority

-
Highly organized, with the discipline to manage a wide range of competing priorities and deliver consistently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

-
A genuine team player who integrates naturally with the regional leadership team — collaborative, low-ego, and as invested in the team’s success as in individual output

Travel & Work Environment

This role is member firm-facing and requires travel. Candidates should expect to travel approximately 30–40% of the time, including regular visits to member firms across the region to support business partnering, onboarding, and M&A integration activity. Candidates must be comfortable with a travel schedule that varies by quarter based on business needs.

Compensation & Benefits

The total rewards package at Current includes base salary and benefits.

Our salary ranges are competitive within the accounting industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.

We provide a robust benefits package, including:

-
Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance (with options for fully paid employee only coverage for health and dental)

-
Company-Paid Life and Long-Term & Short-Term Disability Insurance

-
Ancillary Benefits such as supplemental life insurance, critical illness, and accident insurance

-
Classic Safe Harbor 401(k) Plan with employer contributions

-
Opportunities for professional growth, learning, and development including access to Becker and LinkedIn Learning

Equal Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other applicable legally protected characteristic.

title: Business Process & Change Management Analyst
description:

This mid-level position (Journeyman Business and Financial Operations Specialist) leads change and release management for the Cost Management Module (CMM) on the FileOnQ platform, maintains the Customer Service Program SharePoint site and document repository, and develops the SOPs, desk guides, and training materials that keep CS-OPS processes consistent and auditable. The analyst reports to the Customer Service Program Lead and the Dynamis Program Manager.

Responsibilities:

- Manage CMM change and release management with ICE OCIO, including planned change requests, emergency System Change Requests (SCRs), and the CMM release schedule (PWS 4.4)

- Gather and analyze requirements, develop use cases for system changes, and prepare all documentation required for OCIO change management

- Support the annual Customer Billing Model (CBM) configuration review in CMM: coordinate with OFM process owners to confirm workload drivers and data capture, and maintain the Configuration Activity Log in JIRA (PWS 4.2)

- Design, configure, and maintain the Customer Service SharePoint site and the CS-OPS document repository, including access requests to CBM tools, audit trails, and coordination with OCIO (PWS C.1.5)

- Develop and maintain SOPs, process desk guides, tip sheets, the Document Management Plan, and the Records Retention Plan in accordance with NARA requirements

- Develop training plans and materials and deliver virtual training to CSP and OFM users on CBM tools and systems (PWS 4.3)

- Document business processes and workflows, and support process improvement and special projects (PWS 4.1)

- 3–6 years of relevant professional experience, including Federal-sector change management and release management (change requests, release planning, and SDLC documentation)

- Experience gathering and analyzing requirements and developing use cases for system changes

- Technical writing experience: user guides, technical requirements, SOPs, and business process and workflow documentation

- Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Project, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, and SharePoint; working knowledge of JIRA

- Excellent oral and written communication skills

- U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain an ICE suitability (public trust) determination, with U.S. residency for 3 of the last 5 years

Preferred:

- Master's degree in data analytics, finance, or public policy

- ITIL Foundation certification or equivalent change and release management training

- Experience supporting ICE, DHS, or another federal CFO organization, including familiarity with activity-based costing or shared services (FASS) billing

- Experience with FileOnQ/CMM or similar cost management or billing platforms

- SharePoint site administration and configuration experience; Power BI or Tableau

- Experience with SQL, financial reporting, or audit support

- Experience with federal records management (NARA) and document control

Salary range: $105,000-120,000

title: Director of Digital Product Operations
description:
About Ruggable:

Ruggable is a leading direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand based in Los Angeles, California with an extraordinary track record of high, profitable growth. We pride ourselves on having an extremely loyal customer base and a talented team made up of genuinely caring people who take action and deliver results. We are venture-backed and own a patented washable rug design that's disrupting the home décor industry. Our mission is to empower our customers to live vibrantly with beautiful products that don't compromise on function. If you're passionate about consumer products, e-commerce, and high-growth start-ups, keep reading!

Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly organized, detail-obsessed, and technically versatile Director of Digital Product Operations to anchor the technology roadmap, ecosystem architecture, process rigor, and execution cadence across our global digital storefronts. Reporting directly into the VP of eCommerce, you will serve as the master process owner for the ruggable.com shopping experience, its interconnected tooling, and the operational infrastructure supporting our global digital business.

Success in this role means establishing bulletproof digital product operations: bridging the gap between commercial strategy, merchandising, UX/UI design, marketing, and engineering delivery. You will manage a Technical Product Manager and divide-and-conquer sprint planning, while taking full accountability for our Shopify storefront ecosystem, including headless CMS workflows, merchandising platforms, and operational integrations. You are an exceptional cross-functional thought partner who thrives on bringing stakeholders along, setting explicit delivery milestones, and replacing fragmented processes with highly structured, predictable operations.

What You’ll Do:

Technical Delivery, Agile Execution & Engineering Alignment

- Strategic Intake & Prioritization Partnership: Serve as a key strategic advisor to the VP of eCommerce and Director of Development to establish and govern a centralized intake framework. Co-lead the prioritization of initiatives across commercial, marketing, UX/UI, and operational stakeholders—advising leadership on high-leverage trade-offs between business growth, SaaS enhancements, and technical debt against engineering capacity.

- Engineering Partnership: Partner daily with the Director of Storefront Engineering and dev pods to balance technical debt, sprint capacity, release cycles, and platform health against commercial feature delivery.

- Roadmap & Sprint Governance: Divide and conquer core agile ceremonies with your reporting Technical Product Manager. Author technical PRDs, drive experimentation frameworks, and lead sprint planning, kickoffs and reviews.

- Delivery Accountability: Project manages complex, cross-functional storefront initiatives by providing explicit timelines, milestones, dependencies, and delivery dates to executive leadership.

- Team Leadership & Mentorship: Manage, mentor, and provide operational guardrails for the Technical Product Management function, leveling up the team's ability to manage larger projects and integrations outside of standard sprint-to-sprint ticket writing.

Merchandising, UX/UI Design & Site Experience Alignment

- Design & UX Integration: Collaborate intimately with Experience Design (UX/UI) to translate user research, wireframes, and design concepts into technically feasible, performance-optimized site features.

- Merchandising Engine: Serve as the technical engine behind Digital Merchandising strategies—optimizing product discovery via Constructor, dynamic facet governance, PLP architecture, and complex promotional/bundling logic (Covers, Standard Pads, Cushioned Pads).

Content, Launch & Multi-Storefront Operations

- Content Strategy Support: Empower the Digital Content Strategy team with flexible Contentful (CMS) schemas and modular landing page components, enabling high-velocity publishing without developer bottlenecks.

- Product Drops & Launch Workflows: Establish smooth, error-free operational workflows for high-volume product launches, licensed collaboration drops, and promotional campaigns across PIM (Akeneo), CMS, and storefront channels.

- Global Localization & Inventory Sync: Own the operational reliability of multi-locale storefronts (US, CA, UK, FR, DE, AU), ensuring localized pricing, currency routing, international tax logic, and real-time inventory sync integrity between Shopify and back-office/ERP systems.

MarTech, Growth Marketing & Data Analytics Governance

- Retention & Growth Alignment: Partner with Retention and Growth Marketing to support lifecycle initiatives, ensuring airtight integrations with Klaviyo, Postscript, Yotpo, and affiliate tracking.

- Pixel & Script Governance: Act as the strict gatekeeper for marketing pixel and tracking script implementations (Meta, TikTok, Google via GTM/server-side tracking), balancing attribution needs with front-end site performance and data privacy rules (GDPR/CCPA).

- Analytics Instrumentation: Collaborate with the Reporting & Insights team to maintain event tracking taxonomies in Amplitude and data pipeline integrity in Sigma BI for accurate downstream attribution.

Site Health, CX Operations & Incident Triage

- Consumer Care Integration: Partner with Consumer Care (CX) leadership to manage integrations across Zendesk and Loop Returns, actively prioritizing post-checkout bug fixes and friction points in the customer journey.

- Performance Budgets & Uptime SLAs: Enforce strict site speed, Core Web Vitals, and checkout uptime guardrails, preventing code bloat or performance regression when deploying marketing scripts or running A/B tests.

- Incident Management & RCAs: Oversee severity incident triage (P1/P2 production bugs and site outages), managing the end-to-end lifecycle from initial cross-functional escalation through engineering triage, validation, deployment, and post-mortem Root Cause Analysis (RCA).

- Technical SEO Safeguards: Enforce technical SEO protocols (canonicalization rules, parameter handling, clean URL routing, and schema structure) to prevent dynamic filter combinations in Constructor from diluting domain authority or creating crawl budget issues.

Digital Product Ops, SaaS & Budget Ownership

- Tooling Stack Ownership: Take full control of the Shopify application ecosystem and interconnected platforms, acting as the primary owner for Contentful (headless CMS), Klaviyo, Postscript, Loop (returns), Zendesk, Constructor (search/merchandising), Akeneo (PIM), Amplitude (eventing), and Sigma (BI).

- Vendor & Budget Management: Direct accountability for managing the SaaS technology budget, contract renewals, seat licensing audits, vendor SLAs, and cost optimization across all 3rd-party vendors and microservices.

- The "Master Process Owner": Overhaul, rebuild, and maintain a highly organized, centralized documentation library in Confluence, replacing fragmented or abandoned resources with a single source of truth for the eCommerce and storefront teams.

- Product Ops & QA Protocols: Establish and enforce rigorous Business Analysis (BA) and Quality Assurance (QA) protocols. Drive meticulous Jira hygiene, bug triage workflows, and communications.

Role Success Metrics (KPIs)

- Sprint Predictability & Velocity: Consistent high-percentile delivery against planned sprint commitments and project milestones.

- Bug Resolution & Triage MTTR: Reduction in Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) for storefront bugs and cross-functional P1/P2 escalations.

- Site Health & Web Vitals: Maintaining target Core Web Vitals scores and zero P1 incidents during critical commercial events.

- Documentation Coverage: Total overhaul, adoption, and active maintenance of the Confluence product and operations library.

What You’ll Need to Have:

Required

- Experience: 10+ years of experience spanning digital product operations, technical product management, or business systems analysis in a high-growth DTC e-commerce, digital retail, or CPG environment.

- Shopify & Ecosystem Expertise: Deep architectural command of the Shopify platform, API integrations, and hands-on experience managing 3rd-party microservices (e.g., Contentful, Akeneo, Constructor, Loop).

- Process & Documentation Mastery: "Type-A" obsession with efficiency, process mapping, and documentation. Power-user proficiency in standardizing project workflows, PRDs, and engineering ticket lifecycles in Jira and Confluence.

- Project Management Rigor: Proven ability to act as a rigorous project manager—translating complex business roadmaps into clear milestones, delivery dates, and cross-functional accountability.

- DTC Campaign & Launch Operations: Proven track record of managing technical launch readiness for high-traffic product drops, peak shopping periods (BFCM), and complex promotional logic.

- People Leadership: Experience managing, mentoring, and scaling technical PMs, analysts, or digital operations coordinators.

- Communication & Presence: Exceptional thought partnership and communication skills. Ability to over-communicate, bring stakeholders along, and translate technical tradeoffs into business impacts.

Preferred

- Process Methodologies: Background or certifications in formal process optimization, business process modeling, or project management (e.g., Lean Six Sigma, BPMN, PRINCE2, PMP).

- Data & Analytics Depth: Hands-on capability using product analytics platforms (Amplitude) and BI tools (Sigma) to validate implementations and interrogate event-level data.

- Experimentation & CRO: Strong familiarity with conversion rate optimization (CRO) principles, A/B testing frameworks, and managing client/server-side script performance impacts.

Compensation:

- $170,000 - $185,000 per year base salary

- An annual bonus percentage that varies based on level of role

- Employer matching (up to 3% of base salary) for company sponsored 401K plan

description:

title: Quantitative Research Intern
description:
About EG:
Engineers Gate (EG) is a leading investment manager founded in 2014 as a quantitative, computer-driven trading firm. Today, EG operates as a diversified, multi-strategy investment platform that combines systematic research with selective discretionary approaches.

EG's multi-manager platform allows independent investment teams to pursue distinct strategies while benefiting from shared infrastructure, risk management, and operational support. The firm’s collaborative groups of researchers, engineers, and investment professionals deploy sophisticated statistical models, proprietary technology, and a centralized data platform to isolate and solve challenging problem sets in the global financial markets.

About The Role:

We are seeking a Quantitative Research Intern to join a three-person, fully systematic investment team focused on intraday US equities trading. You will work directly with the portfolio managers and take ownership of a research project from initial data exploration through model development and evaluation, with regular feedback along the way. We are looking for someone who can work independently, develop original hypotheses, and turn a time series dataset into a rigorously tested predictive model. The work involves understanding the data, choosing appropriate methods, and critically assessing whether results are robust and relevant to trading.

Key Responsibilities:

- Clean, validate, and analyze financial time series datasets, including high-frequency data, to establish a reliable foundation for research.

- Develop your own research hypotheses and build statistical or machine learning models to identify predictive signals for systematic trading.

- Design and run backtests that evaluate performance, robustness, and practical relevance, with careful attention to overfitting and data leakage.

- Refine models based on experimental results and feedback from portfolio managers.

- Communicate findings, assumptions, limitations, and proposed next steps clearly.

- Contribute original modeling ideas and explore promising research directions with the team.

Qualifications:

- Currently pursuing a Master’s, or Ph.D. in a quantitative field such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Physics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, or a related discipline.

- Prior finance experience through an internship or full-time role, ideally in quantitative research.

- Academic research experience involving quantitative methods, such as a thesis, research assistantship, or substantial research project.

- Strong programming skills in Python.

- A solid foundation in probability, statistics, and time series analysis, with experience applying statistical modeling or machine learning to data.

- Ability to work independently and carry an open-ended research problem from initial exploration through model evaluation.

- Clear written and verbal communication

Preferred Qualifications:

- Demonstrated interest in quantitative finance beyond coursework or employment, such as independent research, personal modeling projects, competitions, open-source contributions, or relevant student activities

- Independently developed models or research ideas you would like to explore with the team

The annualized base salary for this role is anticipated to be $100,000–130,000, prorated for the duration of the internship, excluding potential bonuses, additional compensation, and benefits. Actual compensation will depend on various factors including skills, experience, and qualifications.

title: FP&A Associate
description:
About the Company

The OpenAI Deployment Company (“DeployCo”) is the deployment arm of OpenAI, purpose-built to deliver enterprise AI transformation at scale. As model capabilities accelerate, deployment has become the primary constraint to realizing AI value creation within large enterprises. DeployCo bridges that gap.

Our ambition is to build the company that defines AI deployment. We operate at the intersection of cutting-edge AI, enterprise transformation, and scaled services delivery. We work with many of the world's largest and most influential companies to solve their most complex business challenges using the latest advances in AI.

People who thrive at DeployCo get excited about ambitious and complex work. We are deep believers in the future with AI. We execute quickly, value intellectual honesty, and obsess over the solutions we build for our customers.

DeployCo is being built from the ground up as a subsidiary of OpenAI and funded with a partnership of outside investors.

About the Role

We are seeking a Member of the Finance Staff to help build DeployCo’s FP&A capabilities as the business scales. Reporting to the FP&A lead, this individual contributor will bring rigorous financial modeling, commercial judgment, and hands-on analytical execution to a growing finance team.

Your core responsibilities will be maintaining the rolling forecast and producing weekly pipeline reporting, translating changes in commercial activity, delivery capacity, and hiring into a clear view of financial performance and priorities. You will also support budgeting, management and board reporting, pricing and deal profitability analyses, strategic projects, and M&A evaluation and integration.

You will help design and build AI-enabled systems and workflows that improve the quality, speed, and repeatability of finance work. Working with Finance, Revenue Operations, GTM, Delivery, and People teams, you will turn incomplete information into well-supported assumptions, reliable models, and clear recommendations.

This role is based in New York City.

In this role, you will:

-
Maintain integrated rolling forecasts for the P&L, balance sheet, and free cash flow, linking commercial and operating assumptions to financial performance.

-
Forecast demand and capacity for deployment professionals by role, skill set, and geography to guide hiring, staffing, and utilization decisions.

-
Produce weekly pipeline reporting with Revenue Operations and GTM teams, reconciling changes in value, stage, probability, and timing to assess forecast implications and capacity planning.

-
Support budgeting, long-range planning, and headcount and expense planning, explaining variances against plan and forecast and highlighting risks and opportunities.

-
Build financial models, scenarios, and sensitivities to evaluate growth, unit economics, and investment decisions and inform management, board, and investor reporting.

-
Support pricing and deal desk decisions through customer and project profitability analyses that assess delivery costs, commercial terms, cash implications, and economic tradeoffs.

-
Support M&A evaluation, financial diligence, and integration planning, assessing business plans and synergies and tracking integration costs and performance through forecasting and reporting.

-
Help design and build AI-enabled forecasting, reporting, and analytical workflows that reduce manual work and improve insights, with checks on inputs, calculations, and outputs.

-
Partner across Finance, GTM, Delivery, People, and Data to reconcile inputs, challenge assumptions, and deliver reliable recurring analyses and clear recommendations on ad hoc questions.

You may thrive in this role if you:

-
Have 3–5 years of total experience and substantial modeling expertise, preferably from an investment banking or private equity environment. Rigorous corporate FP&A and finance rotational backgrounds are also welcome.

-
Have advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills and build auditable models from first principles, linking operating drivers to financial statements and testing scenarios and sensitivities.

-
Bring strong financial judgment across unit economics, pricing, profitability, valuation, and investment returns.

-
Have demonstrated hands-on experience using AI tools for substantive financial analysis, with the judgment to verify data, calculations, and conclusions and develop repeatable workflows.

-
Can structure ambiguous questions, reconcile incomplete data, document assumptions, and investigate discrepancies before drawing conclusions.

-
Thrive in an ambiguous environment - Own recurring deliverables with accuracy and timeliness while balancing ad hoc requests.

-
Communicate clear recommendations and tradeoffs through writing, presentations, and effective collaboration with colleagues outside finance.

-
Ideally bring operating experience in budgeting, forecasting, or data analytics and translating financial plans into business decisions.

-
Experience with SQL or Python is a plus but not required.

title: AVP, Revenue Operations
description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As the AVP, Revenue Operations, you will be tasked with building and leading the global operating model for Channel and Partner Operations, Sales Compensation, Renewals Operations, and Quote-to-Cash, turning a complex, multi-motion go-to-market into a scalable, well-governed operation that keeps pace with our growth. Leading a team of regional and operational leaders, you will set the operating cadence, planning, and executive reporting that give Sales, Finance, and the Board a consistent view of the business. You will also shape how we scale through what comes next, from integrating acquisitions and launching new pricing to applying AI and automation across revenue workflows.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

- Operating cadence and planning: own global forecasting, QBRs, and performance metrics across segments and regions, and lead annual planning for priorities, initiative roadmaps, territory design, and headcount allocation.

- Operating model and team: set the strategy, governance, and performance framework for Channel and Partner Operations, Sales Compensation, Renewals Operations, and quote-to-cash globally, and lead a team of Directors who act as strategic partners to the business, with an org design that scales alongside GTM growth.

- Channel, Partner, and MSSP Operations: scale Deal Registration, Partner SPIFF payments, Partner Activation, co-sell tracking, sourced versus influenced analytics, and the Partner Portal, with automated, standardized processes that support our MSSP program and consumption motions.

- Sales Compensation: drive the annual incentive design cycle (spend analysis, plan design, scenario modeling, communication, and enablement), own all GTM SPIFFs and special incentive programs, and serve as the executive point of contact for Sales leadership on compensation.

- Quote-to-cash and Order Operations: own the quote, order, and booking process end to end, including quoting standards, approval workflows, deal desk escalation, and quarter-end order accuracy, and govern non-standard commercial terms with Finance and Legal.

- Renewals: partner with Global Renewals Sales to scale operations and improve GRR and NRR through aligned process, data, and inspection.

- Executive reporting: own executive and Board reporting for your functions, with consistent metric definitions and narrative quarter over quarter.

- AI and automation: prioritize and manage a portfolio of use cases across these functions, with guardrails set alongside Legal, Security, and Data, and measured adoption and impact.

- M&A integration: lead the operational and systems integration of acquisitions, consolidating partner programs, compensation structures, renewal motions, quoting, and reporting on a clear timeline.

- Readiness and change management: prepare systems, partners, and the Field for product launches, pricing and packaging changes, program redesigns, and international expansion, with the enablement needed to make new processes stick.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

- 12+ years supporting Sales in an operations capacity, with broad experience across Channel and Partner Operations, Renewals Operations, Sales Compensation, and quote-to-cash.

- 5+ years leading leaders, managing Directors and Managers across multiple functions and geographies, with a track record of building and developing teams.

- High-tech industry experience is required, including Global Enterprise, SMB, and MSSP go-to-market motions through indirect Partner pathways, and SaaS subscription, MSSP billing, and consumption business models.

- Working knowledge of quote-to-cash mechanics, including CPQ, approval and discounting governance, order management, and handoffs into billing and revenue recognition.

- Proven ability to build an operating model and cadence, not just run existing processes, and to translate strategy into measurable business outcomes.

- Experience owning or governing a revenue data model and metric definitions, with systems and reporting held to an executive standard of accuracy.

- Practical experience applying AI and automation to revenue operations workflows, with the judgment to separate real leverage from novelty.

- Experience leading M&A integration or other large-scale transformation, such as systems migrations, program consolidation, or post-acquisition GTM alignment.

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Management, Technology, or Economics; MBA a plus.

- Proficiency with Google Workspace, Salesforce, CPQ, Partner Portal applications, Clari, and Excel modeling; experience with NetSuite, incentive compensation platforms, and analytics tools such as Tableau a plus.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

Work Perks & Flexibility

title: Senior Vice President of Engineering
description:
At Koalafi, we believe in a world where no one has to put an important purchase on hold. That’s why we’re making it easier for more people to pay for big purchases over time.

Retailers across the country rely on us to offer flexible lease-to-own financing to their non-prime consumers, while increasing sales and strengthening customer loyalty. Their 2M+ customers love us because we provide a flexible way for them to make payments and give them an opportunity to improve their credit. Our 200+ Koalafi teammates enjoy inspiring and challenging work that accelerates their careers.

Interested in learning more about how we’re transforming the financing experience and joining our team?

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Senior Vice President of Engineering to lead Koalafi’s entire engineering organization, including our Consumer and Merchant Experience, Core Engineering, and Application Experience groups, as well as our Data & AI Platform and Architecture functions.

Reporting to the Chief Product and Technology Officer, you will partner closely with the CPTO and Head of Product to set engineering direction, translate company priorities into execution, and build an organization that delivers meaningful business results. Your scope spans the platforms, applications, services, and data infrastructure that power our customer experiences, merchant relationships, and internal operations.

This is a company leadership role, not solely an engineering leadership role. You will help shape business decisions, influence across functions, and bring a clear perspective on how technology can support growth, improve efficiency, and strengthen the customer experience. You must be equally credible in a technical discussion with engineers and a strategic discussion with the executive team or the board—and move comfortably between those two modes.

We’re also looking for an active AI practitioner who will help evolve how Koalafi works. You should be building and experimenting with AI tools yourself, with a thoughtful perspective on how to apply them across engineering and the broader business. The goal is not simply to increase adoption of tools or token usage, but to drive real, measurable business outcomes by embracing a willingness to fundamentally change how the business operates. You will lead this transformation through practical application, sound judgment, and measurable results.

What You’ll Do

Set engineering direction and own execution

Partner with the CPTO, Head of Product, and cross-functional leaders to translate company objectives into a clear engineering strategy, investment priorities, and execution plans. Ensure teams understand the outcomes they are accountable for, make realistic commitments, and surface risks and tradeoffs early. Own the engineering response when delivery is at risk, aligning leaders on corrective action and following through.

Lead as a business executive

Build strong partnerships across Product, Risk, Operations, Finance, Sales, and other functions. Contribute to company decisions beyond engineering, connecting technical choices to growth, customer experience, operating efficiency, and risk. Communicate complex topics clearly and bring well-vetted recommendations – not simply issues or requests – to executive discussions.

Apply technical depth with sound leadership judgment

Earn the team’s trust through technical expertise, thoughtful questions, and the ability to engage deeply in consequential architectural and engineering decisions. Recognize when an initiative, technical risk, or team challenge needs your direct involvement, and engage early enough to make a difference. Balance that involvement with clear delegation, strengthening your leaders’ ownership rather than becoming a bottleneck or doing their jobs for them.

Build and develop a strong leadership team

Lead, coach, and hold accountable engineering leaders and managers across the organization. Set clear expectations for their technical judgment, business understanding, people leadership, and execution. Invest in succession planning, leadership development, and hiring, while addressing performance gaps directly. Continually evaluate team structure, responsibilities, and leadership capacity so the organization can operate effectively as priorities evolve.

Own architecture, data foundations, and pragmatic modernization

Guide the evolution of our applications, core services, and data platforms, balancing near-term delivery with long-term maintainability, reliability, and scale. Modernize the tech stack where it creates clear business value and be able to defend the ROI. Partner with Risk, Analytics, and Data Science to ensure our data engineering and AI foundations support reliable access, clear ownership, and effective use of data across the company.

Drive engineering excellence and responsible investment

Strengthen quality, test automation, delivery practices, observability, and operational readiness. Establish useful measures of delivery effectiveness, reliability, cost, and business impact, and use them to guide improvement. Own engineering budget and capacity planning in partnership with the CPTO and Finance, challenging staffing and technology proposals against business needs and credible alternatives. Partner closely with IT and Information Security to build and operate secure, resilient systems.

Lead AI adoption through hands-on practice

Maintain an active practice of building, prototyping, and experimenting with AI tools yourself. Use that experience to help teams improve how they design, build, test, deploy, and operate software—not just how they write code. Stay current with emerging capabilities, distinguish useful advances from hype, and turn promising experiments into repeatable practices with measurable improvements in speed, quality, or capacity, with the ultimate goal being to drive better business outcomes for the company.

Help the broader company work more effectively through AI

Partner with business leaders to identify where generative AI, automation, and better internal tools can improve workflows and outcomes. Help teams move from ideas and pilots to solutions people actually use. Ensure adoption is supported by appropriate data access, technical foundations, training, and safeguards, in partnership with Information Security, Risk, and Legal and Compliance.

About You

-

An experienced engineering executive. You bring 15+ years of progressive engineering experience, including substantial experience leading managers and senior engineering leaders across multiple teams. You have owned organization-wide strategy, delivery, talent, and investment decisions, not just an individual product or technical function.

-

Technically credible and comfortable going deep. You have strong architectural judgment across complex applications, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and data platforms. You can challenge assumptions, assess tradeoffs, and help teams work through difficult technical decisions without needing to be the expert in every technology.

-

Business-minded and influential across functions. You understand how engineering decisions affect revenue, cost, customer experience, and risk. You can earn the confidence of executive peers, navigate competing priorities, and build alignment without relying on reporting lines or authority.

-

A leader with strong situational judgment. You know when to delegate, when to coach, when to challenge, and when to get directly involved. You maintain enough visibility to recognize emerging problems and take ownership before they become escalations, without micromanaging your team.

-

A committed developer of leaders. You have a track record of building inclusive, high-performing organizations and helping managers become stronger leaders. You set a high bar, provide candid feedback, address difficult people decisions, and create clear accountability.

-

An active AI practitioner. You can point to things you have personally built, workflows you have redesigned, or experiments you have run using AI tools. You have informed views on their capabilities and limitations, and experience helping others apply them effectively. Your interest extends beyond coding productivity to how AI can improve the way an entire company operates.

-

Pragmatic and accountable for outcomes. You can balance modernization with delivery, speed with reliability, and ambition with available capacity. You communicate clearly, make decisions with imperfect information, and follow through on commitments.

Preferred Qualifications

-

Experience in fintech, payments, lending, or other regulated, transaction-intensive environments is a plus, as is experience with customer- and merchant-facing products, servicing platforms, and internal business systems such as Salesforce.

-

Familiarity with technologies in our environment—including Go, Node.js, React, AWS, Kubernetes, and native iOS and Android development—is helpful. We value strong engineering fundamentals and architectural judgment over expertise in any single stack.

-

Fluency in the modern AI stack and in how it is changing the way software is built. That includes frontier models, coding agents, and the harnesses, evaluations, and guardrails that make them reliable in production. You should understand how the developer workflow is shifting from writing code to designing and supervising agentic loops, where agents plan, build, test, and verify work against clear specifications. We standardize on Claude, but regularly evaluate new frontier models and tools, and knowing which advances actually matter, is a core part of the job.

-

Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Location: Richmond, VA; Arlington, VA; or Remote (U.S.). Associates near one of our office locations may work in-office, hybrid, or remotely. Remote opportunities are available to candidates throughout the United States.

The final salary offer will depend on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and geographic location. The actual annualized salary amount offered to any candidate at the time of hire will be reflected solely in the candidate’s offer letter.

Applications will be accepted until position is filled.

Why choose Koalafi: A career at Koalafi means opportunities to tackle exciting challenges every single day. We take pride in a culture of innovation, trust, and ownership. You'll get outside your comfort zone, build meaningful relationships, and most of all, take charge of projects that ultimately help people get the things they need most.

Benefits:

At Koalafi, you will have a direct impact on our products and help shape the company’s success. We offer competitive compensation & benefits packages to keep you at your best:

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

- 20 PTO days + 11 paid holidays

- 401(k) retirement with company matching

- Student Loan & Tuition Reimbursement

- Commuter assistance

- Parental leave (maternal + paternal)

- Inclusion and Associate Engagement Programs

Who we are & what we value:

- We focus on what’s most important

- We set clear expectations and deliver

- We embrace challenges to reach our full potential

- We ask, “How can this be better?”

- We move fast together
